Preface 

A significant forward step in the legislation of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico was made with the passage of the Rules and Regulations Act of 1958, Act June 30, 1957, No. 112, 3 L.P.R.A. §§ 1041 to 1059. 

Laws of Puerto Rico Annotated made available to the citizens of the Commonwealth the laws enacted by the Legislative Branch and the interpretation of those laws by the Judicial 

Branch. The Rules and Regulations Act performs the same service with respect to the regulations adopted by the Executive Branch for the execution of the laws. 

The regulatory system set up by this Act has two principal features: (1) All regulations which are within the scope of the Act must be filed in the office of the Secretary of State. Beginning three months after June 30, 1957, any such regulation which is not filed with the Secretary of State is void and ineffective. 

This provides an official record of the regulations. (2) For the information and guidance of the people, these regulations will be published by the Secretary of State. This publication will be in two stages: (a) The "Rules and Regulations of Puerto Rico", for which the citation "R.&R.P.R." has been adopted, will be a codification of all regulations originally filed. (b) The "Puerto Rico Register" will be published periodically and will contain new regulations and amendments to existing regulations, thus keeping R.&R.P.R. up to date. After publication of the Register begins, new regulations will not become effective until published therein, except in cases of emergency. 

Rules and Regulations of Puerto Rico. The regulations originally filed with the Secretary of State have been classified by subject matter. A system of arrangement and numbering has been adopted which greatly simplifies the search for the corresponding provisions of the laws and regulations. For this purpose, R.&R.P.R. will have the same title and chapter numbers as Laws of Puerto 

Rico Annotated (L.P.R.A.). Regulations interpreting and applying a law contained in a title and chapter of L.P.R.A. will be found in the same title and chapter of R.&R.P.R. In addition, the 

VII

section numbers of a regulation in R.&R.P.R. will correspond with the section number of L.P.R.A. which authorizes the adoption of that regulation. For example, regulations adopted under 

6 L.P.R.A. § 3 will be found in 6 R.&R.P.R. §§ 3-1 to 3-24, 

With this system a person reading a provision of the law can find the corresponding regulations and a person reading the regulations can find the corresponding law without an extensive search of indexes and tables.

Editorial features. The regulations have been arranged by titles. 

The text has been carefully edited and appropriate catchlines have been supplied. A source note under the first section of each regulation shows the agency which issued it, the approval date, the effective date if one is specified, the date of filing with the Secretary of State, and the File Number which it bears in the records of his office. The statutory authority for the adoption of the regulation is cited. Annotations of court decisions interpreting the regulations have been inserted. 

This set of R.&R.P.R. is published in both Spanish and English editions. Except in a few cases where the contrary clearly appears, the Spanish text has been treated as the official version. 

In some instances it has been necessary to change the English text as filed with the Secretary of State in order to correct apparent errors of translation.

Index and Tables. This volume contains a topical index of the titles which it covers. When the entire set is finished, the last volume will contain a complete and detailed index of all the titles. 

The Table of Agencies at the end of this volume, showing the regulations adopted by each agency which are included in these titles, will be replaced by a complete table at the end of the set showing all regulations of all agencies. 

Supplementation; Puerto Rico Register. R.&R.P.R. will be kept up to date by means of the Puerto Rico Register, which will be published periodically. This will be in the form of loose leaf pages, containing all changes and new provisions, which will be inserted in the original volumes of R.&R.P.R., replacing pages which have become obsolete. Thus, R.&R.P.R. will always be up to date with the latest issue of the Puerto Rico Register.

Printing and Binding. This volume has been produced in loose leaf form so that changes and new regulations can be incor- 

VIII

porated into R.&R.P.R. as quickly as possible after they become effective, and each section of the work will always be up to the minute.

This loose leaf ring binder has been chosen after exhaustive study of all available types of binders. Among its practical advantages are: (1) The pages lie absolutely flat no matter where you open it; (2) there are no hidden inner margins to force you to pry the pages apart in order to read them; and (3) pages can be inserted and removed with minimum time and effort. To insure durability under constant use, we have employed a quality paper throughout and strengthened the title tabs with reinforced holes.

In Appreciation. We acknowledge gratefully the advice, help, and constructive cooperation of all who made this set possible. 

Special appreciation is due the Secretary of State, Honorable 

Roberto Sánchez-Vilella, and Assistant Secretary of State, Honorable Nicolás Almiroty, for their effective cooperation and wise counsel in the planning and execution of this project, and to 

Honorable Hiram Torres Rigual, Executive Assistant to the

Governor, whose vision and tireless efforts assured the success of this undertaking.

As in Laws of Puerto Rico Annotated, the Spanish edition of this set was edited by Mr. Ignacio Rivera, Secretary of the 

Supreme Court of Puerto Rico. His great ability, wise judgment, and devotion to a high ideal deserve full credit for the excellence of this edition.

Conclusion. Equity Publishing Corporation, which performed the editorial work on Laws of Puerto Rico Annotated, is especially proud to have been chosen to edit and publish these Rules and 

Regulations of Puerto Rico, under a contract with the Secretary of State. We consider it a privilege to have this part in the progress and accomplishments of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. 

April, 1960

Equity Publishing Corporation 

Orford, New Hampshire

The Publisher.

Definitions § 22-1. Short title 

This subchapter shall be known as the "Regulations for Mini mum Facilities Developments". 

Authority. J.R. No. 104, app. July 1, 1953 [not set out in

§ 22-2. Applicability 

The dispositions of this subchapter shall be applicable to all the lots in developments with some public services commonly known as Minimum Facilities Developments, established or admin istered by the Puerto Rico Urban Renewal and Housing Corporation. 

§ 22-3. Definitions The following terms shall have the following meaning: 

(1) "Corporation" shall mean the Puerto Rico Urban Renewal and Housing Corporation. 

(2) "Minimum Facilities Developments" shall mean those developments with some public services established and administered by the Corporation under the dispositions of Joint Resolution 

No. 104, approved on July 1, 1953, in connection with Public Law 

No. 88, approved on June 22, 1957 [17 L.P.R.A. § 21 et seq.], as amended by Public Law No. 89, approved on June 26, 1964 

[17 L.P.R.A. § 22], and Executive Order No. 471, dated Febru ary 25, 1958.

April 30, 1966

(3) "Board" shall mean the Puerto Rico Planning Board. (4) "Family" shall mean a group of persons under the head of the family who regularly live together in the same dwelling unit, and it shall include those relatives that contribute economically to support the group. (5) "Head of the family" shall mean the member of the family with the maximum authority in the group. (6) "Board of Directors" shall mean the Board of Directors of the Puerto Rico Urban Renewal and Housing Corporation. 

DIVISION 2. PROCEDURE FOR THE SALE, LEASE AND GRANT OF USUFRUCTS OF THE LOTS IN THE MINIMUM FACILITIES DEVELOPMENTS SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 1. RESIDENTIAL LOTS 

22-21. Authorization and requisites for the sale, lease and grant of usufructs of residential lots 22-22. Special dispositions related to the lease of residential lots 

22-23. Special dispositions related to the grant of usufruct of residential lots 

22-24. Dispositions related to the sale of residential lots § 22-21. Authorization and requisites for the sale, lease and grant of usufructs of residential lots The Corporation may sell, lease or grant in usufruct to those eligible persons, as hereinafter provided in this subchapter, the residential lots established in the Minimum Facilities Developments under the following general conditions: (1) The purchaser, lessee or usufructuary of a lot shall transfer his house to, or shall build one on said lot for him and his family within 120 days after having signed a contract. The construction of the house shall be made according to the rules and regulations of the Board. In case the dispositions of this subd. (1) are not complied with, the contract may be rescinded and the lot shall be left free from obstacle or any improvements and the Corporation will not be obliged to indemnify. The period of time of 120 days may be deferred by the Corporation for a satisfactory reason. (2) The purchaser, lessee or usufructuary cannot alter the boundaries of the lot. Should he request a new measurement or replanting of the lot after he has come in possession of same, April 30, 1966 

Vol. 5, No. 4 2.2

Ch. T.17 § 22-22 

URBAN RENEWAL 

for any reason not attributable to the Corporation, he shall pay the Corporation for said work. 

(3) The Corporation shall execute a contract with the head of the family to whom a residential lot is sold, leased or granted in usufruct within 30 days after such person is duly notified by the Corporation either personally or by certified mail. (4) The purchaser, lessee or usufructuary cannot establish in the lot any kind of business, except those industries known as domestic industries, such as the needlework industry, or any other industry not in conflict with the regulations of the Board. (5) The purchaser, lessee or usufructuary that desires to make improvements in his property shall comply with the rules and regulations of the Board. (6) The purchaser, lessee or usufructuary shall abide by the easements established or those that in the future will be necessary to establish on his lot for the installation of the electric, telephone, aqueduct or sanitary systems. (7) The purchaser, lessee or usufructuary shall maintain his dwelling in good condition and the same shall be occupied exclusively by him and his family. (8) Any violation by the purchaser, lessee or usufructuary of any of the dispositions prescribed in this subchapter and any violation of the conditions established in the contract shall be sufficient for the rescission of the contract by the Corporation. § 22-22. Special dispositions related to the lease of residential lots (a) The lease contracts shall specify the period of time that they will be in effect. (b) In case of the decease of the lessee, the following priority is established for the occupancy of the lot: (1) The widow [or widower] and sons (minors) of the deceased. (2) Other heirs of the deceased residing in the dwelling at the time of his death. (3) Other heirs not residing in the dwelling, if eligible. (4) If among the heirs with a right to occupy the dwelling there should be more than one family head, they shall decide among themselves who will succeed the deceased in the dwelling. (5) If they cannot reach an agreement within a reasonable period of time, the lot shall revert to the Corporation and the heirs may sell the dwelling to an eligible family with the approval April 30, 1966

of the Corporation; or the Corporation may acquire same by paying its appraised value at the time of reversion. (6) In any case, the head of the family that substitutes the deceased or that by any reason rescinded the contract shall execute a new lease contract. (c) The lessee of a residential lot cannot sublet, transfer, rent or in any way dispose of the lease contract executed; neither shall he transfer, rent, lease or encumber the dwelling constructed on the lot without the written consent of the Corporation, except to obtain a loan from the Housing Bank of Puerto Rico. This consent shall be given by the Corporation only in the case that the new applicant meets with all the requisites for eligibility prescribed in this subchapter. (d) The Corporation shall collect from the lessee 1 percent of the sale price of the house or of the improvements made on the lot when said lessee decides to sell the house to another person accepted by the Corporation. The amount represented by the 1 percent collected will be used by the Corporation to pay part of the administrative expenses incurred by it in this transaction.

(5) If they cannot reach an agreement within a reasonable period of time, the usufruct of the lot shall revert to the Corporation and the heirs may sell the dwelling to an eligible family with April 30, 1966

Dispositions related to the sale of residential lots (a) The sale price of the lots in each development shall be determined by the Corporation taking into consideration the cost of construction, location, size and use of each lot. In those cases where the Corporation considers it necessary, it may determine the sale price of the lots based on an adjustment in the assessed value of same. (b) Lots shall be sold for cash or on an installment basis. On an installment basis the debt shall be guaranteed with a mortgage on the lot covering the balance due, and the sale conditions shall be those prevailing in the Housing Bank at the moment of sale. (c) Sales on an installment basis may be granted for periods of time ranging from 1 to 25 years or for a longer period of time at the discretion of the Executive Director of the Corporation. (d) The mortgage established may be administered by the Corporation, the Housing Bank or any other financial institution of high standing in Puerto Rico. (e) The purchaser shall not mortgage the lot during the first 5 years of acquisition without the written consent of the Corporation but a mortgage is hereby authorized to guarantee loans approved by the Federal Housing Administration, or a mortgage in favor of the Government Employees' Retirement System, the 

Teachers' Retirement System, the Employees' Retirement System of the Puerto Rico Water Resources Authority, the Veterans' 

Administration, the Housing Bank and the Government Employees' Association. The loan must be for the construction of improvements to his house or to liquidate the debt of the lot, if any. April 30, 1966

URBAN RENEWAL SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 2. NONRESIDENTIAL LOTS 

22-41. Convenience of nonresidential lots § 22-41. Convenience of nonresidential lots 

The Corporation, with the approval of the Board, shall provide commercial lots for public or semipublic use when considered necessary. Semipublic use shall mean those lots dedicated to churches, private schools or similar uses.

SUBDIVISION 3. PROCEDURE IN THE SALE AND LEASE OF NONRESIDENTIAL LOTS SECTIONS 

22-61. Sale and lease 

§ 22-61. Sale and lease 

Lots for commercial or semipublic uses shall be sold on a cash basis or they may be leased, preferably to those merchants or organizations affected by urban renewal projects or other public works performed by the Municipal or Commonwealth governments. 

DIVISION 3. REQUISITES FOR ELIGIBILITY AND APPLICATION FOR A LOT SECTIONS 

22-81. Requisites for eligibility 

22-82. Order of priority of applicants 

22-83. Application and investigation § 22-81. Requisites for eligibility 

Those persons with the following requisites shall be eligible to acquire a residential lot: (1) Be the head of a family. (2) A family with an income of $4,800 annually or less, after deductions for retirement system and social security are made. 

The Executive Director of the Corporation or the official on whom he delegates may consider as eligible families with an income in excess of $4,800 if there are circumstances that justify such eligibility. (3) No member of the family living in the house shall own another residential property. (4) The members of the family shall be persons of high moral standards and be known as such in the community where they live. April 30, 1966 

Vol. 5, No. 4 2.7

T.§ 22-82 Ch. 2 

HOUSING § 22-82. Order of priority of applicants 

Eligible families for lots shall be selected according to the following priority: (1) Families affected by urban renewal projects and other public works performed by Municipal or Commonwealth governments and families that have lost their houses due to hurricanes, water, floods, fires or any other disaster due to natural causes. (2) Families with high-income living in public housing projects and that are not able to solve their housing problem through private enterprise. (3) Families without a house of their own living in undesirable conditions. (4) Families being evicted through court action for any cause other than default in rental payments. (5) Families living in the rural zone that can prove to the Corporation their necessity to live in the urban zone due to total or partial physical inability of a member of the family and its necessity of medical treatment, or for any other urgent reason that justifies its necessity of living in the urban zone. (6) Other eligible families. 

§ 22-83. Application and investigation 

(a) The persons interested in obtaining a lot in the minimum developments shall fill out a written application provided by the Corporation. Thereafter, the Corporation will investigate the applicant to verify if he complies with the requisites established in this subchapter. (b) The Corporation will use the appropriate means to investigate the income of the applicant and of his family and other circumstances.

DIVISION 4. ASSIGNMENT OF LOTS SECTIONS 

22-101. Procedure 22-102. Effectiveness 

§ 22-101. Procedure 

(a) (1) The Corporation, after having studied the applications and made the necessary investigations, will prepare a registry of applicants for each municipality, and in it will write the name and address of eligible persons.

April 30, 1966 

Vol. 5, No. 4 2.8

Ch. T.17 § 22a-1 

URBAN RENEWAL 

(2) The eligible applicants must be included in said register in the proper order according to the priorities established in sec. 22-82 of this title. (3) The Corporation must notify all applicants of its decision in regard to the application and those applicants that are not included in the register of eligible families shall be informed of the reasons for not including them. (b) In case that the number of lots in a minimum development is lower than the number of eligible applicants in a municipality, the Corporation shall proceed to cast lots among the applicants that meet the requisites in order of priority. The lots not assigned after the priority order has been exhausted shall be cast among the remaining eligible applicants. 

§ 22-102. Effectiveness 

The regulation set out in this subchapter shall take effect as soon as it is published [in the Puerto Rico Register].

Subchapter 22a. PHA-Aided Low-Rent Housing Projects Operated by Urban Renewal and Housing Corporation DIVISION 1. STATEMENT OF POLICIES GOVERNING ADMISSION TO AND CONTINUED OCCUPANCY SECTIONS

§ 22a-1. Conditions governing eligibility 

(a) Eligibility for admission: There are to be eligible for admission to PHA-aided low-rent housing projects operated by this Corporation only those applicants who, at the time of admission, meet all the following requirements: 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 4 2.9

T.§ 22a-1 Ch. 2 

HOUSING 

(1) Who qualify as a family. (See sec. 22a-9 (a) of this title.) (2) Who qualify as a family of low income for admission as set forth in the latest Schedule of Maximum Income Limits fixed by this Corporation and approved by PHA. (See Exhibit I.) 

(3) Whose Net Family Assets do not exceed $2,500 except, that in the case of families evicted or forced to vacate to give way to a public improvement or redevelopment project, such assets, including the indemnity received for the demolished property, shall not exceed $4,000, provided that the Executive Director or his designee may waive the maximum asset limitations on a case to case basis in extraordinary circumstances and with consideration given to the type of assets and the cash income the family is receiving. (4) Who are: (A) to be displaced (see sec. 22a-2 (a) of this title), or (B) actually without housing through no fault of their own (see sec. 22a-2(b) of this title), or (C) about to be without housing as a result of a court order of eviction due to causes other than the fault of the tenant (see sec. 22a-2 (c) of this title), or (D) equivalent to condemned (see sec. 22a-2(d) of this title), or (E) living in dwelling determined to be unsafe, insanitary or overcrowded (see sec. 22a-2 (e) of this title). (5) Who conform to the occupancy standards set forth in sec. 22a-5 of this title. (6) Who by reason of the moral conduct of any member of the family who is to occupy the dwelling do not constitute a hazard to the residents of the project. (7) Who do not own a house unless it is substandard and relinquished for demolition, or unless it is established to the satisfaction of the Corporation that the applicant or the tenant cannot live in the house owned because it is not within normal commuting distance from his place of business or employment, provided that its value does not exceed the applicable amount prescribed in subsec. (a) (3) of this section. (b) Eligibility for continued occupancy: There are to be eligible for continued occupancy in all PHA-aided housing projects operated by this Corporation only those occupants who at the time of reexamination meet all the following requirements: 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 4 2.10

Ch. T.17 § 22a-1 

URBAN RENEWAL 

(1) Who qualify as a family (see sec. 22a-9 (a) of this title), except that a person or persons remaining as the residuum of a family shall be permitted to remain in occupancy. If an addition, related to the residuum by blood, marriage or adoption, is made to a residuum household, and the new group qualifies as a family, it shall be so considered.

The lessee of a residuum household may be allowed to bring an unrelated person into the dwelling for reasons of age, health or disability, subject to the approval of the Executive Director or his designee, and provided that: (A) The new household qualifies for continued occupancy in every respect except as a family; (B) A larger dwelling is not required to accommodate the enlarged household; and (C) It is understood that the person so admitted will not be permitted to continue in occupancy if the residuum is removed from or leaves the household. However, if the unrelated person has been residing with and taking care of the lessee for a period of 6 months or more, he may be considered as the residuum of a tenant family after the death of the original residuum lessee and be subject to the applicable provisions specified above. (2) Who qualify as a family of low income for continued occupancy as set forth in the latest Schedule of Maximum Income 

Limits fixed by this Corporation and approved by PHA. (See

Exhibit I.) 

(3) Whose net family assets do not exceed $4,000, provided that the Executive Director or his designee may waive the maximum asset limitation on a case to case basis in extraordinary circumstances and with consideration given to the type of assets and the cash income the family is receiving. Housing conditions prior to admission (a) (1) To be displaced: This provision is applicable to families who are to be displaced by any low-rent housing project or by any urban renewal project, or through action of a public body or court, either through the enforcement of housing standards or through the demolition, closing or improvement of dwelling units, as to families whose present or former dwellings are situated in areas determined by the Small Business Administration subsequent to April 1, 1965, to have been affected by a natural disaster, and which have been extensively damaged or destroyed as a result of such disaster. (2) This provision applies also to families who are required to move because they cannot afford the increased rent caused by improvement of a dwelling unit to bring it into compliance with housing standards prescribed by laws or codes. If due to a disaster, fire, 1972

storm, flood, etc., a family is occupying makeshift quarters or is being temporarily sheltered through the benevolence of some interested agency or individual solely for the purpose of protecting it from the elements while seeking housing accommodations, but the Small Business Administration did not determine that there is a disaster area, then such family shall be classified under this category. Evictions¹ by private enterprise or individuals necessary for cleaning sites to be used for works resulting in the benefit of groups in the community i.e., hospitals, schools, churches, asylums, etc., shall also be considered as to be displaced. The 3 categories discussed in this paragraph shall be considered "to be displaced" solely for the purposes of scoring the Housing Conditions Prior to Admission specified under sec. 22a-3(b) (1) (A)(i) of this title. (2) Families which are forced to take up residence with relatives or friends for reasons not the fault of their own. If through legal or common-law marriage, a member (son, daughter, etc.) of any family living in one of our projects forms a new family group, and cannot secure housing quarters elsewhere, the new family group shall be classified under this condition, provided that the tenant family member had been included in the family composition at time of admission, or was part of the natural growth of the family; or (3) Family members involuntarily living apart as separate entities without ready access to each other or to any facilities necessary to family life, for reasons not the fault of their own; or (4) Families whose place of abode is not within reasonable commuting distance for the family head to commute daily to his place of work or the cost or time involved in commuting is substantially in excess of that which is considered normal and usual. (e) Unsafe, insanitary or overcrowded dwellings: The Puerto

Rico Urban Renewal and Housing Corporation considers the existence of any of the following conditions an adequate basis for determining that a dwelling is unsafe, insanitary or overcrowded: (1) Location: The location of the unit is such that it creates a health, fire, or safety hazard for the occupants of such dwelling unit. (2) Condition of structure: The condition of the structure is such as to create serious safety or health hazards by reason of structural deficiencies or of continuous dampness or exposure, brought about by neglect or dilapidation. (3) Water supply: Lack of potable water within the dwelling unit. (4) Sanitary facilities: Where conditions of sewerage systems, toilet and bath facilities are found to be inadequate according to health and safety standards generally acceptable. (5) Kitchen facilities: Lack of permanent, safe, and reasonably efficient kitchen facilities within the dwelling unit, including sink with running water and provisions for cooking stove. (6) Lighting facilities: Dwelling not wired or inadequately wired for electric lighting. 

(7) Light and ventilation: Living room, bedroom or kitchen with no windows, or with windows on an airshaft, or toilet or bathroom without adequate ventilation. (8) Overcrowded: The number of persons occupying a dwelling unit exceeds the maximum occupancy limits established (see 1971

sec. 22a-5 of this title) or when 2 or more families are occupying a dwelling unit designed for single-family occupancy. (f) Attached as Exhibit CRUV-PR-Viv.-67 is a score sheet to be used by the staff of this Corporation in evaluating the physical housing conditions of families found to be living in unsafe, insanitary, or overcrowded dwellings.

(C) To facilitate and encourage normal family life when disrupted because the location of the family head's place of employment does not permit him to commute daily to the family's place of abode. (D) To solve existing serious social and moral problems in which the safety and well-being of minors are involved.

§ 22a-5. Occupancy standards 

To avoid overcrowding and prevent waste of space, dwellings are to be assigned in accordance with the occupancy standards set forth below. Where it is found that the size of the dwelling is no longer suitable for the family in accordance with these standards, the family is to be required to move as soon as a dwelling of appropriate size becomes available. 

(1) Number of bedrooms: 

1 2 3 4 5 

Number of persons Minimum

Maximum 22 2357 11 1 2 4 12 (A) The minimum standards established above for multibedroom units may be reduced by one person when the sex, relationship, health or disability so require. (2) In assigning dwellings to families, consideration shall be given to the age, sex, and relationship of the members of the family and other factors, such as health and disability. The number of persons and relationship of members of the family in determining the maximum occupancy for each bedroom shall be: (A) Married couple with a child under 3 years of age. (B) Three children of same sex under 13 years of age. (3) Dwelling will be assigned not requiring the use of the living room for sleeping purposes. (4) In applying the above standards, every member of the family, regardless of age, shall be considered as a person. (5) Accommodation of oversize families: (A) Admission: Families whose size is in excess of the maximum number of persons established for the largest size unit in the project may be permitted to occupy 2 units (preferably contiguous) provided such units contain no more rooms than necessary to

accommodate the family without overcrowding, considering as bedroom the living room and the kitchen of one of the 2 units. (B) Continued occupancy. (A), clause (5) of this section. (6) Two or more unrelated elderly single persons, nonelderly single persons 45 years of age or over displaced from Federally- Aided Urban Renewal Projects, PHA sites and Commonwealth or Municipal Public Works, or remaining members of tenant families which are each eligible as individuals for admission or continued occupancy as the case might be, may be permitted to live in the same unit, even though the combined income of the group may exceed the limit for a family of the same number of persons, provided that: (A) Rent must be determined separately for each person in accordance with the approved rent schedule; except that in cases where 2 unrelated elderly single persons are accommodated in the same dwelling unit, if the contract rent after considering total income is less than $13.00, the rent shall be divided among them in equal parts. A minimum rent of $3.50 shall be paid by each one of them or what is the same, $7.00 will be the minimum rent for the dwelling unit in these special cases. When a single person is living in a dwelling unit and another person is to be accommodated in that unit, a special reexamination shall be made in order to establish a rent after considering the total income. (B) Separate leases are to be executed with each person. (C) Each lease should provide that the unit is leased to all occupants as tenants in common of the entire unit, and each tenant should have the right to use and occupy the entire unit in common with his cotenant.

§ 22a-6. Receipt of applications and determination of eligibility 

This section sets forth the basic steps which are to be taken in obtaining and verifying data for the purpose of (a) determining whether applicants meet the conditions of eligibility for admission set forth in sec. 22a-1 of this title; (b) determining the order of selection for admission established in sec. 22a-3 of this title; (c) determining the rent to be charged families admitted in accordance with sec. 22a-4 of this title; and (d) the size of dwelling required in accordance with sec. 22a-5 of this title. (1) Application for admission: The application for admission. constitutes the basic form of the permanent record to be established for each family from which an application for admission is accepted. To assure compliance with the order of selection for admission as set forth in sec. 22a-3 of this title, applications from all persons seeking admission to a project are, until the end of the Initial Operating Period, to be accepted, regardless of the number of eligible applications on file. If, after the end of the Initial

Operating Period, there are sufficient applications on file from families having a substantial housing need to fill vacancies as they occur, additional applications from families living in unsafe, insanitary and overcrowded dwellings are not to be taken. In any event, a pool of eligible applications shall be maintained to the extent possible and as necessary to assure full occupancy of the projects at all times. (2) Procedure governing receipt of applications: For each family applying for admission there shall be obtained and recorded on Application for Admission (Form CRUV-PR-Viv.-66) sufficient data and information which, when verified, will permit proper determination of and certification as to the family's eligibility and order of selection for admission, the rent to be charged and the size of the dwelling required by the family. The accuracy of the information provided shall be attested to and the form signed by a responsible member of the applicant's family, preferably the family head. All entries shall be made in ink or indelible pencil, or typed in. 

Corrections or changes shall be made by lining through the original item and entering the correct data. All changes shall be dated and initialed by the person recording the change. The reason and authority for making the change shall also be noted. If during the application interview it appears that the applicant is definitely not eligible, the applicant shall be so informed and the application 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 2 2.21

T.§ 22a-6 Ch. 2 

HOUSING 

classified as ineligible. Sufficient information shall be entered on the application form to establish ineligibility and the applicant's signature shall be obtained. 

(3) Verification and documentation of application data: To substantiate determinations with respect to eligibility and order of selection for admission, dwelling size and rent to be charged and to establish the validity of the Corporation certification of a family's eligibility for admission, the representations made by the applicant family in its application for admission are to be verified and all verified findings relating thereto are to be documented. Documentation of verified findings shall consist of, but not routinely be limited to, the following items: 

(See Annexes IV-A-IV-H and form CRUV-PR-Viv.-74.) 

(A) Letters or other statements from employers and other pertinent sources giving authoritative information concerning all items and amounts of income and deductions, together with other eligibility and preference determinations; (B) Photostatic or carbon copies of documents in the applicant's possession which substantiate his statements, or a brief summary of the pertinent contents of such documents signed and dated by the Corporation's employee who viewed them; (C) Statements from self-employed persons, and from persons whose earnings are irregular, such as salesmen, taxi drivers, etc., setting forth gross receipts, itemized expenses and net income; (D) Memoranda of verification data obtained by personal interview, telephone or other means, with source, date received, and the person receiving the information clearly indicated; (E) A record of the physical inspection of the applicant's housing accommodations or other documentary evidence that the dwelling is unsafe, insanitary, or overcrowded, and that the applicant is actually living in such dwelling. This is required only when residence in unsafe, insanitary or overcrowded housing is a condition of his eligibility for admission or is necessary to determine order of selection for admission (see sec. 22a−1(a) (4) (E) of this title); (F) Proof that an applicant is, if claimed, actually dispossessed through a court order of eviction by no fault of his own; (G) A court order of eviction, if applicant claims that he is about to be without housing through no fault of his own; 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 2 2.22

Ch. 

T.17 § 22a-6 URBAN RENEWAL 

(H) Proof that an applicant is, if claimed, to be displaced under one of the circumstances cited in secs. 22a-1(a)(4)(A) and 

22a-2(a) of this title; (I) Proof that an applicant is, if claimed, living in conditions equivalent to condemned as specified in secs. 22a-1(a)(4) (D) and 

22a-2(d) of this title; (J) Proof that an applicant was, if claimed, displaced under any of the conditions specified under sec. 22a-2(a) of this title; (K) Birth certificate or other proof of age for nonelderly single persons of 45 years of age or over displaced from Federally-Aided Urban Renewal Projects, PHA Sites and Comonwealth or Munic ipal Public Works. 

(4) Summary of verified data: 

(A) Verification data shall be reviewed and evaluated as received for completeness, accuracy, and conclusiveness. Where the information received is not completely adequate in all respects, followups or new efforts to obtain such information shall be made and carried through to conclusion. If during the verification process it becomes evident that for one or more reasons an applicant is ineligible for admission, the investigation shall be discontinued and the applicant notified of his ineligibility and the reason therefor. (B) As verifications of all necessary items for each application are completed, a summary of the verified information shall be prepared on Form CRUV-PR-Viv.-68. The summary shall cover the following determinations and the basis for such determinations: (i) Eligibility of the applicant group as a family; (ii) Eligibility of the family with respect to income limits for admission; (iii) Eligibility of the family with respect to its net assets; (iv) Eligibility of the family with respect to housing need; (v) Eligibility of the family with respect to occupancy standards; (vi) Eligibility of the family with respect to moral conduct; (vii) Eligibility of the family with respect to residence in the municipality; (viii) Order of selection for admission; (ix) Urgency of the family's need for housing; (x) Size of unit to which the family should be assigned; (xi) Rent which family should pay; (xii) Nonownership of house, or ownership subject to sec. 

22a-1(a) (8) of this title. : 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 2 2.23

T.§ 22a-6 Ch. 2 

HOUSING 

(5) Rechecking verified findings prior to admission: Only families of low income who at the time of admission meet specified requirements shall be admitted. To comply with this, the procedure established below must be followed by the Housing Investigator or the Housing Manager: (A) If the verified data used in determining the applicant's eligibility, order of selection for admission, rent to be charged and size of dwelling required are no more than 3 months old and the applicant states that no change has occurred in his status, the data will be accepted as reflecting the applicant's status at the time of admission. If any change is reported the person in charge of the investigation must verify the change, record, and sign it. In the event the applicant states that there has been no change in his family income or any other requirement for eligibility, he or she must sign a certificate to that effect. (See Exhibit V, Form CRUV- PR-Viv.-77.) (B) If data on file are over 3 months old, all factors are to be reverified and findings recorded except as follows: (i) In the case of supports given or received voluntarily, and of Public Welfare assistance, once a year verification is acceptable. (ii) In the case of such regular incomes as Social Security benefits, Veteran Administration awards, Retirement Pensions from public and private enterprises, once verified reverification will be needed only when a change in the amount received is expected, as per applicable laws and regulations. Reverification may be handled informally by telephone or other means, provided findings are properly documented, together with the name of the source of information, by whom obtained, and when. This should, of course, be signed and dated by the personnel responsible for passing on such matters. (6) Certification: As a part of the application record of each applicant determined to be eligible for admission, the tenant selector is to certify that an investigation has been made of such family and that on the basis of this investigation it has been determined that the applicant and his family meet all the conditions governing eligibility. 

§ 22a-7. Leasing of dwelling units 

A lease agreement shall be entered into between this Corporation and each family which is to occupy a dwelling. This lease agreement 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 2 2.24

Ch. T.17 § 22a-7 

URBAN RENEWAL 

shall be kept current at all times and shall reflect the rent being charged and the conditions governing occupancy. 

(1) Execution of lease agreement: 

(A) For each family accepted as a tenant the "Head of the family" (see sec. 22a–9 (b) of this title) accepted as a tenant, shall be required to execute a lease agreement prior to actual admission (Form CRUV-PR-Viv.-101). One copy of the agreement is to be given to the tenant and one executed copy shall be retained in the tenant's file. (B) If, through any cause, any signer of the agreement ceases to be a member of the tenant family, the agreement shall be voided and a new one executed and signed by a remaining member of the family who can qualify as a tenant, provided the family is otherwise eligible for continued occupancy. If no member is qualified to sign a new lease agreement, the existing one shall be voided and the family required to vacate. (C) If a tenant family transfers to a different dwelling in the same or another low-rent project operated by this Corporation, the existing lease agreement shall be cancelled and a new one signed by a member of the family who meets the requirements set forth above, for the dwelling into which the family is to move. (D) If at any time during the life of the lease agreement, a change in the tenant status results in the need of changing or amending any provision of the agreement, or if this Corporation desires to waive any provision with respect to any tenant, either (a) the existing lease agreement is to be cancelled and a new one executed, (b) an appropriate rider is to be prepared and made part of the existing agreement, or (c) appropriate insertions are to be made within the instrument. All copies of all occupancy agreements, and of all riders and insertions are to be dated and signed by the tenant and the management aide. 

(2) Cancellation of the occupancy agreement: Cancellation of a tenant's lease is to be in accordance with the provisions of the tenant's lease agreement. (3) Acquainting tenants with conditions of occupancy: Prior to or at the time of signing the lease agreement, assistance shall be given each applicant accepted as a tenant in understanding (a) the obligations which he and his family assume as tenants of lowrent housing; (b) the privileges to which they are entitled; and 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 2 2.25

T.§ 22a-7 Ch. 2 

HOUSING 

(c) the responsibility of this Corporation to its tenants and to the public in fulfilling its obligations to operate the projects in conformance with controlling legislation. This assistance shall be given through interviews conducted by one or more qualified employees of the Corporation. It is necessary that during the interview each tenant receive a copy of the rules which govern the families in a housing project. Such interview, should, among other things: (A) Summarize, within the understanding of the applicant, the purposes of the local low-rent public housing program; (B) Explain the principle of relating rent to income; (C) Acquaint the applicant with provisions of legislation which most directly affect him and his family, such as the establishment of conditions of eligibility of admission and for continued occupancy and the order of selection for admission in the selection of tenants; (D) Assist the applicant in understanding the provisions of the lease agreement and the terminology used therein; (E) Impress upon the applicant his responsibility as a tenant for paying rent when due and advise him specifically of the Corporation's regulations with respect to rent payments; (F) Inform the applicant of his responsibilities with respect to the care of his dwelling, grounds, project equipment, and other phases of tenant maintenance; (G) Provide opportunity for the applicant to present questions on matters on which he desires further explanation or clarification; (H) Lay the foundation for and encourage a cooperative tenant-management relationship. § 22a-8. Reexamination of tenant eligibility and redetermination of net family income (a) Periodic reexamination of eligibility and adjustments of rent: (1) To assure that tenancy in the projects is restricted to families meeting the eligibility requirements for continued occupancy set forth in sec. 22a-1 (b) of this title, and that such families are charged appropriate rents, the eligibility status and the income of each tenant's family is to be reexamined annually as per the established Schedule of Regular Annual Reexaminations; provided, that the length of time between the admission of a family and the first reexamination may be extended to not more than 18 months if necessary to fit a reexamination schedule. However, families 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 2 2.26

Ch. T.17 § 22a-8 

URBAN RENEWAL 

whose bona fide heads (or their spouses) or whose sole members are 62 years of age or over, are to be reexamined only once every 2 years, provided that for these families not more than 24 months may elapse between reexaminations or between their admission and first reexamination. (b) Readjustment of rent between periodic reexaminations: (1) Rents may be readjusted between admission and first annual or biennial reexamination or between other regularly scheduled annual or biennial reexaminations as applicable only when a substantial change in income occurs. (2) All factors pertinent to redetermination of rent shall be fully verified and considered at time of each redetermination, except as provided in sec. 22a-6(5) (B) (ii) of this title. (3) Effective date for changes in rent resulting from redetermination of rent as described under clause (1) of this subsection shall be the first day of the month following that in which the tenant reports the change, except as provided in clause (7) of this subsection. (4) Eligibility will be redetermined only at time of regularly scheduled annual or biennial reexamination, as applicable. (5) Once a family has had a decrease in rent, pursuant to clause (1) of this subsection, that tenant will be required to report promptly all subsequent increases in family income occurring prior to his next regular annual or biennial reexamination. (6) If at the time of the regular reexamination it is not possible to make a determination of Net Family Income for the ensuing 

12-month or 24-month period, as applicable, with a reasonable degree of accuracy because of conditions such as the following: (A) Tenant is unemployed and there are no anticipated prospects of employment, (B) The conditions of employment are so unstable as to invalidate usual and normal standards for determination of income, an estimate will be made and those tenants will be notified that all subsequent increases in income and family circumstances affecting the determination of income are to be reported. (7) Increases in rent resulting from substantial increases in income as per reports required from tenants as specified under clauses (5) and (6) of this subsection will be effective the first day of the month following that in which the substantial increase in income occurred. 1971

(1) Receipt of application for continued occupancy:

For each family applying for continued occupancy sufficient data and information shall be shown on this form which, when verified, will permit proper determination of and certification as to the family's eligibility for continued occupancy, the rent to be charged, and the size of dwelling required by the family. The accuracy of the information provided should be attested to, and the form signed, by a responsible member of the family, preferably the family head. All entries shall be made in ink or indelible pencil or typed in. Corrections or changes shall be made by lining through the original item and entering the correct data. All changes shall be dated and initialed by the persons recording the change. The reason and authority for making such change will also be noted. (B) The application for continued occupancy provides space for recording: (i) Family data including: (a) The name, relationship to family head, sex, age, and employment status of each person who is residing in the dwelling; (b) For any persons who were not members of the family group the last time the family's eligibility status was determined, the date of birth; (c) Any change in the status of the family since the previous determination of eligibility, as that of a disabled, 1971

§ 22a-9. Definition of terms (a) (1) Family: Family means (1) a group of 2 or more persons related by blood, marriage or legal adoption, who will live regularly together in the same dwelling unit in the project; or (2) a single person 62 years of age or over or who is under a disability as defined in sec. 223 of the Social Security Act¹ or is handicapped within the meaning of sec. 202 of the Housing Act of 19592 or (3) a nonelderly and nonhandicapped single person 45 years of age. or over displaced from Federally Aided Urban Renewal Project, from the site of a federally aided low-rent housing project or 

Commonwealth or Municipal Public Works. 

(2) There may be also considered as part of a family other persons who will live regularly as a part of the family group (including foster children and members of the family temporarily absent), and whose income and resources are available in meeting the living expenses of the group. (3) The above definition of "family" does not exclude a person living alone during the temporary absence of a family member who will later live regularly as part of the family. (4) Elderly families means: Families whose heads (or their spouses) or whose sole members are 62 years of age or over or are under a disability as defined in sec. 223 of the Social Security

To be under a disability as defined in this section does not mean that a person must be receiving disability benefits from the Social Security Administration (e.g.) a person under such a disability might receive benefits from the Veterans' Administration or some other agency or not be entitled to benefits from any source.

However, the necessity for such an arrangement must be evidenced by a doctor's certificate or must be deemed essential, and so certified by welfare or other responsible sources. (d) Serviceman: For the purpose of determining order of selection for admission a "serviceman" means a person (man or woman) now in the active military or naval service of the United States who has also served therein at any time (a) on or after September 16, 1940, and prior to July 26, 1947, (b) on or after April 6, 1917, and prior to November 11, 1918, or (c) on or after June 27, 1950, and prior to February 1, 1955. (e) Family of a veteran or serviceman: (1) A family is a "family of a veteran or serviceman" when: (A) The head of the family is a veteran or serviceman; (B) A member of the family, related to the head by blood, marriage, or adoption, is a veteran or serviceman; (C) The former head of the family is a deceased veteran or serviceman, provided his spouse has not remarried, or (D) A former member of the family, related to the head by blood, marriage, or adoption, is a deceased veteran or serviceman and was a member of the family at the time of death. (2) To qualify as a "family of a veteran or serviceman" the veteran or serviceman, unless deceased, must be living with the family or be only temporarily absent unless: (A) The veteran or serviceman, formerly the head, is permanently absent because of hospitalization, separation, or desertion; (B) The veteran or serviceman, formerly the head, is divorced, provided there remains in the family one or more persons for whose support he is still legally or morally responsible and provided that the spouse has not remarried; or (C) The veteran or serviceman, not the family head, is permanently hospitalized, provided that he was a member of the family at the time he was hospitalized and provided further there remain in the family 2 or more persons related to him by blood, marriage or adoption. (f) Military or naval service of the United States: "Military or

Naval Service of the United States" means only the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, and since July 29, 1945, the commissioned corps of the U.S. Public Health Service. Such service does not include Merchant Marine, Red Cross, UNRRA,

ECA, or any other organization not actually part of the military or naval service of the United States. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 2 2.35

T.§ 22a-9 Ch. 2 

HOUSING 

(g) Minor: "Minor" means a person less than 21 years of age, other than the head of a family or his spouse and not legally emancipated. (An unborn child may not be counted as a minor.) (h) Utilities: "Utilities" means water, electricity, gas, and any other lighting and cooking fuels. (i) Contract rent: "Contract rent" means the rent charged a tenant for use of the dwelling accommodation, equipment, services, and utilities supplied by the project. Contract rent does not include charges for utilities which may be purchased by the project and sold to the tenant as a transaction separate from the payment of such rent, charges for excess utility consumption or miscellaneous charges. (j) Gross rent: "Gross rent" means "contract rent" plus the estimated value or cost to the tenant for reasonable amounts of utilities not included in the contract rent. (k) Displaced families: Families actually or about to be without housing or living in conditions equivalent to condemned or in dwellings determined to be unsafe, insanitary or overcrowded, and which were displaced for any of the reasons specified in sec. 22a- 

2(a) of this title, and filed an application for admission within one year after being so displaced, except for families who refused the opportunity for housing offered by this Corporation when they were to be displaced. (1) Date of full availability: "Date of full availability" with respect to each project shall mean the last day of the month in which substantially all dwelling units in such project become available for occupancy. (m) Initial operating period: "Initial operating period" with respect to each project shall mean the period commencing with the date of initiation of such project and ending with either (a) the end of the calendar quarter in which 95 percent of the dwelling units in such project are occupied, or (b) the end of the calendar quarter which is 6, 7 or 8 months after the date of full availability of such project, or (c) the end of the calendar quarter next preceding the date of physical completion of such project, whichever is the earlier.

Text references. The Housing Act of 1959 mentioned in the text is classified to 12 U.S.C. § 1701 et seq.

§ 22a-21. Proposed definition of family income for rent and eligibility applicable in projects under the leasing housing program-Exhibit A 

(a) Aggregate family income: (1) "Aggregate family income" means the income from any source whatsoever, as defined below, before deductions or exemptions, anticipated to be received during the 12 months following the admission or redetermination of net family income (as the case may be) by all persons, including minors, actually occupying or who are going to occupy the dwelling, and by a family head temporarily separated from the group. (2) Aggregate family income shall include: (A) The full amount, before any payroll deductions, of regular wages and salaries, including other compensation for personal services (such as commissions, fees and tips). (B) Compensation for overtime wages and salaries, in the amount by which it exceeds $100 per year. (C) Bonuses received from employers, in the amount by which they exceed $200 per year. (D) Net income from the operation of a business or profession. Expenditures for business expansion or amortization of capital investment shall not be considered in determining this net income. Installment payments for a motor vehicle used as the principal means of earning a living are not amortization of capital indebtedness and shall, therefore, be considered as expense in determining this net income. (E) Interest and dividends. (F) Net income of any kind from real or personal property. (G) The full amount received from annuities, periodic payments derived from insurance policies, retirement income, pensions, periodic benefits for disability or death and other similar types of periodic receipts. (H) Payment in lieu of earnings, such as unemployment and disability compensations, social security benefits, workmen's compensation and dismissal wages, excluding, however, lump-sum payments under health and accident insurance and under workmen's compensation. (I) Cash relief receipts including rental allowances. (J) Periodic and determinable allowances, such as alimony and regular contributions or gifts, including amounts received from any persons not residing in the dwelling. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 2 2.38

Ch. T.17 § 22a-21 

URBAN RENEWAL 

(K) The full amount received for the care of foster children and for the care of dependent adults. (L) All regular pay, special payments, and allowances (such as longevity, hazardous duty, overseas duty, rental allowances, allowances for dependents, etc.) received by a member of the

Armed Forces who is the head of the family, whether or not he is living in the dwelling, or by any other member of the Armed Forces who is living in the dwelling. The value of the serviceman's rations whether furnished in kind or supplied through a cash allowance shall not be included. (M) The additional income received by enrollees and trainees from Titles I, II, and V of U.S. Public Law 88-452, Economic Opportunity Act of 1964. 

(3) The following are not to be included in aggregate family income: (A) Amounts which are specifically received for, or are a reimbursement of, the cost of illness or medical care. (B) Casual and irregular gifts. (C) Lump-sum additions to family assets, such as inheritances, insurance payments, capital gains, settlements for personal or property losses, and mustering-out pay of recently discharged veterans. (If such sums exceed the maximum assets permissible, the family will be ineligible.) (D) Amounts paid by the United States Government to a veteran or to an educational institution for use in meeting costs of tuition, fees, and books, to the extent that such amounts are used.¹ (E) Amounts of educational scholarships which are paid directly to the educational institution for use in meeting the costs of tuition, fees, and books, to the extent that such amounts are so used.¹ (F) Amounts of educational scholarships paid directly to the student under conditions that such amounts be used to meet the costs of tuition, fees, and books, to the extent that such amounts are so used.¹ (G) Amounts actually paid by the Bureau of Social Welfare as school subsidy to children receiving economic assistance from that Bureau, as long as they attend school.

Earned income is defined in pars. (2) (A), (B), (C), (D), and (L) of the above definition of aggregate family income, subsec. (a) of this section. This deduction is allowed to reflect normal expenses incident to employment and is in lieu of specific deductions previously allowed for Social Security, employee contributions to retirement, group insurance, hospitalization or other fringe benefits, furnishing of laundering of uniforms, provision of personal tools, union dues, purchase of lunches and other expenses incidental to employment. This deduction also includes the cost of normal local public transportation from home to place of employment and return. No other deductions except as specifically authorized below shall be allowed. This deduction shall be allowed to the earned income of the head of family and/or spouse regardless of the amounts of any compulsory deductions made by an employer. (ii) In case where the head of family and/or spouse is employed at a location beyond the area served by local public transportation, the excess cost above normal local transportation cost actually paid for regular transportation between his home and place of employment shall be allowed as a deduction. (e.g. If the local bus fare is 10¢, normal local transportation would be 20¢ per day or $1.00 per week for 5 working days. If a worker is employed in another town and must pay 25¢ fare on an interurban bus or public taxi, his total cost would be 50¢ per day or $2.50 per week. The excess cost over normal local transportation would be $2.50 less $1.00, or $1.50 per week which shall be allowed as a deduction.) (2) Aggregate family income shall include: (A) The full amount, before any payroll deductions, of regular wages and salaries, including other compensation for personal services (such as commissions, fees and tips). (B) Compensation for overtime wages and salaries, in the amount by which it exceeds $100 per year. (C) Bonuses received from employers, in the amount by which they exceed $200 per year. (D) Net income from the operation of a business or profession. Expenditures for business expansion or amortization of capital investment shall not be considered in determining this net income. Installment payments for a motor vehicle used as the principal means of earning a living are not amortization of capital indebtedness and shall, therefore, be considered as expense in determining this net income. (E) Interest and dividends. (F) Net income of any kind from real or personal property. (G) The full amount received from annuities, periodic payments derived from insurance policies, retirement income, pensions, periodic benefits for disability or death and other similar types of periodic receipts. (I) Cash relief receipts including rental allowances. (J) Periodic and determinable allowances, such as alimony and regular contributions or gifts, including amounts received from any persons not residing in the dwelling. (K) The full amount received for the care of foster children and for the care of dependent adults. (A) Ten percent shall be allowed on all earned income. 

Earned income is defined in pars. (2) (A), (B), (C), (D) and (L) of the above definition of "aggregate family income", subsec. (a) of this section. This deduction is allowed to reflect normal expenses incident to employment and is in lieu of specific deductions previously allowed for Social Security, employee contributions to retirement, group insurance, hospitalization or other fringe benefits, furnishing of laundering of uniforms, provision of personal tools, union dues, purchase of lunches and other expenses incidental to employment. This deduction also includes the cost of normal local public transportation from home to place of employment and return. No other deductions except as specifically authorized below shall be allowed. This deduction shall be allowed to all wage earners regardless of the amounts of any compulsory deductions made by an employer. (B) In cases where a worker is employed at a location beyond the area served by local public transportation, the excess cost above normal local transportation cost actually paid for regular transportation between his home and place of employment shall be allowed as a deduction. (e.g. If the local bus fare is 10¢, normal local transportation would be 20¢ per day or $1.00 per week for 5 working days. If a worker is employed in another town and must pay 25¢ fare on an interurban bus or public taxi, his total cost would be 50¢ per day or $2.50 per week. The excess cost over normal local transportation would be $2.50 less $1.00, or $1.50 per week which shall be allowed as a deduction.) (C) Reasonable amounts actually paid to other than members of the family for the care of children or aged or incapacitated family members to permit a wage earner to engage in a gainful occupation outside the home shall be allowed as a deduction, provided that (a) no other family member is available to provide the necessary care, and (b) in no event the amount deducted is greater than the amount of net income (after the earned income expense deduction allowed under par. (b)(2) (A) of this section) produced by the family member thus released for such occupation. Related policies and procedures: 

(1) Displaced families may be admitted, and transfers from other low-rent housing projects may be made, under the "regular" or "special" rent category, according to their income, from among families whose income is above the maximum income limit associated with the "hardship" rent category. (2) New admissions of nondisplaced families are to be made under the "regular" rent category, from among families whose net income for rent is above the maximum income limit for rent associated with the "special" rent category. (3) Families in occupancy who suffer economic setbacks could apply for a lower rent, either under the "special" or "hardship" rent categories as applicable, after demonstrating their income to be below the qualifying income limit for the rent requested. These interim redeterminations of rent will be made effective the first day of the month in which the decrease in income is reported. The affected families will benefit of the lower rent until their next annual reexamination when a new rent and eligibility determination will be performed. (4) At the time of the annual reexamination all families paying either "hardship" or "special" rents, and whose income has increased above the qualifying income limit for the rent established will be charged the corresponding rent according to the above schedule. (5) Elderly families to be admitted in any of the fourteen units specially designed for elderlies could be admitted under "regular", "special" or the "hardship" rent category according to their income. 1971

§ 22a-61. Eligibility for admission 

There are to be eligible for admission to PHA-aided low-rent housing projects operated by this Corporation only those who, at the time of admission, meet all the following requirements: (1) Who qualify as a family. (2) Who qualify as a family of low income as set forth in the following Schedule of Maximum Income Limits fixed by this Corporation and approved by HAA.

(4) Who are: (A) To be displaced: (i) This provision is applicable to families who are to be displaced by any low-rent housing project or by any urban renewal project, or through action of a public body or court either through the enforcement of housing standards or through the demolition, closing or improvement of dwelling units, as to families whose present or former dwellings are situated in areas determined by the Small Business Administration, subsequent to April 1, 1965, to have been affected by a natural disaster, and which have been extensively damaged or destroyed as a result of such disaster. (ii) This provision applies also to families who are required to move because they cannot afford the increased rent caused by improvement of a dwelling unit to bring it into compliance with housing standards prescribed by laws or codes. If due to a disaster, fire, storm, flood, etc., a family is occupying makeshift quarters or is being temporarily sheltered through the benevolence of some interested agency or individual solely for the purpose of protecting it from the elements while seeking housing accommodations but the Small Business Administration did not determine there is a disaster area, then such family shall be classified under this category. Evictions by private enterprises or individuals necessary for clearing sites to be used for works resulting in the benefit of groups in the community, i.e., hospitals, schools, churches, asylums, etc., shall also be considered as to be displaced. The 3 categories discussed in this paragraph shall be considered "to be displaced" solely for the purposes of scoring the housing conditions prior to admission specified under Section III-B-1-a (1). (B) Actually without housing due to causes other than the fault of the tenant: A family shall be classified as "actually without housing", if being temporarily sheltered by an interested agency or individual because the family has been actually dispossessed through a court order of eviction due to causes other than the fault of the tenant. (C) About to be without housing due to causes other than the fault of the tenant: This provision shall apply to families against which a court order of eviction has been issued for reasons other than the fault of their own. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 2 2.81

T.§ 22a-61 Ch. 2 

HOUSING 

(D) Equivalent to condemned: Situations that shall fall into this category are the following: (i) Families which are forced to take up residence in makeshift quarters for reasons not the fault of their own; or (ii) Families which are forced to take up residence with relatives or friends for reasons not the fault of their own; or (iii) Family members involuntarily living apart as separate entities without ready access to each other or to any facilities necessary to family life, for reasons not the fault of their own; or (iv) Families whose place of abode is not within reasonable commuting distance for the family head to commute daily to his place of work or the cost or time involved in commuting is substantially in excess of that which is considered normal and usual. (E) Unsafe, insanitary or overcrowded dwellings: The Puerto

Rico Urban Renewal and Housing Corporation considers the existence of any of the following conditions an adequate basis for determining that a dwelling is unsafe, insanitary and overcrowded: (i) Location: The location of the unit is such that it creates a health, fire, or safety hazard for the occupants of such dwelling unit. (ii) Condition of structure: The condition of the structure is such as to create serious safety or health hazards by reason of structural deficiencies or of continuous dampness or exposure, brought about by neglect or dilapidation. (iii) Water supply: Lack of potable water within the dwelling unit. (iv) Sanitary facilities: The conditions of sewerage systems, toilet and bath facilities are found to be inadequate according to health and safety standards generally acceptable. (v) Kitchen facilities: Lack of permanent, safe, and reasonably efficient kitchen facilities within the dwelling unit, including sink with running water and provisions for cookstove. (vi) Lighting facilities: Dwelling not wired or inadequately wired for electric lighting. 

(vii) Light and ventilation: Living room, bedroom or kitchen with no windows, or with windows on an airshaft, or toilet or bathroom without adequate ventilation. 

(viii) Overcrowded: The number of persons occupying a dwelling unit exceeds the maximum occupancy limits established, 1971

§ 22a-62. Selection of tenants for public housing 

(a) Every applicant family shall at least meet one of the following factors or conditions prior to admission: (1) Factors to be scored: (A) Housing conditions prior to admission. (i) Family is to be displaced: Score (a) If family as defined in acceptations (1) and (2) of sec. 22a-63 (a) (1) of this title. 550 (b) If family as defined in acceptation (3) of sec. 22a-62 (a) (1) of this title. 95 (ii) Family is actually without housing due to no fault of its own. 450 (iii) Family is about to be without housing due to no fault of its own. 350 (iv) Family is living under conditions equivalent to condemned: (a) Family is living in makeshift quarters. (b) Family has taken up residence with friends or relatives. 250 150 (c) Family members involuntarily living apart as separate entities. 100 (d) Residence of family not within reasonable commuting distance from the head's place of employment. 50 (v) Family is living in unsafe, insanitary or overcrowded housing conditions. 5-150 (B) Other conditions. (i) Displaced status. (a) Family was displaced. 40 (ii) Veteran or serviceman status. (a) Family of disabled veteran. 30 (b) Family of deceased veteran or serviceman. (c) Family of other veteran or serviceman. 20 10 (iii) Health conditions. (a) Chronic health condition or physical impairment present. 10 1971

URBAN RENEWAL T.17 § 22a-63 

Score (iv) Elderly status. (a) Elderly family. 10 (b) Families will be selected for admission strictly following the scoring system specified above. The highest score will be first considered among all eligible applicants for each size and composition of available dwelling units. (c) If a house vacated by a family which was "to be displaced”, becomes occupied subsequent to the relocation of such family, the new occupant of the house vacated shall not be considered as "to be displaced" even though it may be necessary to serve him an official notice to vacate. (d) Priorities: As among families which are "to be displaced" this Corporation, through its Executive Director or his designee, may from time to time extend priorities to specific groups. 

§ 22a-63. Definition of terms 

(a) (1) "Family": "Family" means: (1) a group of 2 or more persons related by blood, marriage or legal adoption, who will live regularly together in the same dwelling unit in the project; or (2) a single person 62 years of age or over or who is under a disability as defined in Section 223 of the Social Security Act¹ or is handicapped within the meaning of Section 202 of the Housing Act of 19592 or (3) a nonelderly and nonhandicapped single person 45 years of age or over, displaced from Federally-Aided Urban Renewal Project, from the site of a federally-aided low-rent housing project or Commonwealth or Municipal Public Works. There may also be considered as part of a family other persons who will live regularly as a part of the family group (including foster children and members of the family temporarily absent), and whose income and resources are available in meeting the living expenses of the group. 

The above definition of "family" does not exclude a person living 1 The term is there defined (42 U.S.C. 423 (c) (2)) as "inability to engage in any substantial gainful activity by reason of any medically determinable physical or mental impairment which can be expected to result in death or which has lasted or which can be expected to last for a continuous period of not less than 12 months". To be under a disability as defined in this section does not mean that a person must be receiving disability benefits from the Social Security Administration. 

2 A person shall be considered handicapped if such person is determined to have a physical impairment which (1) is expected to be of long continued and indefinite duration, (2) substantially impedes his ability to live independently, and (3) is of nature that such ability could be improved by more suitable housing conditions. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 2 2.85

T.§ 22a-63 Ch. 2 

HOUSING 

alone during the temporary absence of a family member who will later live regularly as part of the family. (2) "Elderly family" means: Families whose heads (or their spouses) or whose sole members are 62 years of age or over or are under a disability as defined in Section 223 of the Social Security Act or are handicapped within the meaning of Section 202 of the Housing Act of 1959. A person necessarily residing with a family by reason of employment by or for such family (a) to permit the employment of a wage earner, or (b) for the health and welfare of a sick or incapacitated member of the family need not be considered as a member of the family for the purposes of determining net family income or establishing rent. However, the necessity for such an arrangement must be evidenced by a doctor's certificate or must be deemed essential, and so certified by welfare and other responsible sources. Under no circumstances may such an arrangement be continued longer than necessary or permitted only for the convenience of the tenant or such employee. This provision is applicable both for admission and continued occupancy and is not restricted to elderly families. (b) "Head of the family": The head of the family is that member of the group who is legally or morally responsible for the family. He must be a person 21 years old or over, unless emancipated by legal marriage. The head of the family shall at all times represent the family and sign the dwelling lease, except in the case of a serviceman stationed away from the Island, in which instance, the wife shall be considered the head of the family until the return of such serviceman. HOUSING § 41-21. Family 

"Family" means a group of two or more persons related by blood, marriage, or legal adoption who will live regularly together in the same dwelling unit in the project. In addition to this group of two or more related persons, the family may include other persons (including foster children and members of the family temporarily absent) who will live regularly as part of the family group and whose income and resources are available for use in meeting the living expenses of the group. (The income of such persons must be included in determining the income of the family.) A single elderly person or group of unrelated elderly persons living together, whose ages are 65 years or over; if such persons have been displaced or are to be displaced by a Low-Rent Housing Project or 

Urban Renewal Project or a Public Slum Clearance Project.

§ 41-22. Head of a family 

The "head of a family" is that member of the group who is legally or morally responsible for the family. 

§ 41-23. Veteran 

For the purposes of applying preferences and waiving the previous housing requirements a "Veteran" means a person (man or woman) who has served in the active military or naval service of the United States at any time (1) on or after September 16, 1940 and prior to July 26, 1947, (2) on or after April 6, 1917 and prior to November 11, 1918, or (3) on or after June 27, 1950 and prior to February 1, 1955, and who has been discharged or released therefrom under conditions other than dishonorable. 

§ 41-24. Serviceman 

For the purpose of applying preferences and waiving the previous housing requirements a "serviceman" means a person (man or woman) now in the active military or naval service of the United States who has also served therein at any time (1) on or after 

September 16, 1940 and prior to July 26, 1947, (2) on or after 

April 6, 1917 and prior to November 11, 1918, or (3) on or after
