$ 41-29. Contract rent "Contract rent" means the rent charged a tenant for use of the dwelling accommodation, equipment, services, and utilities supplied by the project. Contract rent does not include charges for utilities which may be purchased by the project and sold to the tenant as a transaction separate from the payment of such rent, charges for excess utility consumption or miscellaneous charges. § 41-30. Gross rent "Gross rent" means Contract Rent plus the estimated value or cost to the tenant for reasonable amounts of utilities not included in the contract rent. § 41-31. Aggregate family income (a) "Aggregate family income" means all the income from any source whatsoever, before deductions or exemptions, anticipated to be received during the twelve months following admission or redetermination of net family income (as the case may be) by all persons including minors, actually occupying, or who are actually to occupy the dwelling, and by a family head temporarily separated from the group. (b) Aggregate family income shall include but need not be limited to: (1) The full amount, before any payroll deductions, of wages and salaries, including compensation for overtime and all other compensation for personal services (such as commissions, fees, tips, and bonuses), including the cash value of any compensation in kind (such as meals), and allowance for carfare. (2) Net income from the operation of a business or profession. Expenditures for business expansion or amortization of capital indebtedness shall not be considered in determining net income. Installment payments for a motor vehicle used as the principal means of earning a living are not amortization of capital indebtedness and shall, therefore, be considered as expenses in determining net income. (3) Interest, dividends, and net income of any kind from real or personal property. (4) The full amount received from annuities, periodic payments derived from insurance policites, retirement in-

Ch. T.17 § 41-31 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

come, pensions, periodic benefits for disability or death and other similar types of periodic receipts. (5) Payments in lieu of earnings, such as unemployment and disability compensations, social security benefits, workmen's compensation and dismissal wages, excluding however, lump-sum payments under health and accident insurance and under workmen's compensation. (6) Cash relief receipts and the value of determinable relief allowance in kind including rental allowances. (7) Periodic and determinable allowances, such as alimony and regular contributions or gifts, including amounts received from any persons not residing in the dwelling. (8) The full amount received for the care of foster children. (9) All regular pay, special payments, and allowances (such as longevity, overseas duty, rental allowances, allowances for dependents, etc.) received by a member of the armed forces who is the head of the family, whether or not he is living in the dwelling, or by any other member of the armed forces who is living in the dwelling. (10) Subsistence allowances or receipts in connection with education or training received by a former member of the armed forces who is head of the family, whether or not he is living in the dwelling or by any other former member of the armed forces who is living in the dwelling. 

Since the allowance paid to veterans receiving training under the Veteran's Readjustment Act of 1952 includes the full amount allowed for subsistence, tuition, books, fees, and other costs, there should be included in aggregate family income only the amount considered to be for subsistence. If a lump sum is received with no specific amount designated for subsistence, include in aggregate family income an amount equal to the subsistence allowance paid to veterans of World War II receiving similar training.¹ (c) The following are not to be included in aggregate family income: (1) Amounts which are specifically received for, or are a reimbursement of, the costs of illness, or medical care. (2) Casual and irregular gifts.

§ 41-32. Net family income 

(a) "Net family income" means "aggregate family income" less deductions allowed pursuant to par. (2) of subsec. (b) of this section, and anticipated during the 12-month period for which "aggregate family income" is estimated. (b) The following deductions, but no other, may be made; however, they must in any event be applied uniformly to all families: (1) Special occupational expenses necessary to employment and for which no reimbursement is made by the employer, but only to the extent by which such expenses exceed normal and usual expenses incident to employment, i.e., special tools and equipment, miner's explosives, transportation in excess of that normal to employment in the locality and meals as required by condition of employment. (2) Deductions from wages, if required by law or required by the employer as a condition of employment, such as deductions for social security, pension, retirement funds, or death benefits, or for health, accident or medical benefit plans; except as provided in (3) below. (3) Amounts paid, if reasonable and necessary, and not in excess of 10% of the net family income, for the support of a person or persons not residing with the family but for whose support one or more members of the family are legally or morally responsible; but not including expenses incurred for the support of children away from home for purposes of normal and voluntary education; provided that this 10% limitation may be increased to a maximum of 33 1/3% in justifiable cases and subject to the approval of the Executive Director or his designee. (4) Amounts paid, if reasonable, for the care of children or aged or incapacitated family members, in order to

Ch. T.17 § 41-33 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

permit employment of a sole earner to engage in a gainful occupation outside the home, provided that (A) no other member of the family is available to provide the necessary care; and (B) in no event the amount deducted is greater than the amount of income produced by the family member thus released for such occupation. (5) Predictable medical expenses for continuing illness, if determined to be proper and reasonable, in excess of 3% of the aggregate income of the family and where not specifically compensated for or covered by insurance. 

Expenses incurred must be supported by receipts or other written evidence. (6) In the case of a former member of the armed services who is the family head, who is absent from home and who is receiving allowances in connection with education or training, an amount equal to the allowance received by a former member of the armed services without dependents who is receiving the same education or training. (7) In the case of a member of the armed services who is the family head and who is stationed away from home, an amount equal to the balance of the serviceman's pay after his portion of the dependent's allowance has been deducted, but never in excess of $50 per month, to cover necessary occupational expenses. (c) In no event shall the following items be allowed as deductions: (1) Payments of income tax, including payroll deductions therefor. (2) Payments for saving bonds, or the acquisition of other assets, including payroll deductions therefor. (3) Payroll deductions for pensions or other purposes not required by law or by the employer as a condition of employment. (4) Payments on or garnishments for installment purchases, repayment of loans, or interest and finance charges on such items. (5) Any other items not specifically enumerated in subsection (b) of this section. 

§ 41-33. Initial operating period 

"Initial operating period" with respect to each project shall

T.§ 41-33 Ch. 3 

HOUSING 

mean the period commencing with the date of initiation of such project and ending with either (1) the end of the calendar quarter in which ninety-five per cent of the dwelling units in such project are occupied, or (2) the end of the calendar quarter which is six, seven, or eight months after the date of full availability of such project, or (3) the end of the calendar quarter next preceding the date of physical completion of such project, whichever is the earlier.

§ 41-81. Eligibility for admission 

There are to be eligible for admission to PHA-aided low-rent housing projects operated by this Authority only those applicants who, at the time of admission, meet all the following requirements: (1) Who qualify as a family (see section 41-21 of this title). (2) Whose Net Family Income, less (A) an exemption of $100 for each minor member of the family other than the head of the family and his spouse, does not exceed the applicable income limits for admission set forth in Exhibit I, section 41-221 of this title, provided, however: (i) that the net family income for rent determination does not exceed that shown in the Schedules of Dwelling Rents for the $33.00 Contract Rent, and (ii) that in Projects PR-3-1, 3-2, 3-3, 3-4, 3-5, 3-6, 3-7, 3-8, 3-10, and 3-12, where a ceiling rent of $24.00 Contract Rent has been established, the net income for rent determination does not exceed that shown in the Schedules of Dwelling Rents for such ceiling rent, and (B) an exemption of all amounts paid by the U.S. Government for disability or death occurring in connection with military 10

41-221 of this title. (3) Whose net family assets do not exceed $2,000 except, that in the case of families evicted or forced to vacate to give way to a public improvement or redevelopment project; such assets, including the indemnity received for the demolished property, shall not exceed $3,500; provided that the Executive Director or his designee may waive the maximum asset limitations on a case to case basis in extraordinary circumstances and with consideration given to the type of assets and the cash income the family is receiving. (4) Who, except for the family of any veteran or serviceman or of any deceased veteran or serviceman (see sec. 41-25 of this title) applying for admission not later than March 1, 1959 are: (A) living in unsafe, insanitary or overcrowded dwellings (see section 41-84 of this title), or; (B) displaced: (i) by another low-rent housing project or by any public slum clearance, redevelopment, or urban renewal project; or (ii) through action of a public body or court either through the enforcement of housing standards or through the demolition, closing, or the improvement of a dwelling unit or units; or (iii) who are required to move because they cannot afford the increased rent caused by improvement of a dwelling unit to bring it into compliance with housing standards prescribed by laws or codes; or (C) actually without housing due to cause other than the fault of the tenant (see sections 41-85 and 41-86 of this title); or (D) about to be without housing as the result of a court order of the eviction due to causes other than the fault of the tenant (see sections 41-86 and 41-87 of this title). (5) Who conform to the occupancy standards set forth in sections 41-131 to 41-135 of this title. (6) Who by reason of the moral conduct, past or present, of any member of the family, do not constitute a severe hazard to the moral standing of the project. § 41-82. Eligibility for continued occupancy 

There are to be eligible for continued occupancy in all PHA-aided housing projects operated by this Authority only those occupants who at the time of reexamination (or at any time in the case of paragraph (6) of this section) meet all the following requirements: (1) Who qualify as a family (see section 41-21 of this title), except that a person or persons remaining as the residuum of a family shall be permitted to remain in occupancy. If an addi- 12

tion, related to the residuum by blood, marriage, or adoption, is made to a residuum household, and the new group qualifies as a family, it shall be so considered.

The lessee of a residuum household may be allowed to bring an unrelated person into the dwelling, subject to the approval of the Executive Director or his designee, and provided that: (A) The new household qualifies for continued occupancy in every respect except as a family; (B) A larger dwelling is not required to accommodate the enlarged household; and (C) It is understood that the person so admitted will not be permitted to continue in occupancy if the residuum is removed from or leaves the household for any reason. T.§ 41-83 Ch. 3 

HOUSING § 41-83. Maximum income limits 

Maximum income limits for admission and continued occupancy are set forth in Exhibit I, section 41-221 of this title. No minimum income limits are established. § 41-84. Housing conditions prior to admission 

(a) The Puerto Rico Housing Authority considers the existence of any of the following conditions an adequate basis for determining that a dwelling is unsafe, insanitary, or overcrowded. (1) Location. The location of the unit is such that it creates a health, fire, or safety hazard for the occupants of such dwelling unit. (2) Condition of structure. The condition of the structure is such as to create serious safety or health hazards by reason of structural deficiencies or of continuous dampness or exposure, brought about by neglect or dilapidation. (3) Water supply. Lack of potable water within the dwelling unit. (4) Sewerage system. No connection between plumbing fixtures and adequate sewage disposal system. (5) Toilet facilities. No flush toilet in the dwelling unit, or if present, unfit for use. (6) Bath facilities. No bathtub or shower in the dwelling unit, or, if present, unfit for use. (7) Kitchen facilities. Lack of permanent, safe, and reasonably efficient kitchen facilities within the dwelling unit including sink with running water and provisions for cooking stove. (8) Lighting facilities. Dwelling not wired or inadequately wired for electric lighting. (9) Light and ventilation. Living room, bedroom, or kitchen with no windows, or with windows opening on an airshaft, or toilet or bathrooms without adequate ventilation. (10) Overcrowded. The number of persons occupying a dwelling unit exceeds the maximum occupancy limits established (see sections 41-131 to 41-135 of this title) or when two or more families are occupying a dwelling unit designed for single-family occupancy. 14

Ch. T.17 § 41-87 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

(b) Attached as Exhibit VII, section 41-102 of this title, is a score sheet to be used by the staff of this Authority in evaluating the physical housing conditions of families found to be living in unsafe, insanitary, or overcrowded dwellings. § 41-85. Without housing without fault

Families will be considered to be actually without housing when living under any of the following circumstances: (1) A family is temporarily sheltered through the benevolence of some interested agency or individual, solely for the purpose of protecting it from the elements while seeking housing accommodations. (2) Family members are involuntarily living apart from each other as separate entities without ready access to each other or to any facilities necessary to family life. (3) Families whose place of abode is not within reasonable commuting distance of the family head's place of employment. "Not within reasonable commuting distance", as used here, means that the family's residence is so located as to make it impossible for the family head to commute daily to his place of work, or the cost or time involved in commuting is substantially in excess of that which is considered normal and usual. § 41-86. Causes other than fault of tenant

Being without housing for willful or deliberate failure to pay rent or to carry out other normal obligations of tenancy is not to be interpreted as due to causes other than the fault of the tenant. 

However, if a substantial reduction in a family's income, or an increase in rent beyond its reasonable ability to pay, has resulted in loss of accommodations, the applicant may qualify under this provision. 

§ 41-87. Eviction 

The mere prospect of eviction is not sufficient to qualify a family for admission on the basis that it is about to be without housing. 

A court order of eviction must actually have been received by the family and it must have been issued for causes not construed to be the fault of the tenant. 15

§ 41-101. Order of preference 

In selecting tenants from among eligible applicant families of the size and composition appropriate to available dwelling units, the following order of preferences shall be applied within each of the ranges of specified rents as established by Exhibit II, section 41-222 of this title, titled Ranges of Specified Rents and Dis tribution of Units Thereto (see Exhibit IV, section 41-230 of this title). (1) First preference shall be given to families which are to be displaced by any low rent housing project or by any public slum clearance, redevelopment, or urban renewal project, or through action of a public body or court, either through the enforcement of housing standards or through the demolition, closing, or improvement of dwelling units, or which were so displaced within three years prior to making application for admission. This first preference is applicable also to families required to move because they cannot afford the increased rent caused by improvement of a dwelling unit to bring it into compliance with housing standards prescribed by laws or codes; Provided that as among such projects. or actions, the Authority through its Executive Director, may from time to time extend a prior preference or preferences. Among families within any such preference group, priority shall be given as follows: 

(A) families of disabled veterans whose disability has been determined by the Veterans' Administration to be serviceconnected; (B) families of deceased veterans and servicement whose death has been determined by the Veterans' Administration to be service-connected; (C) families of other veterans and servicemen; (D) other families. (2) Second preference shall be given to families of veterans and servicemen not qualifying as displaced families as in paragraph (1) of this section. Among such families priority will be given as follows: 16

Ch. 3

T.17 § 41-103 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

(A) families of disabled veterans whose disability has been determined by the Veterans Administration to be serviceconnected; (B) families of deceased veterans and servicemen whose death has been determined by the Veterans Administration to be service-connected. (3) Within each of the preference groups set forth in paragraphs (1) and (2) of this section, and as among other eligible applicant families, in selecting families for admission until the end of the initial operating period preference is to be given to families having the most urgent housing need, determined in accordance with the provisions of section 41-102 of this title. In selecting tenants for admission after the end of the initial operating period, consideration is to be given to the date of application as well as to the urgency of the family's housing need. (4) As among eligible families, within each preference group, first consideration shall be given to families residing in the urban zone. (5) In the event a house vacated by a family entitled to preference pursuant to paragraph (1) of this section above, becomes occupied subsequent to its having been vacated by the displaced family, the new occupant shall not also be entitled to preference even though it may become necessary to serve him with an official notice to vacate.

against families, otherwise eligible for admission, because their incomes are derived in whole or in part from public assistance. 

No quotas or other devices, except as necessitated by allocation of units to ranges of specified rents, are to be established to limit the number of tenants receiving public assistance. 

§ 41-104. Transfer of tenants 

A transfer of a family within a low-rent project or transfer to such a project from any other PHA-aided or Commonwealth project operated by this Authority, when such family is eligible for continued occupancy in the dwelling to which it is transferred, shall not for any purpose be deemed to be an admission to the project and shall not be subject to the preferences established by law.

Transfers of tenants from a project in one municipality to a project in another municipality, both operated by this Authority, shall be limited to an agreement of interchange between two tenants, except that this limitation may be waived in the following circumstances: (1) When a tenant is being transferred from one project to another in a different municipality, but both in the San Juan 

Metropolitan Area. 

(2) When the transfer of the tenant will result in benefit to the project to which he is transferred, on account of the services he can render to the Authority. (3) When such a transfer enables an eligible family displaced by a public slum clearance or redevelopment project in the area of operation of this Authority to move into the project. (4) When necessary to reach or maintain full occupancy and/or the financial solvency of the project to which the tenant is being transferred. 

Tenants being transferred within a project or to another project in the same or in a different municipality, at their request and for their own benefit shall be charged a fee of $5.00 for the additional cost to the Authority. This amount of $5.00 is payable at the time the transfer is executed.

No tenant in debt with this Authority shall be transferred until he has paid in full.

The approval of any transfer is subject to there being available a dwelling unit of appropriate size in the project to which the tenant is being transferred. 18

Ch. T.17 § 41-131 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

This Authority shall not admit on a transfer basis the tenant of a project operated by another Local Authority. Such an action would result in the admission of a new tenant and, therefore, all the conditions governing eligibility for admission must be met. 

SECTIONS DIVISION 5. RENTS 

41-121. Schedule of dwelling rents 41-122. 

Minimum rents 

41-123. Welfare rents 

§ 41-121. Schedule of dwelling rents 

Tenants of this Authority are to be charged rents in accordance with the schedules of dwelling rents attached as Exhibit III-A through Exhibit III-G, sections 41-223 to 41-229 of this title. § 41-122. Minimum rents

The minimum gross rent to be charged any tenant regardless of how low his income may be, is to be the minimum rent shown in the applicable schedule of dwelling rents; provided that in Projects PR 3-7, 3-8, 3-10, 3-11, and 3-14, no rental increase shall be made to families being charged now a $2.50 contract rent, unless their annual net family income changes to exceed the highest net family income that had been established for such rent in the schedule of dwelling rents previously in effect. 

§ 41-123. Welfare rents 

Rents charged families dependent in whole or in part on public assistance shall be the same as the rents charged other families with the same income.

To avoid overcrowding and prevent waste of space, dwellings are to be assigned in accordance with the occupancy standards set forth below. Where it is found that the size of the dwelling is no longer suitable for the family in accordance with these stand- 19

Maximum 23379 34 55 36801 11 The above limits may be increased by administrative determination of the Executive Director or his designee, but only in individual and urgent cases of families who are to be displaced from a slum clearance and redevelopment project, but in no event shall such increase permit occupancy in excess of three persons per bedroom. One person, the residuum or a tenant family, is to be permitted to occupy the smallest size unit in the project. § 41-132. Factors to be considered

In assigning dwellings to families consideration shall be given to the age, sex, and relationship of the members of the family and other factors, such as, health and disability. Dwellings shall be so assigned that it will not be necessary for persons of opposite sex, over six years of age, other than husband and wife, to occupy the same bedroom. 

§ 41-133. Living room as bedroom 

Dwellings shall also be assigned as not to require use of the living room for sleeping purposes, except for one-bedroom units. 

§ 41-134. Children 

In applying the above standards, every member of the family, regardless of age, shall be considered a person.

(a) Admission. Families whose size is in excess of the maximum number of persons established for a dwelling unit may be permitted to occupy two units (preferably contiguous) provided such units contain no more rooms than necessary to accommodate ¹A 2-BR unit may be assigned to a two-person family for reasons of health and disability.

(c) Rental charges for multi-unit occupancy. The rent for a family occupying more than one unit shall be related to its net family income and not to the number of units occupied. 

SECTIONS DIVISION 7. RECEIPT OF APPLICATION AND DETERMINATION OF ELIGIBILITY

§ 41-151. Steps in determining eligibility 

This division sets forth the basic steps which are to be taken in obtaining and verifying data for the purpose of (1) determining whether applicants meet the conditions of eligibility for admission set forth in section 41-81 of this title; (2) applying the preference requirements covered in section 41101 of this title; (3) determining the rent to be charged families admitted in accordance with section 41-121 of this title; and, (4) the size of dwelling required in accordance with sections 

41-131 to 41-135 of this title. 

§ 41-152. Application for admission 

The application for admission constitutes the basic form of permanent record to be established for each family from which an application for admission is accepted. To assure compliance with the preference requirements of section 41-101 of this title, applications from all persons seeking admission to a project are, 21

T.§ 41-152 

Ch. 3

HOUSING 

until the end of the initial operating period, to be accepted regardless of the number of eligible applications on file; except that, if the number and type of applications received is such as to indicate that tenants will be selected only from those groups having a preference priority (see section 41-101), applications from families without such preference priority are to be discontinued. If, after the end of the initial operating period, there are sufficient applications on file from families with a preference priority, or from non-preference families having a substantial housing need to fill vacancies as they occur, additional applications from families without a preference priority are not to be taken. In any event, a pool of eligible applications shall be maintained to the extent possible and as necessary to assure full occupancy of the projects at all times. 

§ 41-153. Procedure governing receipt of applications 

For each family applying for admission there shall be obtained and recorded on application for admission (Form No. TS-1) sufficient data and information which, when verified, will permit proper determination of and certification as to the family's eligibility for admission, its preference status, if any, the rent to be charged and the size of the dwelling required by the family. The accuracy of the information provided shall be attested to and the form signed by a responsible member of the applicant's family, perferably the family head. All entries shall be made in ink or indelible pencil, or typed in.

Corrections or changes shall be made by lining through the original item and entering the correct data. All changes shall be dated and initialed by the person recording the change. The reason and authority for making the change shall also be noted. 

If during the application interview it appears that the applicant is definitely not eligible, the applicant shall be so informed and the application classified as ineligible. Sufficient information shall be entered on the application form to establish ineligibility and the applicant's signature shall be obtained. 

§ 41-154. Verification and documentation of application data 

To substantiate determinations with respect to eligibility, preference status, dwelling size and rent to be charged and to establish the validity of the Authority's certification of a family's eligibility for admission, the representations made by the applicant family 22

Ch. T.17 § 41-155 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

in its application for admission are to be verified and all verified findings relating thereto are to be documented. 

Documentation of verified findings shall consist of, but not routinely be limited to, the following items: (1) Letters or other statements from employers and other pertinent sources giving authoritative information concerning all items and amounts of income and deductions, together with other eligibility and preference determinations; (2) Photostatic or carbon copies of documents in the applicant's possession which substantiate his statements, or a brief summary of the pertinent contents of such documents signed and dated by the staff member who viewed them; (3) Statements from self-employed persons, and from persons whose earnings are irregular, such as salesmen, taxi drivers, etc., setting forth gross receipts, itemized expenses and net income; (4) Memoranda of verification data obtained by personal interview, telephone or other means, with source, date received, and the person receiving the information clearly indicated; (5) A record of the physical inspection of the applicant's housing accommodations or other documentary evidence that the dwelling is unsafe, insanitary, or overcrowded, and that the applicant is actually living in such dwelling. This is required only when residence in insafe, insanitary, or overcrowded housing is a condition of his eligibility for admission or is necessary to determine order of preference (see sections 41-23 and 41-24 and 41-81(4) (A); (6) Proof that an applicant is, if claimed, actually without housing through no fault of his own; (7) A court order of eviction, if applicant claims that he is about to be without housing through no fault of his own; (8) Proof that an applicant is, if claimed, to be displaced under one of the circumstances cited in section 41-81 (4) (B); (9) A certificate of non-subversive activity attesting to the fact that neither the applicant, nor any member of the group to constitute his household in the project, is a member of any organization designated as subversive by the Attorney General of the United States. The certificate shall include the latest published list of organizations designated as subversive. 

§ 41-155. Summary of verified data 

(a) Verified data shall be reviewed and evaluated as received 23

T.§ 41-155 Ch. 3 

HOUSING 

in order to determine correctness, accuracy, and conclusiveness. 

Where the information received is not completely adequate in all respects, new steps shall be taken to obtain full information. If during the verification process it becomes evident that for one or more reasons an applicant is ineligible for admission, the investigation shall be discontinued and the applicant notified of his ineligibility and the reason therefor. (b) As verifications of all necessary items for each application are completed, a summary of the verified information shall be prepared on Form No. TS-8. The summary shall cover the following determinations and the basis for such determinations: (1) Eligibility of the applicant group as a family; (2) Eligibility of the family with respect to the requirement prohibiting occupancy in public housing projects to any person who is a member of an organization designated as subversive by the Attorney General of the United States; (3) Eligibility of the family with respect to income limits for admission; (4) Eligibility of the family with respect to its net assets; (5) Eligibility of the family (excluding veterans and servicemen who apply not later than March 1, 1959) with respect to housing need; (6) Eligibility of the family with respect to occupancy standards; (7) Eligibility of the family with respect to moral conduct; (8) Eligibility of the family with respect to residence in the municipality; (9) Preference status, if any, of the family; (10) Urgency of the family's need for housing; (11) Size of unit to which the family should be assigned; (12) Rent which family should pay; (13) Non-ownership of house. (See section 41-81(9).) § 41-156. Rechecking verified findings prior to admission 

Only families of low income who at the time of admission meet specified requirement shall be admitted. 

To comply with this requirement, the procedure established below must be followed by the Housing Investigator or the Housing Manager: (1) If the verified data used in determining the applicant's eligibility, preference rating, rent to be charged, and size of dwelling 24

Ch. 

T.17 § 41-171 HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

required are no more than one month old and the applicant states that no change has occurred in his status, the data will be accepted as reflecting the applicant's status at the time of admission, but if any change is reported the person in charge of the investigation must verify the change, record, and sign it. (2) If data on file are between one and three months old inquiries are to be made of the applicant, his replies recorded, and any reported changes which may affect his eligibility, preference rating, rent, and unit size, are to be reverified prior to leasing; but if after inquiry no changes are reported, the person in charge of the investigation must certify it, write the date and sign the information recorded. (3) If data on file are three or more months old, all factors are to be reverified and findings recorded.

Reverification may be handled informally by telephone or other means provided findings are properly documented, together with the name of the source of information, by whom obtained, and when.

This should, of course, be signed and dated by the personnel responsible for passing on such matters. 

§ 41-157. Certification 

As a part of the application record of each applicant determined to be eligible for admission, the tenant selector is to certify that an investigation has been made of such family and that on the basis of this investigation it has been determined that the applicant and his family meet all the conditions governing eligibility. 

DIVISION 8. OCCUPANCY OF DWELLING UNITS SECTIONS

§ 41-171. Occupancy agreement requirement 

An occupancy agreement shall be entered into between this Authority and each family which is to occupy a dwelling. 

This occupancy agreement shall be kept current at all times and shall reflect the rent being charged and the conditions governing occupancy. 25

T.§ 41-172 Ch. 3 

HOUSING § 41-172. Execution of occupancy agreement 

(a) The husband and/or wife or the person morally responsible for the family accepted as a tenant shall be required to execute an occupancy agreement prior to actual admission. One copy of the agreement is to be given to the tenant and one executed copy shall be retained in the tenant's file. (b) If, through any cause, any signer of the agreement ceases to be a member of the tenant family, the agreement shall be voided and a new one executed and signed by a remaining member of the family who can qualify as a tenant, provided the family is otherwise eligible for continued occupancy. If no member is qualified to sign a new occupancy agreement, the existing one shall be voided and the family required to vacate. (c) If a tenant family transfers to a different dwelling in the same or another low-rent project operated by this Authority, the existing occupancy agreement shall be cancelled and a new one signed by a member of the family who meets the requirements set forth above, for the dwelling into which the family is to move. (d) If at any time during the life of the occupancy agreement, a change in the tenant's status results in the need of changing or amending any provision of the agreement, or if this Authority desires to waive any provision with respect to any tenant, either (1) the existing occupancy agreement is to be cancelled and a new one executed, (2) an appropriate rider is to be prepared and made part of the existing agreement, or (3) appropriate insertions are to be made within the instrument. All copies of all occupancy agreements, and of all riders and insertions are to be dated and signed by the tenant, the management aide, or by the Housing Superintendent or his designated representative. 

§ 41-173. Cancellation of the occupancy agreement 

Cancellation of a tenant's agreement is to be in accordance with the provisions of the tenant's occupancy agreement. § 41-174. Acquainting tenants with conditions of occupancy 

Prior to or at the time of signing the occupancy agreement, assistance shall be given each applicant accepted as a tenant in understanding (1) the obligations which he and his family assume as tenants of PHA-aided low-rent housing; (2) the privileges to 26

Ch. T.17 § 41-191 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

which they are entitled; and (3) the responsibility of this Authority to its tenants and to the public in fulfilling its obligations to operate the projects in conformance with controlling legislation. 

This assistance shall be given through one or more interviews conducted by a qualified member or members of the Authority's staff. It is necessary that during the interview each tenant must receive a copy of the rules which govern the families in a housing project. 

Such interview should, among other things: (1) Summarize, within the understanding of the applicant, the purposes of the local low-rent public housing program; (2) Explain the principle of relating rent to income; (3) Acquaint the applicant with provisions of legislation which most directly affect him and his family, such as the establishment of conditions of eligibility for admission and for continued occupancy and the application of preferences in the selection of tenants; (4) Assist the applicant in understanding the provisions of the occupancy agreement, and the terminology used therein; (5) Impress upon the applicant his responsibility as a tenant for paying rent when due and advise him specifically of the Authority's regulations with respect to rent payments; (6) Inform the applicant of his responsibilities with respect to the care of his dwelling, grounds, project equipment, and other phases of tenant maintenance; (7) Provide opportunity for the applicant to present questions on matters on which he desires further explanation or clarification. (8) Lay the foundation for and encourage a cooperative tenantmanagement relationship.

§ 41-191. Periodic reexaminations 

To assure that tenancy in the projects is restricted to families 27

T.17 S41 

Ch. 3 HOUSING 

meeting the eligibility requirements for continued occupancy (set forth in section 41-82 of this title), and that such families are charged appropriate rents, the eligibility status and the net family income of each tenant family is to be periodically reexamined as set forth below. Regular periodic reexaminations will be made of each family on one of the two following bases: (1) Annually. All families receiving stable income from sources which make it possible to predetermine with a fair degree of accuracy the amount of income a family will receive in the succeeding year, shall be assigned to a group termed "Class A". The incomes of such families and their eligibility status shall be reexamined once a year.

The annual reexamination is to cover all project tenants except those who have been in residence less than six months. (2) Quarterly. Those families in the project whose incomes are unstable and not capable of being estimated with a fair degree of accuracy for a projected twelve-month period, shall be assigned to a group termed "Class B".

In addition to the regular scheduled annual reexamination, all such families shall be reexamined as to eligibility status and their income redetermined at every third, sixth, and ninth month thereafter. Such reexamination shall be as full and complete as the regular annual reexamination and subject to all actions pertaining thereto. 

Families once having been classified as "Class B" may not be switched to the "Class A" category, except immediately following a regular quarterly reexamination. Families classified as "Class

A" may be switched to "Class B" at any time. In either case a reclassification shall be made only if justified by a change in the type of income received by the family. After the tenant's eligibility status and the net family income have been determined in accordance with the above policy, such action as may be necessary is to be taken. 

§ 41-192. Reexamination procedures 

Data assembled at the time of reexamination shall be filed in the folder set up for the family at the time of its application for admission (see section 41-152 of this title). These records shall be available for audit by PHA at any time during normal business hours. 28

Ch. T.17 § 41-193 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

§ 41-193. Receipt of application for continued occupancy (a) Each tenant shall be required at the time of reexamination to submit and sign an application for continued occupancy. For each family applying for continued occupancy sufficient data and information shall be shown on this form which, when verified, will permit proper determination of and certification as to the family's eligibility for continued occupancy, the rent to be charged, and the size of dwelling required by the family. The accuracy of the information provided should be attested to, and the form signed, by a responsible member of the family, preferably the family head. 

All entries shall be made in ink or indelible pencil or typed in. 

Corrections or changes shall be made by lining through the original item and entering the correct data. All changes shall be dated and initialed by the persons recording the change. The reason and authority for making such change shall also be noted. (b) The application for continued occupancy, Form No. PRHA 

74, provides space for recording: (1) Family data including: (A) the name, relationship to family head, sex, age, and employment status of each person who is residing in the dwelling; (B) for any persons who were not members of the family group the last time the family's eligibility status was determined, the date of birth; (C) any change in the status of the family since the previous determination of eligibility, as that of a disabled, deceased or other veteran or serviceman. (In the event of any change in veteran or service status, include information such as periods of service, nature and date of discharge, date of death, and whether disability or death was service-connected.) (2) Employment and income data including: (A) total income and its source, including value, time worked, etc., of all income any member of the family may be receiving or shall receive during 12 months after the reexamination date; the employment of each member, and in case the income is obtained from the United States Government, the total of the amount paid due to incapacity or death related to the service; 29

T.§ 41-193 Ch. 3 

HOUSING 

(B) itemized amounts to be deducted in determining net family income; and (C) employment and income data for each member of the family who received income from any source during the 12 months immediately preceding the date of application. § 41-194. Verification and documentation of reexamination data (a) To substantiate determinations with respect to eligibility for continued occupancy, size of unit required, and appropriateness of rental charges and also to establish the validity for the certification of a tenant's eligibility for continued occupancy, the representations made by the tenant family in its application for continued occupancy are to be verified. Reverification of veteran or service status is not required for those members of the family concerning whom these facts have previously been verified and recorded, except in the event of any change in the status of the family since the previous determination of eligibility.

However, employment and income data are to be verified in every instance. All verified findings are to be documented and placed in the tenant's folder. The data verified cannot be more than 90 days old at the date of completion of the reexamination of the project. (b) Documentation of verified findings is to consist of, but not routinely be limited to, the following items: (1) letters or other statements from employers and other pertinent sources giving authoritative information concerning all items and amounts of income and deductions, together with other eligibility determinations; (2) photostatic or carbon copies of documents in the applicant's possession which substantiate his statements, or a brief summary of the pertinent contents of such documents signed and dated by the staff member who viewed them; (3) statements from self-employed persons, and from persons whose earnings are irregular such as salesmen, taxi drivers, etc., setting forth gross receipts, itemized expenses, and net income; (4) memoranda of verification data obtained by personal interview, telephone or other means, with source, date received, and the persons receiving the information clearly indicated. 30

As verifying data are assembled, they, together with pertinent data on file, are to be reviewed and evaluated in light of established eligibility criteria for continued occupancy. In instances of marked variance between existing records and newly verified material, the reasons for discrepancies are to be ascertained and action taken in accordance with the provisions of paragraph D below.

§ 41-196. Summary of verified data 

(a) Verification data shall be reviewed and evaluated as received for completeness, accuracy, and conclusiveness. Where the information received is not completely adequate in all respects, follow-ups or new efforts to obtain such information shall be made and carried through to conclusion. (b) As verifications of all necessary items for each application are completed, a summary of the verified information shall be prepared on the application of continued occupancy covering the following determinations and the basis for such determinations: (1) Eligibility of the tenant group as a family or as the residuum of a family; (2) Eligibility of the family with respect to the requirement prohibiting occupancy in public housing projects to any person who is a member of an organization designated as subversive by the Attorney General of the United States; (3) Eligibility of the family with respect to income limits for continued occupancy; (4) Size of dwelling required; (5) Rent which the family should pay; (6) Eligibility of the family with respect to its net assets; (7) Eligibility of the family with respect to moral conduct; and, (8) Non-ownership of house. (c) When the verified findings are at substantial variance from the data furnished by the tenant in his application for continued occupancy the tenant shall be reinterviewed and an opportunity should be given him to explain the discrepancies. 31

T.S 41-197 Ch. 3 

HOUSING § 41-197. Certification 

As a part of the record of each family reexamined, the occupancy officer or the person designated by him is to certify that an investigation has been made of said family, and that on the basis of the investigation it has been determined that the tenant and his family are eligible or are ineligible for continued occupancy. 

§ 41-198. Action required following reexamination 

Within 90 days, after the tenant has submitted all the information required of him and called for on the application for continued occupancy, he is to be informed in writing concerning: (1) Eligibility status and, if ineligible, the date by which the family must vacate; (2) Any change to be made in the rent if it is found that the rent being charged the family no longer conforms to the approved rent schedule; (3) Any change to be made in the size of dwelling occupied, if it is found that the size or composition of the family has changed so that the dwelling occupied contains a number of rooms less or greater than necessary to provide decent, safe, and sanitary accommodations for the occupants thereof, without overcrowding; and (4) Any instances of misrepresentation or non-compliance with the terms of the lease revealed through reexamination and any corrective or punitive action which is to be taken.

Each tenant found to be ineligible for reasons other than membership in organizations designated as subversive by the Attorney General of the United States, is to be issued a notice to vacate, allowing him a period of three months to move from the project. 

A tenant found to be ineligible (at time of reexamination, or at any other time) because of membership in a subversive organization, is to be issued a notice to vacate which shall allow him fifteen days to move from the project. 

Ineligible tenants who do not move voluntarily by the expiration date of their notices to vacate shall be evicted. To the extent possible the management staff is to assist ineligible tenants in locating other accommodations. "This 90-day period means the time elapsed between the date the reexamination of a project is started, and the date it is completed. 32

Ch. T.17 § 41-221 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

If the reexamination discloses that the tenant, at time of admission or at any previous reexamination made misrepresentations which resulted in his being classified as eligible when in fact he was ineligible, the tenant is to be required to vacate even though he may currently be eligible. Also, if at time of reexamination it is found that the tenant's misrepresentations have resulted in his paying a lower rent than he should have paid, he is to be required to pay the difference between the rent he has paid and what he should have paid, or in justifiable cases, such other steps as are deemed advisable, are to be taken. 

§ 41-199. Reporting and certifying to PHA 

There shall be submitted to PHA, in the form and manner prescribed by that agency, periodic reports showing the rents charged and the income, size, composition and other data relating to the eligibility of the tenant families reexamined during the period covered by such report.

Subchapter 84. Lots; Sale, Conveyance and Use

DIVISION 1. GENERAL PROVISIONS SECTIONS 84-1. Short title 

84-2. Application 

§ 84-1. Short title 

This subchapter shall be known as "Rules and Regulations for Lots".

Source. §§ 84-1 to 84-111: Regulations for sale, conveyance and use of lots located in the land and utilities projects of the 

Puerto Rico Housing Authority promulgated by the Puerto Rico Housing Authority. Filed with Secretary of State Sept. 

19, 1957; File No. 172. 

Authority. Act June 22, 1954, No. 79, p. 398, § 8; 17

L.P.R.A. § 84. 

Preamble. The regulations set out in this subchapter contained the following preamble: "To regulate the sale, conveyance and use of the lots located in the Land and Utilities 

Projects, the Puerto Rico Housing Authority resolves: 

§ 84-2. Application 

Except as otherwise expressly provided, the provisions of this subchapter shall apply to all the lots in the land and utilities projects of this authority.

§ 84-21. Requirements for eligibility 

In order to be eligible to an option for a lease with right to ownership only those applicants who meet the following requirements shall be considered: (1) Be an American citizen (2) Be over 21 years of age 56

Ch. T.17 § 84-23 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

(3) Be a "bona fide" resident of the town where the lot is located, except for the residents of the Metropolitan Area (San 

Juan, Río Piedras, Bayamón and Cantaño) which will be eligible for the projects located in any of the municipalities included in the zone. (4) Not to have been convicted of a felony or infamous crime. (5) To be a person of good moral conduct and behavior. (6) To be the head of the family. (7) Not to own at the time of the application real property valued in excess of $4,500, or an annual income (including rents, salaries, pensions or others) in excess of $3,600. (8) To be in an economic standing that will enable him to comply with the provisions of the lease agreement with right to ownership. (9) Not to own at the time of the transaction a residential lot.

The Executive Director or his designee may waive any or all the above mentioned requirements for eligibility in the case of residents of areas where urban renewal or slum clearance projects are taking place. 

§ 84-22. Payment plans 

The following payment plans are established: 

(1) A 5-year Plan (2) A 10-year Plan (3) A 15-year Plan 

( 60 months) (120 months) (180 months) (4) A 20-year Plan 

§ 84-23. Determination of monthly rent 

(240 months) The rent of the lot, including sanitary, water and electrical installations to the limits of the lot, will be determined by the Puerto 

Rico Housing Authority on the basis of the following formula: 

The total cost of the project will be distributed among the total number of square meters of the lots in the project, and the cost of each square meter will be multiplied by the number of meters which make up the lot. The product of this operation, plus interest at an annual rate of 4%, will be distributed among the number of months of the plan to which the lessee must agree according to his income, in conformity with the amortization schedule set by the Authority, so that the lessee will pay the total cost of the lot plus interest in equal monthly installments. 57

T.§ 84-23 Ch. 3 

HOUSING 

When a project is not actually completed, in order to determine the cost of its finished portion the Authority will apply the percentage of the total cost that properly belongs to that portion already completed. § 84-24. Payment of monthly rent

The lessee shall make the payment of the monthly rent within the period established in the contract in accordance with the payment plan. Nevertheless, the lessee may anticipate payment for any period of the contract not yet due; and even for the whole period agreed upon. 

§ 84-25. Extension of time 

The Authority may grant reasonable extensions of time in connection with the method and date of payments if, for justified reasons, the lessee should be temporarily unable to fulfill this obligation. If at the time of expiration of the extension so granted the 

Authority understands that the lessee is not able as yet to fulfill his contractual obligation, the contract will be resolved and written notice will be delivered to the lessee that within 30 days after receipt of that notice, he will move out surrendering to the Authority the lot object of the terms of the contract. It is provided, however, that the possibility of the lessee to convey the lease and sale of the house to a third person, prior approval of the Authority, in accordance with section 84-29 of this title, will not be affected by the aforementioned provision. 

§ 84-26. Use of lots 

(a) The lots will be dedicated exclusively for the building of structures to be inhabited by the lessee and the members of his family and in case of death by his heirs. (b) The building of structures for commercial purposes, factories or industries other than home-craft industries on residential lots is hereby forbidden. 

§ 84-27. Approval of plans 

After having obtained the lease contract to a lot under any of the payment plans, the lessee shall not be allowed to build houses on, or transfer houses to the lot, nor shall he be permitted to repair houses built on the lot until the plans for such construction 58

Ch. T.17 § 84-29 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

have been approved by the Board of Permits of the Puerto Rico 

Planning Board and the Puerto Rico Housing Authority. 

§ 84-28. Restrictive measures applying to use and construction (a) To begin the construction of a concrete or block house of a value not less than $4,000 that meets the requirements of the 

Puerto Rico Planning Board, within 180 days after the signing of the contract and to finish the same before 360 days after the construction began. (b) Structures of a temporary nature shall not be used as residences. (c) Not to build fences around the lot unless they are made of concrete or blocks of not more than two feet six inches high along all the front and at least two meters along the sides. From there on to the rear to build, in blocks or concrete, fences at a height of not more than six feet; or not to build a fence along the front, but to build one in concrete or block, not more than six feet in height along the sides toward the rear part of the lot beginning two meters from the front. 

§ 84-29. Cession of rights 

(a) The lessee will not convey his title or sublet his acquired right, directly or indirectly, by sale or lease of the house built on the leased lot, nor will he transfer, lease, mortgage or encumber his property without the prior written approval of the Authority, which will be granted only: (1) When the alleged reason for the petition is justified, to the best judgment of the Authority; and (2) if the acquirer meets the requirements for constituting himself as a lessee in accordance with the prevailing regulations governing the project in which the lot is located; provided, however, that the preceding provision shall not apply against the execution of a mortgage. 

If by reason of execution of a credit or by the judicial sale in personal action against the lessee or his heirs, the structure is transferred to a creditor or a third person who does not meet the requirements of a lessee, the contract will be resolved and the acquirer must remove the house if it is removable within 30 days from the date he acquired the legal title to it. In case of a nonremovable structure the creditor or person in possession must pay the balance of the debt on the lot. 59

T.§ 84-29 Ch. 3 

HOUSING 

(b) In no case shall this Authority grant the consent for the cession of the lease or sale of the building if the lessee has not paid all the rents due on the contract and has complied with all the conditions stipulated in this subchapter. (c) In case the original lessee sublets the property, he shall keep and execute all the obligations of his contract with the Authority. (d) In case of death of the lessee, the heirs will succeed him in all the rights and obligations of the contract, while these heirs continue as residents in the house of the former lessee. In all cases and when there are no reasons for other determinations, this Authority shall give preference to the widow and minor children of the lessee. If among the heirs there are some that constitute independent families, for which reason they are legally unable to use the house at the same time, they must arrive at an agreement to determine which of the families will succeed the former lessee in the enjoyment of his rights and of his obligations with the Authority.

If they do not comply with this requirement, the Authority reserves the right to resolve the contract. 

§ 84-30. Termination of contract 

(a) At any time before the date set for the termination of the contract, if the lessee has faithfully satisfied all the rents due, the lessee may apply to the Authority for the transfer of the fee simple title of the leased property by paying an amount of money to be determined by the Authority and which in no case will exceed the difference between the rent paid by the lesssee and the rent that he must pay for the whole period of the contract. (b) If at the expiration of the contract the lessee has satisfied the total payment of the rent established in the contract, the Authority will grant property title over the lot, with no other reserve or limitation than not to convey, sell, encumber, transfer, or in any other form dispose of the acquired lot to a third person who owns a house or lot. (c) The contract shall be terminated and rescinded outright and unilaterally by the Authority if any of the following reasons are present: (1) Observance by the tenant of scandalous or immoral conduct, or breaching in any form the peace of the neighborhood. (2) Failure to pay three consecutive monthly rental charges, 60

Ch. T.17 § 84-51 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

except in cases in which an extension of time has been granted according to section 84-25 of this title. (3) Failure to comply with any of the conditions established in the lease agreement. (4) Infringement of any rule or regulation in force in connection with the use of the leased property. (d) After the lessee receives notice of the rescission of the lease agreement he must proceed to the relinquishment of all rights upon the leased property by removing the structure if this is of a removable nature, without affecting in any form the installations and alterations made by the Authority, provided however, that if the structure is of a nonremovable nature, the defaulting lessee is under obligation to pay the balance owed on the lot. If this condition is not met within 30 days from the date of the notification the Authority will be in its right to start the necessary judicial proceedings, to reposses the property. The lessee will notify the Authority the date on which he plans to remove the structure so that the Authority may take the necessary steps and make the necessary provisions for the protection of its property. 

§ 84-31. Responsibility in case of destruction 

If the house or any structure built on the lot is destroyed by a fire or hurricane, or by any other cause or act of God the Authority will not assume any responsibility. The lessee will be granted the opportunity to build again within two years after the disaster occurs. If at the end of this two year period the lessee has not yet built a new structure the contract shall be rescinded. The amount to be reimbursed will be the total rent paid by the lessee during the period or time that the contract remained in force less the amount he would have paid as the maximum rent established for eligibility for that project for the lease of the lot without right to ownership.

of this subchapter shall apply to lease agreements without right to ownership. § 84-52. Monthly rent

The monthly rent for the lease agreement without right to ownership shall be determined on the basis of the income of the lessee.

SECTIONS DIVISION 4. CONVERSION OF CONTRACTS 

84-61. Conversion of lease agreements with right to ownership 

84-62. Conversion of contracts without right to ownership to contracts with right to ownership 

84-63. Termination of a lease contract with right to ownership 

84-64. Acquisition of fee simple title 

§ 84-61. Conversion of lease agreements with right to ownership

The lessee may at any time make the conversion of the lease agreement with right to ownership to one without right to ownership.

At the time of the conversion, the Authority shall withhold from the amount paid by the lessee the amount which the lessee would have paid for the time he has occupied the property on the basis of the maximum rent established for eligibility for that project for the lease of the lot without right to ownership. The remaining balance shall be credited to the lessee as an advanced payment of the monthly rent until it is exhausted. No moneys shall be reimbursed to the lessee. § 84-62. Conversion of contracts without right to ownership to contracts with right to ownership

The lessee may, if he so wishes, at any time make the conversion of a lease agreement without right to ownership to one with right to ownership effective on the date in which the application for such conversion is approved. In this case the lessee shall not receive credit for payments made during the time he has been using the property under lease without right to ownership. The new lease agreement with right to ownership will have the following restrictions: (1) The buyer will begin the construction not later than a year after the date of the signing of the lease agreement and the same will be finished not later than 18 months after that date. 

In case that the lessee does not comply with this condition, the Authority 62

Ch. T.17 § 84-62 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

may repossess the lot at the original price of sale deducting the cost of any expenses incurred by the Authority in the execution of the transaction. If at the time of the repossession of the lot the lessee has made any physical improvements to the lot, the Authority shall decide whether to credit him with the cost of said improvement or with the amount which said improvement may be of usefulness to the Authority. (2) The house built by the lessee of the lot shall be used as residence of the lessee and not for rental purposes. (3) The property, including its accessions, improvements or enlargements, may be mortgaged in favor of any banking institution in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico when the loan is guaranteed by the FHA or the Veterans' Administration; in favor of the Teachers' Retirement Fund, or in favor of the Government Employees' Association and/or in favor of the Government Employees' Retirement Fund. In case that any of the above mentioned mortgagees executes a mortgage over these properties, the execution proceedings by which the property has been awarded to any legal or natural person, shall have the effect of clearing the property of any and all of the restrictions stated under subdivision (4) of this section even though the number of years there mentioned has not yet elapsed. (4) With the exception of the mortgages authorized under subdivision (3) of this section it is hereby forbidden to lease, transfer, convey or mortgage the property or any part thereof without the written prior consent of the Authority, unless three years have elapsed since the property was acquired by the last owner, in which case he or his heirs may freely dispose of the property without any intervention of the Authority. (5) In cases of liquidation of a lease agreement with right to ownership for the intention of obtaining the fee simple title of the property, the restrictions established in subdivision (4) of this section will be applied in the following form: (A) When the contract has been in force for more than three years, the restrictions will continue in effect for one year after the date of the deed of conveyance. (B) When the contract has been in force for two years the restrictions will continue for two years. (C) When the contract has been in force for one year, the restrictions will continue for three years. 63

T.§ 84-62 

Ch. 3

HOUSING 

(D) When the contract has been in force for less than one year the restrictions will continue for four years. § 84-63. Termination of a lease contract with right to ownership

If the lessee wishes to terminate his contract with right to ownership his account will be liquidated by reimbursing the lessee all amounts paid including down payment, after deducting the charge for the time he has used the property on the basis of the maximum monthly rent for eligibility. 

§ 84-64. Acquisition of fee simple title 

A lessee holding a lease with right to ownership may acquire the fee simple title of the property by paying the outstanding debt. The price of the lot will be credited with all amounts paid for amortization. These amounts will be computed by charging interest at the rate of 4% on the annual balance due and crediting the total amount of rental charges paid during that same year. 

In every case the lessee must have complied with all the provisions stated in the contract.

§ 84-81. Residential lots Sales policy 

The Authority hereby establishes the procedure to be followed in the sale of residential lots located in projects of this Authority. $ 84-82. Conditions for sale 

The sale of lots will be made subject to the compliance with the following conditions: (1) The sales will be made on a cash basis or on terms. In term sales the debt will be guaranteed by a mortgage upon the lot for the balance of the debt and interest at an annual rate of 4%. 64

Ch. T.17 § 84-88 HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

(2) The purchaser must pay to the Authority the amount of $10.00 to cover administrative expenses. § 84-83. Sale of houses built on lots of the Authority to other 

persons The sale of houses by families who have lots under lease contracts to third persons is authorized under the following condi tions: 

(1) The purchaser must meet all the requirements for eligibility according to section 84-21 of this title. (2) The purchaser must buy or lease the lot from the Authority before the sale and conveyance of the house is finally authorized. (3) The vendor, in this case the original owner of the house, will pay to the Authority 1% of the sales price of the house to cover administrative and clerical expenses. 

§ 84-84. Signing of documents 

The Executive Director or his designee is hereby authorized to sign for and in behalf of the Puerto Rico Housing Authority any document or documents necessary for the sale or lease of lots. 

§ 84-85. Commercial lots - Sales policy 

Any sale of lots for commercial purposes will be made on a cash basis and through public bids, except in the case of displaced merchants with commercial premises in areas undergoing process of elimination. These cases will be considered according to their individual merits. 

§ 84-86. Auction 

The auction will be announced by advertisements placed in public places in the area where the lot is located. 

§ 84-87. Offers 

The offers will be addressed in writing to the Puerto Rico Housing Authority and will be accompanied by 10% of the amount of the offer. 

§ 84-88. 

Deposit

The successful bidder must deposit with the Authority the difference to cover the total cost of the lot, 10 days after notification of the award. In default of this condition the deposit will be for- 65

T.§ 84-88 

Ch. 3

HOUSING 

feited and the Board of Commissioners of the Authority will decide the action to be taken in connection with the lot. 

§ 84-89. 

Non-cash offers

In exceptional cases, when the conditions so justify and subject to authorization of the Executive Director, offers not on a cash basis may be accepted. 

§ 84-90. 

Offers less than cost

Offers for less than the cost of the lot will not be accepted. 

§ 84-91. Preferences 

Preference will be given, under similar conditions, to persons who own houses built on the lots, to the residents of the project, and to persons who own an establishment in an area undergoing renewal. § 84-92. 

Administrative expenses

A reasonable amount will be charged the successful bidder to cover administrative expenses incurred in the recording of the transaction.

SECTIONS DIVISION 6. DEVELOPMENTS FOR "BONA FIDE" GROUPS 

84-111. Conditions for the development of projects for "bona fide" groups § 84-111. Conditions for the development of projects for "bona fide" groups

The following conditions are established for the development of projects sponsored by the Puerto Rico Housing Authority and the Local Municipal Governments or by Cooperatives, for "bona fide" moderate income groups: (1) The Municipality or the Cooperative will select a "bona fide" group of potential candidates for the acquisition of lots. (2) Single persons living alone are excluded. (3) The families in the group must have an annual income not in excess of $4,800 and shall not own any other residential property. (4) The Municipality or the Cooperative must contribute at least, in cash and/or land, an amount not less than 50% of the total estimated cost of the project before beginning the preliminary studies of the project. The Authority will then proceed to acquire 66

Ch. T.17 § 84-111 

HOUSING AUTHORITIES 

the land if this was not contributed, beginning the preliminary studies, preparing the construction plans, and obtaining the necessary approval of the government agencies. The Authority will then proceed to the construction of the project. (5) The Authority will acknowledge in favor of the members of the group selected by the Municipality or the Cooperative a right to an option of sale to all or any of the lots. This option will be in force for one year, beginning on the date in which the Authority notifies in writing to the Municipality or the Cooperative that the Inscription Map has been approved by the Puerto Rico Plan ning Board and that the lots are available for sale. (6) Once the project is completed and the cost per square meter has been determined the Authority will proceed to the sale of lots to the members of the group selected by the Municipality, or the Cooperative. (7) From the product of the sale of the lots the Authority will recover the funds invested by it in the project and will reimburse to the municipality the funds contributed by the municipality. 

In the case of a deficit in the Project, it will be covered from the funds contributed by the municipality. In the case of a Cooperative, the amount advanced by it for the construction of the project shall constitute a fund (which shall not accrue interest), against which the Authority shall charge the price of the lots at the time of conveyance to the Cooperative itself or to any of its members. Once this fund is exhausted no lot shall be conveyed unless its price is paid in cash at the time the deed of conveyance is signed. (8) At the end of the year granted by the Authority to the group selected to exercise its right to option of sale, the Authority shall continue in possession of the lots not yet sold and shall be at liberty to sell them to any person even if this person is not a member of the group selected by the Municipality or the Cooperative under the conditions and at the price it may deem convenient. 

(9) The person who acquires Fee Simple Title of property of a lot and decides not to build, cannot transfer his right of ownership to a third person without written consent of the Authority. 

The Authority shall have discretion to grant the sale or repossess the lot reimbursing to the owner the amount paid for the lot, deducting from this amount the expenses incurred by the Authority in recording the transaction. 67

T.§ 84-111 Ch. 3 

HOUSING 

(10) The buyer cannot mortgage or in any form encumber the lot with a third person except with mortgages guaranteed by the 

FHA, or by the Veterans' Administration, Teachers' Retirement Fund, Government Employees' Retirement Fund or any other or ganization which grants loans for construction of houses, provided that said mortgage, must be to obtain a loan to finance the construction of the house. These restrictions will continue in force until a year after the use permit has been granted by the Board of Permits of the Puerto Rico Planning Board for the house built on the lot. (11) The buyer of the lot must begin the construction not later than six months after having acquired it, and must finish not later than 18 months after signing the deed of conveyance. (12) The cost of each of the houses to be built on these lots, including the cost of the lot, must not exceed $8,500. (13) The restrictions, conditions and requirements before mentioned will constitute an encumbrance on the lot and so will appear on the deed of conveyance. 68

§ 114-1. Presentation of plans to Registry 

For the purpose of being registered in the Registry of Renovation and Redevelopment Plans created by Act No. 66 of June 17, 1957 [17 L.P.R.A. § 114], all final plans for renovation or for redevelopment, or any modification or amendment thereof, upon approval by the Puerto Rico Planning Board, shall be presented, in triplicate, by the Puerto Rico Housing Authority or by the corresponding Municipal Authority, to the Section of the Property Registry of Puerto Rico in whose territorial district the property which is the object of the renovation or redevelopment may be situated, provided, that if such property should be situated in the territorial district of two or more Sections of the Registry, said plan shall be presented in similar manner to all the Sections.

§ 186-26. Definitions 

Whenever used in this subchapter, the terms hereinafter expressed shall mean: 

(1) "Administration" the Economic Stabilization Administration of Puerto Rico. 

(2) "Administrator" the Economic Stabilization Administrator of Puerto Rico. 

(3) "Landlord" and/or "owner" any owner, lessor, sublessor, administrator, natural or legal person, manager, and attorney for the purposes of the administration of one or more rental properties. (4) "Tenant" includes lessee, sublessee, and any natural or legal person living, using, or occupying one or more rental properties. (5) "Rental property" includes any building, room, apartment, and any part thereof, irrespective of its use, as well as lots used for any purpose. (6) "Rent" means lease rental or sum paid by the tenant. (7) "Contract" and "lease" includes all lease contracts and all verbal or written agreements through which the owner gives the tenant the use of a rental property or a part thereof at a fixed price. 

Vol. 4, No. 1 72

Ch. 

T.17 S 186-27 

REASONABLE RENTALS 

(8) "Dwelling" includes shelter, lodging, room, house, and building, or a part thereof used for shelter or lodging. (9) "Room" includes a rental unit which is let and which may consist of one or more spaces. (10) "Buildings used for commercial purposes" includes buildings used as private hospitals and/or clinics. (11) "Business premise" includes any premise or building used for business purposes, and offices used for commercial, industrial or governmental purposes. (12) "Rental unit" includes each of the dwelling or business premises rented separately in the same building. (13) "Constructed after Oct. 1, 1942" in addition to all buildings constructed after that date, includes any building which has suffered a substantial structural alteration, as this term is clarified under sec. 186-30 (2) (E) of this title. (14) "Hotel" and/or "rooming house" includes any establishment open for the public to provide its guests, either partially or totally, with or without profitable purposes, shelter or room with or without meals. The guests should be provided with such services and facilities as linen service, towel service, maid service, water, light, and any other service furnished by all modern hotels. (15) "Non-profitable activities" includes all those carried out by individuals or associations without profitable purposes. (16) "Cooperative activities" includes all cooperative organized associations, or those organized pursuant to the provisions of Act 

No. 291, approved April 9, 1946, as amended [5 L.P.R.A. § 881 et seq.], and Act No. 10 approved July 1, 1947 [7 L.P.R.A. § 651 

et seq.], or any other act approved or which might be approved for the organization of cooperative associations. (17) "Major capital improvements" includes any change in the property, as distinguished from ordinary repair, replacement or maintenance, which has resulted in a substantial increase in its rental value. 

§ 186-27. Exemptions 

This subchapter does not apply to the following: (1) To properties belonging to the agencies and instrumentalities of the Government of the United States of America, the Government of Puerto Rico, or the Municipal Governments of Puerto Rico; Provided, however, That these properties will be subject to
