the provisions of this subchapter, in case that the lessors sublease them to any private person. (2) To properties used as hospitals or clinics, insofar as to the relation between the person running such business and his patients. (3) To hotels and rooming houses, insofar as to the relation between the person conducting such business and his guests or tenants, or between the owner of the building and/or lot, and/or furniture and any equipment, and the person running such hotel or rooming house business. This exemption does not cover such rooming houses or hotels for the lodging of resident tenants, insofar as to the relation between the owner of the building and/or lot, and/or furniture and equipment, and the person running such hotel or rooming house business. For purposes of this section the term "resident tenant" means any person living in a hotel or rooming house uninterruptedly although his or her permanent resi-

(4) To all rental units with a rent of $200 or more per month, when the same are used for dwelling purposes, and with a rent of $400 or more per month, when used for commercial, industrial, professional, social or recreation purposes. This exemption does not cover lots. In those cases where the rents charged for dwelling and commercial units are $200 or more per month, or $400 or more per month, respectively, a study will be made by the Administration, in order to determine if such units fall within the scope of this subchapter, or are exempt from same. Should it be determined that the unit falls within the scope of this subchapter, the Administrator shall request the registration statement from the landlord, allowing him a period of 15 days to submit same. (5) To the so-called "going concerns", as defined by jurisprudence of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico. 

(6) The following rental properties are exempt from the rent regulations, but only as to the rent to be charged: (A) All buildings, the construction of which started during the year 1946, and was completed within a period of one year from the starting date of construction, unless the Administrator, for a justified reason, granted an extension which in no case would exceed one year. To qualify for this exemption the landlord must request the proper determination from this Administration. § 186-28. Filing of registrations 

Every landlord shall file with the Administration a registration statement for each unit rented, within thirty days after first renting. § 186-29. Maximum rents

The following are the maximum rents that may be collected by the landlord: (1) For rental properties constructed before October 1, 1942: (A) The rent fixed by either the Federal Rent Office, the 

Insular Rent Office, or the Economic Stabilization Administration. 

(B) The rent in effect on October 1, 1942. In commercial premises which were rented on October 1, 1942, the maximum rent will be either the rent collected on July 17, 1946, as long as this rent does not exceed 50 percent of the rent in effect on October 1, 1942, or the rent fixed thereafter. (C) The rent established by a lease or other rental agreement before October 1, 1942, which provided for a lower or higher rent after that date. (D) If the rental property was not rented on October 1, 1942, and the maximum rent of same has not been fixed, the maximum rent shall be the first rent charged. This rent shall be subject to review by this Administration as provided in sec. 186-30 (1) of this title. (2) For rental properties constructed after Oct. 1, 1962. (A) The rent fixed by either the Federal Rent Office, the 

Insular Rent Office or the Economic Stabilization Administration. 

(B) If the maximum rent has not been fixed, the first rent charged shall be the maximum rent. This rent shall be subject to review by this Administration, as provided in sec. 186-30 (2) of this title. 

Vol. 4, No. 1 75

T.§ 186-29 Ch. 9 

HOUSING 

(3) For lots wherein no structure is built: (A) The rent charged on June 19, 1964, or the first rent charged thereafter. These rents are subject to review by this 

Administration, as provided in sec. 186-30 (3) of this title. § 186-30. Criteria to be used in fixing maximum rents 

The following criteria will be used in fixing maximum rents: (1) In the case of buildings constructed before October 1, 1942.

If the rental property was not rented on October 1, 1942, the Administrator shall fix the maximum rent on the basis of the actual rent authorized to comparable properties located in similar zones, which were rented on October 1, 1942. (2) In the case of buildings constructed after October 1, 1942.

The Administrator shall fix the maximum rent on the basis of the following: (A) Cost of construction of the building, as shown by authentic evidence submitted by the landlord. In no event will the landlord be granted more than 12 percent per annum of the cost of construction of the building. In the absence of the evidence on the part of the landlord as to the cost of construction of the building, the Administration will prepare, under acceptable assessment principles, an estimate of such cost, which will be attached to the case. The procedure in connection with this assessment is explained hereafter. (B) Cost of the lot as evidenced from the purchase deed in favor of the person who constructed or for whom the building was made, or the cost for the purposes of taxation, raised to 100 percent, whichever is greater. In no event will the landlord be granted in excess of 12 percent per annum of either of these costs. (C) Equipment or furniture provided to the tenant. A maximum of 18 percent per annum of the total cost thereof shall be granted. (D) Cost of the services provided to the tenant. (E) The fixing of a maximum rent to a rental property on the basis of a substantial structural alteration proceeds when the amount spent by the landlord in major capital improvements represents not less than 60 percent of its actual depreciated cost at the time of the alteration. (F) After consideration of the above factors, the Administrator shall notify both landlord and tenant the resulting rent, in the form of a notice of proceedings, affording each party an opportunity 

Vol. 4, No. 1 76

Ch. 9

T.17 § 186-30 REASONABLE RENTS 

to file any objection, in writing, to the proposed action, within ten days from the date of said notice. (G) Should there be no objection to the proposed rent, the maximum rent shall be fixed in accordance with the terms specified in the notice of proceedings. (H) If any objection to the notice of proceedings is filed, both landlord and tenant shall be summoned to a hearing, at which time each party is at liberty to offer the corresponding evidence in support of the objections. (I) The Administrator shall fix the maximum rent after considering all evidence in the case, as well as any further evidence submitted by either party. (J) The total rent corresponding to the structure shall be distributed among all rental units, in accordance with the regulations approved to the effect by the Administrator. (3) In the case of lots wherein no structure is built. The maximum rent of a lot wherein no structure is built shall be determined on the basis of the appraisal value of the lot for the purposes of taxation, raised to 100 percent; Provided, That in no case the maximum rent on a per annum basis shall exceed 8 percent of the cost as determined hereinbefore. (4) In lots where there is a structure belonging to an owner other than that of the lot, if the maximum rent of the lot has not been fixed, same shall be determined on the basis of the actual rents authorized to comparable lots which were rented on October 1, 1942, and which are located in similar zones. (5) When a segregation or a consolidation of rental units is effected and the maximum rents of the units before such change had been fixed on the basis of the prevailing rent for comparable units, the maximum rent for the new units created by such changes shall be fixed on the basis of the actual rents authorized to comparable units located in similar zones, which were rented on October 1, 1942. (6) If a change from a dwelling to a business use, or vice versa, occurs to a rental property which was constructed prior to October 1, 1942, and which was rented on that date, the landlord shall file a new registration statement and request that the maximum rent be fixed for the new unit created by reason of the change in use. This is also applicable in those cases where a property has been registered for a determined use before its rent has been fixed, and later its use is changed. The above does not apply to rental

properties having an established rent on the basis of construction costs.

Grounds for increase in the maximum rent (a) The landlord may request an increase in the rent of the rented property on the following grounds: (1) The rent on October 1, 1942, was materially affected by personal, or other special relationship or circumstances between the landlord and tenant, and as a result was substantially lower than the rent generally prevailing for comparable properties located in comparable zones. Upon evidence of any of the above facts, the maximum rent shall be determined as provided under sec. 186-30 (1) of this title. (2) Major capital improvements, increase in space, furniture, equipment or accessories, and increase in services, or in its cost. (A) In the case of major capital improvements or increase in space, a maximum of 12 percent per annum over the amount spent shall be allowed. (B) For furniture a maximum of 18 percent per annum over the cost of the furniture shall be allowed. (C) For equipment and accessories, the allowance shall be 18 percent per annum over the cost of same, or the rental value assigned to the equipment and accessories, whichever is greater. (3) Increase in territorial taxes. In these cases an allowance shall be granted equivalent to the increase in taxes. (b) Limitations in granting increases: (1) No increase in the maximum rent shall be authorized by reason of major capital improvements, increase in space, services, equipment, furniture or accessories, effected after June 19, 1964, unless same have been requested by the tenant, or unless the change occurred while the rental unit is vacant. It is also provided that in the case of major capital improvements for the maintenance of the property, the Administrator may authorize the increase in the rent without the consent of the tenant. (2) The existence of a lease agreement for a specific term does. not prevent the fixing or increase in the rent by the Administrator, other than the one agreed in the lease. However, the increase in the rent shall not be effective while the lease is in force. 

Vol. 4, No. 1 78

Ch. 9

T.17 § 186-33 

REASONABLE RENTS 

§ 186-32. Grounds for decrease in maximum rent (a) A tenant may request a reduction of the maximum rent on any of the following grounds: (1) For considering that the rent charged is unreasonable. (2) For substantial deterioration in the rental property. (3) When the landlord has reduced, without written consent of the tenant or without the consent of the Administrator, any service, furniture, equipment or space in the property leased. Once this reduction has been evidenced through inspection or through the holding of a hearing, the Administrator shall request the landlord to restore service, furniture, equipment or space. If the landlord does not comply with the Administrator's request, a reduction in the maximum rent shall be effected corresponding to the rental value of the service, furniture, equipment or space reduced. The reduction in rent shall be retroactive to the date of the decrease in service, furniture, equipment or space. (b) The landlord may request the Administrator to be relieved from supplying a determined service, furniture, equipment or space included in the rent. (1) Such request shall be authorized, provided that it is feasible for the tenant to provide himself the service, furniture or equipment provided by the landlord. A reduction in the maximum rent shall be effected, equivalent to the rental value of the service, furniture, or equipment. (2) No decrease in space shall be authorized unless the tenant consents to same. In this event, a reduction of the maximum rent shall be effected, in proportion to the space reduced. (c) In all cases under subsec. (b) of this section, the reduction in the rent shall be prospective. § 186-33. Duty of landlord to effect repairs (a) The landlord shall make all necessary repairs to the property rented during the period of the lease in order to maintain it in a condition suitable for the use to which it has been devoted and to maintain all its services in operation. The landlord shall not be required to effect repairs which may be necessary because of malicious damages caused by the tenant. The following rules are applicable for necessary repairs: (1) The tenant shall request, in writing, from the landlord, that he effect the necessary repairs within the period specified in 

Vol. 4, No. 1 79

T.§ 186-33 Ch. 9 

HOUSING 

the request.

Copy of such request shall be sent by the tenant to the Administration. 

(2) If the landlord fails to effect the repairs within the specified period, and after this has been duly ascertained, the Administrator shall summon the parties to a hearing which will be held in the premises, for the purpose of determining the required repairs and the cost of same. (3) The Administrator shall order the landlord to effect such repairs within a reasonable period, notifying him of the cost of the repairs. (4) If after the period granted by the Administrator, the landlord has not effected the necessary repairs, either in whole or in part, the tenant shall be authorized to effect same. If the tenant effects the repairs, the Administrator shall authorize him to deduct from the rent the amount spent, until the total amount is recovered. 

Should it be impossible for the tenant to effect the repairs, then a reduction of the monthly rent shall be made by the Administration, equivalent to 1/12 of the amount of the repairs. 

(b) Under sec. 13 of the Reasonable Rents Act [17 L.P.R.A. 

§ 203], both landlord and tenant are subject to the following responsibilities: (1) The landlord has to comply with the rules, regulations and orders issued by the Secretary of Health, the Executive Director of the Puerto Rico Water Resources Authority or their representa tives, for the protection of public health and safety as regards to rental properties. (2) The tenant has to keep up the rented property with due diligence. (3) Any landlord who violates any health law or regulation, or any orders or provision issued by the Secretary of Health for the protection of public health and safety, or who fails to effect the repairs ordered by the Secretary of Health or the Executive

Director of the Puerto Rico Water Resources Authority or their representatives, shall be subject to a misdemeanor and shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine of not less than $25 or by imprisonment for a term of not less than 10 days, or both penalties, at the discretion of the court. In case of a subsequent offense, the fine shall be from $50 to $300, or imprisonment for a term from 30 to 

90 days, or both penalties, at the discretion of the court. 

Vol. 4, No. 1 80

Ch. T.17 § 186-35 

REASONABLE RENTALS § 186-34. Prospective effect of adjustment orders, exceptions 

The determination made by the Administrator fixing, increasing or reducing the rent of a rental property will have a prospective effect, except in the following instances, when the Administrator shall issue a retroactive order requesting the refund of the overcharge: (1) When the landlord has not filed the registration statement within the 30 days period required by law, in the event that the rent collected is higher than the maximum rent fixed by the Administrator. In this instance, the refund shall be retroactive to the date of occupancy by the tenant, but in no case before June 19, 1964. (2) When the Administrator has issued an order fixing a provisional maximum rent until the case is finally decided. In this instance, the refund shall be retroactive to the date indicated in the provisional order. (3) When the landlord has reduced, without the written consent of the tenant, or without the Administrator's order, any service, furniture, equipment or space, in the rental property. In these instances, the refund shall be retroactive to the date in which such a reduction occurred. § 186-35. Overcharges, refunds, security deposits and bonds (a) Any rent collected or received by a landlord in excess of the maximum rent shall be refunded to the tenant within 30 days after being requested to do so, in writing, either by the tenant or by the Administrator. (b) In those cases where the Administrator reduces the rent including reimbursement to the tenant, the landlord shall effect such refund within the 30 days following the date of the order of reimbursement. (c) Reimbursement need not be made within the term prescribed in subsecs. (a) and (b) of this section if within said term the parties agree, or if in lieu thereof and upon petition of any of the parties the Administrator authorizes that reimbursement be made in the form of future partial payments. In those cases where the tenant continues in possession of the premises, said partial payments may be deducted from the immediate future rents. (d) If the 30 days mentioned in subsecs. (a) and (b) expire without the landlord making the reimbursement, or without the 

Vol. 4, No. 1 81

T.§ 186-35 Ch. 9 

HOUSING 

parties making the agreement mentioned in subsec. (c), the tenant may file an action against the landlord for three times the amount of the reimbursement, or for $50, whichever is greater, plus the costs and attorney's fees of the plaintiff. For the purposes of the right to file an action for a minimum of $50, all existing reimbursements owing to the tenant at the time of filing the complaint shall be considered a single cause of action, and the right to sue for a minimum of $50 for each overcharge subject to reimbursement shall not be recognized. (e) If 90 days expire counting from the date of expiration of the term fixed for the reimbursement, without the landlord making same, and without the agreement between the parties mentioned in subsec. (c), and if the tenant has not commenced the action for treble damages authorized under subsec. (d), the Administrator shall have the power to initiate such action in behalf of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. The Administrator may administratively collect the sum involved in each case, without costs or attorney's fees, and shall pay the tenant the amount of a single reimbursement, and shall pay the balance of the sum collected to the Secretary of the Treasury of Puerto Rico, to be deposited by the latter into the general funds of the public treasury. (f) If the Administrator fails to obtain from the landlord, through administrative action, the payment of the sums involved in the cause of action, within a reasonable term, which shall in no case exceed 30 days, the Administrator shall file the proper complaint in a competent court in the manner prescribed in the preceding subsec. (d). Such actions shall be filed and prosecuted free of any fees whatsoever. (g) Once the Administrator has initiated the action indicated in subsec. (e), the same shall in no way be affected by the fact that the landlord may subsequently pay directly to the tenant the amounts involved in the claim. (h) The action for treble damages authorized by this section shall be filed only within the year following the date on which the last overcharge was paid or the date on which the Administrator ordered a reduction in the rent, including reimbursement to the tenant, as the case may be. The claim for treble damages authorized by this section shall be limited to rents accrued and paid after the effective date of this Law. Any landlord who demands, requires, requests, receives or accepts from the tenant any sum in the form of a cash bond, or the constitution of a deposit of money, to 

Vol. 4, No. 1 82

Ch. T.17 § 186-38 

REASONABLE RENTALS 

guarantee the payment of the agreed rent, or who obtains payment thereof in advance shall credit the tenant monthly with interest at the rate of 4 percent per annum of the amount of said bond, deposit, or advance payment when it exceeds the rent of 2 months. 

The interest shall be computed over the total amount of the bond, deposit, or advance payment. When paying the rent, the tenant may deduct the earned interest. 

§ 186-36. Penalties 

Any landlord who charges a rent higher than the maximum rent or who charges a tenant a surcharge or commission in addition to the maximum rent, or who violates any provision of this subchapter, or any order, ruling or provision of the Administrator, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine of not less than $25 or by imprisonment for a term of not less than 10 days, or by both penalties, in the discretion of the court. In case of a subsequent offense, the fine shall be from $50 to $500 or imprisonment for a term of from 30 to 90 days, or both penalties, at the discretion of the court. 

§ 186-37. Reconsideration hearings 

The Administrator shall not make any final determination as to reduction, increase, or fixing of a maximum rent, or neither shall he deny any petition for adjustment of rent, unless the parties affected have been notified of the proposed action. This proposal may be objected to by either party and upon request of a hearing from either one the Administrator shall hold same before making his final determination. The procedure to be followed in connection with these hearings is outlined in the Rules and Procedures of the Administration, approved May 1, 1955.

§ 503-2. Functions of Director 

In addition to the faculties conferred by Law, he shall: (1) Issue or revoke, depending on the particular case, the license granted to developers and builders. (2) Issue the orders and notices authorized by Law. (3) Ascertain that the Option Contracts and Contracts of Purchase and Sale of Housing, executed between the parties, comply with the provisions of the Law. Accordingly, any developer or builder who has obtained a license under the provisions of the Law and this subchapter shall submit to the Director of the Consumers Services Administration, within the first 5 days of each month, a list of all Option Contracts and Contracts of Purchase and Sale ex ecuted during the previous month. (4) Intervene in the proceedings leading to the dissolution, transfer or change in the control of corporations engaged in the business of development or construction, in order to ascertain that they comply with the responsibilities required by Law. To this effect, any corporation holding a license under the provisions of the Law and this subchapter must notify the Director of any agreement or determination, be it in preliminary or final form, leading to the dissolution, bankruptcy, transfer or change in the control of the corporation, even if such determination has not been officially notified to the 

State Department. 

(5) Keep the following records: (A) Registry of developers or builders to whom any type of license has been issued. 1969

4(k) of the Law [17 L.P.R.A. § 504 (k)]. 

§ 503-3. Licenses-Requirements 

Any developer or builder shall obtain from the Director a license which will enable him to engage in the development or construction of housing in Puerto Rico, and which will be renewable every 2 years, if temporary, and every 3 years in the case of a regular license. To this effect, he shall file an application under oath in which he complies with the provisions of sec. 6 of the Law [17 L.P.R.A. § 506]. In cases where the applicant is not an authorized engineer or architect with a license to practice in Puerto Rico, he shall state in his application that he has obtained the services of an engineer or architect licensed by the Board of Engineers and Architects of 

Puerto Rico. 

This application shall be submitted in triplicate to the Office of the Director at least 30 days before presenting any documents related to the urbanization projects which are submitted to the Puerto Rico Planning Board or any government agency. It shall contain, in addition, a certificate to the effect that he is aware of the provisions of the Law.

The existence of the license shall be evident on every document submitted to the aforementioned government agencies. 

The application shall be accompanied by a postal money order or certified check issued to the Secretary of the Treasury. Once the

Director has made the necessary investigations he shall proceed to issue said license, which shall bear the official seal of the Consumers 

Services Administration. 

This license shall be displayed in a conspicuous place to the public. 

Any developer or builder who has not had previous experience in Puerto Rico in the construction of housing may file the application described in this section, requesting a temporary license. The license issued will expire 2 years after date of issuance. In case that a renewal of this type of license is requested, the Director shall determine, before it is issued, if the original project or urbanization 1969 

Vol. 8, No. 4 82.5

T.§ 503-3 Ch. 17 

HOUSING 

for which it was issued had been completed or is pending completion. If completed, a regular or temporary license may be issued, as determined by the Director. If the original project or urbanization for which the license was requested has not been completed, any renewals issued shall be temporary until the project or urbanization has been completely finished. § 503-4. Restrictions

Any license, whether regular or temporary, issued to a developer or builder shall not be transferable. When it has been issued to a legal person, any changes in the control of same shall be notified to the Director within 30 days following the change.

Any developer or builder holding a license under the provisions of this subchapter, who requires a renewal of such license, shall file an application for renewal in the Administration within 30 days prior to the expiration date of the former license. 

§ 503-5. Fees for issuance 

Fees for the issuance of licenses herein authorized shall be $75 for the regular license and $50 for the temporary license, payable in the manner described in sec. 503-3 of this title. Provided that in case of change in the type of license issued the applicant shall be entitled to reimbursement for the period during which the former license was not used. § 503-6. Revocation

When the Director, after giving due notice and after holding an administrative hearing, determines that a developer or builder holding a license under the provisions of the Law and this subchapter has incurred in any of the actions or omissions set forth in sec. 7 of the Law, as amended [17 L.P.R.A. § 507], he may revoke said license by issuing an order to that effect. Said revocation of license shall be published by the Director in a newspaper of general circulation. § 503-7. § 503-9. Requirements for valid Option Contracts and Contracts of Purchase and Sale Any Option Contract or Contract of Purchase and Sale, copy of which shall be sent to the Office of the Director, as a model, shall comply with each and every requirement imposed by sec. 10 of the 

Law, as amended [17 L.P.R.A. § 510], so that same may be accepted as a valid contract under the provisions of the Law and this subchapter. In addition, it shall contain a clause which clearly describes the sight of slopes, transformers, compact fill or any other irregularity not clearly contemplated in the plan. 

Any developer or builder who executes a contract in violation of the provisions stated herein shall be subject to an administrative fine which shall not be less than $100 nor more than $500. 

§ 503-10. Penalties 

Any developer or builder bound under the provisions of the Law and this subchapter to obtain a license to engage in the construction of private housing in Puerto Rico, who should engage in such activity without said license, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be subject to the penalties imposed by sec. 18 of the Law 

[17 L.P.R.A. § 518]. 

Any violation to the provisions contained in this subchapter or to any order or resolution issued by the Director, shall be punished by an administrative fine of not less than $100 nor more than $1,000, after a hearing and other proceedings required by Law have been complied with.

The officials of the Department of Education shall not carry on correspondence as to educational matters with the chiefs of the departments of the Government of Puerto Rico, with the exception of the Secretary of Education.  § 31-4. Persons residing in United States 

No official of the Department of Education shall directly communicate on official matters with persons residing in the United States. The letters received from the United States pending answer shall be referred to the Secretary of Education. Whenever it is necessary to send a message to the United States, the officials of the Department of Education shall solicit their transmission from the Secretary.

DIVISION 2. GENERAL DUTIES OF PRINCIPALS, DIRECTORS, AND TEACHERS SECTIONS 

31-41. Principals or directors 

31-42. Teachers 

§ 31-41. Principals or directors (a) The principals or directors shall fulfill the following duties: 

(1) They shall be in their respective buildings at least 20 minutes before the beginning of each session. (2) They shall keep a register of the daily attendance of the professors under their direction, from whom they shall require the signing of their names in said books, on arriving at the school, writing down the exact hour of their arrival. The principals shall also sign said register twice, at the hour of their arrival and 10 minutes before the start of each session. (3) They shall be responsible to the Secretary of Education or to his representatives, for the organization, discipline and distribution of time in their schools; and to the school director for the care of the building and of all the public property, while under their immediate responsibility and custody. (4) They shall help the school superintendents in the distribution of books and materials provided by the department. (5) They shall see to the good order and cleanliness of the buildings under their supervision. (6) They shall enroll and classify the students of the schools under their supervision. (7) They shall hear all the suggestions and criticism offered by the school superintendent, and shall keep all the books in which they have written down their work plans, and at the end of the school year they shall file them in the office for future reference. (8) They shall see that the schools under their direction are 88

Ch. T.18 § 31-41 

open at a determined hour, and that all the teachers dedicate themselves exclusively to the instruction of their students during class hours, and that good discipline shall be kept, conducting themselves with propriety and faithfully following the plan of studies prescribed by the Secretary of Education. (9) They shall not allow any person to visit the schools with the purpose of selling merchandise, or advertise books, printed matter, concerts, exhibitions or any other matter, without the written permission of the Secretary of Education. 

(10) They shall not permit the teachers or students to sell movie or theatre tickets or badges, or articles of any kind during school hours without the written permission of the Secretary of Education. Likewise they shall prevent anyone using the name and prestige of the school for non-scholastic activities. (11) They shall be responsible for the correct time of the school clocks and of their own. (12) They shall see that all the reports of the schools under their supervision are promptly filled in the proper way and are at the disposal of the school superintendents. (13) They shall be responsible for the faithful execution and fulfillment of the rules and regulations of their respective schools. (14) They shall render reports of the work, conduct, etc., of the teachers under their direction, as far as it is possible to give information on these subjects, besides attending their daily classes, if any. These reports shall be rendered to the school superintendent or to the school director, when requested. Likewise they shall have and keep in their office, in individual portfolios, the criticisms and suggestions which they have given to their teachers for the improvement of their school work, and other records required by the supervision system. (15) They shall maintain a natural discipline in all the schools under their supervision. (16) They shall render reports on the state of the school property to the school directors and to the school superintendents. (17) They shall immediately notify the school superintendent of any permission which they might have given the teacher to dismiss his students during school hours. (18) They shall be willing to comply with the additional duties which the Secretary of Education or his representatives may indicate. (b) It shall be borne in mind that whenever the word "principal" 89

T.§ 31-41 Ch. 3 

PUBLIC SCHOOLS 

or "director" is used in this Division what has been said about him shall likewise apply to the principal or to the assistant director or to the teacher in charge.

§ 31-42. Teachers The teachers shall comply with the following duties: 

(1) They shall respect the authority of the principals and shall not hinder nor usurp their duties nor their rights. (2) In the rural schools they shall be in their respective schools at least 20 minutes before the classes start. (3) Those who work in school buildings in the charge of principals, assistant principals, or teachers in charge, shall be in their respective schools at least 10 minutes before the classes start. (4) They shall keep the attendance book provided by the department, in accordance with the instructions given in said book. (5) They shall be responsible for the care and return of textbooks, and of the economical use of the materials supplied by the department. (6) They shall not close their schools during class hours, unless they are compelled to do so through absolute necessity. In such case they shall imediately notify the principal or the superintendent of the district. (7) They shall present in the proper form all the necessary reports and shall deliver them to the school superintendent. (8) They shall always follow the instructions of the Secretary of Education or of his representatives and shall become familiar with the school laws and with the rules and regulations of the department. (9) They shall carefully observe and strictly follow the teaching methods traced by the Department of Education. (10) They shall keep in their schoolrooms, to be inspected by the supervisors or other employees of the department, all the written suggestions or criticisms received from their superintendents during the year, as well as all the books in which they have written their school plans until the end of the school year. (11) When so asked by the superintendent, they shall be with 90

Ch. T.18 § 31-83 

their students in the playground, during recess, to keep order and to direct the games.

§ 31-81. Physical condition of school 

The school superintendents are strictly responsible for the physical conditions of every school. No school shall be opened unless the size of the locality in which it will be located and the equipment to be installed and used meet requirements established by the department.

It shall be the duty of the superintendents and the principals to take necessary steps to see that adequate sanitary installations are provided and that the janitors keep them scrupulously clean. 

There shall be one installation for every 20 students. 

Source. §§ 31-81 to 31-93: Rules and regulations of De partment of Education, app. by Secretary of Education, Vol.

§ 31-82. Schoolrooms and equipment for schools

The schoolrooms shall have a minimum floor space equivalent to 15 square feet per student. The equipment shall consist of 50 school desks and a teacher's desk, 2 chairs, a 4 gallon container for filtering water, a closet for books and 60 square feet of blackboard. The admission of a greater number of students than the available school desks is absolutely prohibited. 

§ 31-83. School calendar 

A school calendar shall be supplied to each superintendent so that it shall serve him as a guide in sending the reports to the 91

T.§ 31-83 Ch. 3 

department. Such reports shall be punctually rendered so that the official in charge of the statistics does not suffer unnecessary delays. Copies of the school calendar in sufficient numbers shall also be provided to the school superintendents so that they may distribute one to each teacher. 

§ 31-84. Registration 

(a) The first grade and the second grade in the schools of the urban zone shall be organized according to the interlocking system, in a uniform manner, in all the school districts. A registration of 35 students should be assured for the morning session and an equal number for the afternoon session. Also everything possible should be done to keep a registration of 70 students in each one of the interlocking schools during the year. (b) An effort should be made to complete the registration from the very first day of the school opening. To achieve this, the parents should be notified on time. Such notifications should be made through leaflets, posters, etc., which shall be made to reach every "barrio," or by placing in visible sites. The school authorities should try to obtain the cooperation of the deputies, the school committees, the police and other authorities. (c) The minimum registration accepted by the department for the rural schools is as follows: 

35 school students in one single session; 

50 school students in schools organized under the interlocking plan. (d) It shall be the duty of the superintendents to carry out a survey of the probable registration of each one of the rural schools under his jurisdiction and take the necessary steps for the closing or transfer to other "barrios" of schools with insufficient registration. (e) Under no circumstances shall children less than six years of age be admitted in the schools. (f) Not later than on the third day of class, the superintendents shall report the registration in the urban elementary and secondary schools, corresponding to each one of the municipalities of their respective districts. 

§ 31-85. Program preparation 

The general organization and the program of the schoolrooms shall be carefully prepared under the immediate direction of the 92

Ch. T.18 31-90 

superintendent. Each program shall be signed by the teacher and his immediate superior and shall be placed in a visible site in the schoolroom. 

§ 31-86. Interlockings 

The "interlockings" may be organized upon obtaining the pre vious consent of the Department of Education. 

§ 31-87. Organization sheets 

The organization sheets should be submitted, in duplicate, to the central office not later than on the day following the end of the first week of classes, including the work of the elementary and secondary schools. 

§ 31-88. Fourth year program 

The individual programs of senior high schools for the fourth year should be submitted on the same date for their approval. 

After that date no individual program shall be taken into consideration. § 31-89. "School" defined

For the purpose of this Division, the term "school" shall apply not only to schools composed of one schoolroom and employing only one teacher, but also to those of two or more schoolrooms usually (although not necessarily) installed in the same building with one director or teacher in charge. Therefore the one schoolroom rural school is "a school"; the two schoolroom rural school is also "a school"; and the second rural unit (or the urban elementary school, or the senior high school), although installed in two or more buildings, is likewise "a school". The term "school" therefore refers to a determined group of teachers and students and not to the buildings used for school purposes. When the Department requires information about said buildings, they shall be referred to as "school buildings" or "schoolhouses" and when it wishes to refer to schoolrooms they shall be called "schoolrooms". 

§31-90. Enumeration of schools 

A number shall be assigned to each elementary school, be it urban or rural, starting with the number 1 in the urban zone and with 501 in the rural and consolidated schools of each municipality. In all the reports the schools shall be designated with these numbers. The rural-urban schools shall be considered as urban. 93

T.§ 31-90 Ch. 3 

Their enumeration shall be comprised between 1 and 500 and shall in addition carry the initials UR.

No number shall be assigned to schools whose students are above the sixth grade.

These rules are also applicable to the reports on visits. During the school year the numbers shall not be duplicated nor modified. 

Whenever possible, the rural schools shall be designated with the same numbers which they have had in preceding years.

SECTIONS DIVISION 4. EMERGENCY SCHOOL SERVICE 

31-121. Free teacher service 31-122.

§ 31-121. Free teacher service

When in any town of the island there exist classrooms duly equipped but which are not being used through the lack of budgetary appropriations for additional teachers' salaries, and there are teachers not in active service who offer their services free if the use of said classrooms is granted, the acceptance of said offer is hereby authorized, and the organization of additional school groups in harmony with the following basis: (1) The service shall be known as emergency school service, and may be established in urban and rural schools. (2) The classroom, equipment and the educational material shall be provided by the school director. (3) The school superintendent is hereby authorized to provide books and school material to where the regular necessities of the school permit. (4) Only teachers with elementary license who have high school and normal course diplomas and bachelor's degrees with elementary licenses shall be accepted for the emergency school service. (5) When the number of teachers offering their services in accordance with this plan exceeds the necessary number, the selection of candidates shall be carried out, applying to the utmost the provisions of this division. (6) The teachers whose services are accepted in accordance with this plan shall obligate themselves to serve for a minimum period of one semester and shall be subject to the rules and regulations of the Department of Education as to their functions as such teachers. The appointment to a regular office relieves the teacher of his obligation in accordance with the provisions of section 31123 of this title. (7) The names of the teachers chosen for the emergency school service shall be submitted to the Secretary of Education in the official forms which are used at present for the nomination of regular teachers. (8) In no case shall the services of a teacher be accepted for one semester unless at the same time the services of another teacher are obtained for the second semester, necessary to guarantee the functioning of the school during the whole year.

The teachers included in the emergency school service shall be visited by the superintendents with the necessary frequency to assign them official classification for their work during the period served. This classification shall be valid for the purposes of appointments to regular offices and the teachers comprised in this service shall occupy the turn determined in the regulation for the selection of teachers. § 31-123. Appointment to regular service 

The emergency school service shall not be a reason for eliminating from the succession list said teachers whose services have been accepted. Therefore, these teachers may, at any time, leave the emergency service to accept regular appointments.

§ 31-141. Classification by letters 

The work of the students in all the subjects shall be classified by the system of letters. For the normal groups an "A" mark shall mean that the child's knowledge falls within the highest percentage (3-7) of the class in a certain subject. A "B" mark shall indicate the next lowest percentage (22-24). "C" shall indicate the percentage that follows in a descending order (38–50).

The majority of the class will be found within this group, the group whose work corresponds to a medium classification. "D" shall indicate inferior work as compared to the medium classification and shall include the lowest percentage (22-24) of the 98

Ch. T.18 § 31-145 

class. "D" shall be the lowest passing grade. "F" denotes failure, that means, that the work of the child corresponds to the lowest percentage (3-7) of the class.

Source. §§ 31-141 to 31-156: Rules and regulations of 

Department of Education, app. by Secretary of Education, Vol. I, pp. 24 to 29, "Classification System and Students' 

Report Cards," "Classification and Promotion of Students," and "Accumulative Report on School Progress." Filed with 

Secretary of State Sept. 28, 1957; File No. 344.

Authority. Act Mar. 12, 1903, p. 60, §§ 2, 66; 18 L.P.R.A. 

§§ 31, 32 (3 L.P.R.A. §§ 141, 142). 

§ 31-142. Intelligence classification 

When the groups have been classified on the basis of intelligence or selected on some other known basis, a different method should be used. An informative character scale is added to these rules, in which the marks are defined in terms of specific knowledge. 

§ 31-143. Report cards 

Object The main object of the report cards is to supply information to the parents on their children, which places them in the position of helping their children to succeed and as a means of developing the cooperation between the home and the school. 

§ 31-144. Contents 

The subjects reported in the cards shall correspond to the regular subjects of the curriculum. They shall be classified, as usual, by the method of normal experimentation, or particular methods, or other convenient procedure. The details inherent to the dispositions or characteristics shall also be reported. 

The blank space under the heading of "Reasons for Poor Grades" may be used by the teacher in explaining the deficiencies of the child's grades. The explanations given in this space shall guide the parents as to the help which they may give to the child in order to stimulate his progress. 

31-145. Final examination

The fact that no space has been provided on the printed report cards supplied by the department for the final yearly examination grades, does not imply that no examination shall be given. The manner of giving the examination shall be determined by the superintendent. Anyway, since the teachers carry a registry for grades, which shall be the basis for the periodical grades, it seems feasible that the grades of the final examination should be recorded in this 99

T.18 31 Ch. 3 

register or a new column might be added with this purpose to the card. 

§ 31-146. Promotions Superintendent's responsibility 

From here on, the classification and promotion of students shall be left in the hands of the school superintendent. 

§ 31-147. 

Standards Since such responsibility has been absolutely placed on the superintendents, it is hoped that in this matter they shall exercise the best judgment. Therefore, it is advisable, that through consultations with the principals and teachers, conclusive standards are adopted for the promotion of students. The number of failures in any determined group depends, naturally, on such factors as intelligence, assiduity, and regular assistance of the individuals in the classes. A group that exceeds the average intelligence, with the same conditions, should have a less amount of failures than that of another class composed of students of medium or inferior intelligence. Naturally, unless the students are specially brilliant, under the present organization, a number of failures are to be expected. Therefore, there should be a careful investigation when the whole class is promoted. § 31-148. Report on those probable 

The practice of asking the teachers to submit reports with due anticipation on probable promotions is advisable, in order that the principals and superintendents may revise the proposed plan. § 31-149. Maximum time in one grade 

No student under any circumstance should remain in the same class for over two years. For the slightest advantage that such student may derive from his promotion, shall always be greater than if he had remained another year, the third, in the same grade. 

§ 31-150. 

Report card grades

The grades awarded to the students in the report cards shall be taken into consideration in deciding his promotion. The failure of students who have received passing grades during the course of the school year has no possible explanation. 

§ 31-151. Distribution of grades 

Reasonable care should be taken in distributing the grades to 100

Ch. T.18 § 31-153 

avoid overcharging the proportion of high grades during the course of each term. § 31-152. Grades to reflect performance variations 

The grades A, B, C, D, and F shall be awarded in harmony, as much as possible, with the corresponding definition of each one. 

The grade spread is wide enough to cover the most unexpected deviations. 

§ 31-153. Promotion principles 

The following principles, taken from the work of Cubberley, "The Principal and His School", pages 366-67, may be of use in the adoption of promotion standards: (1) The judgment of the teacher should be used as much as possible in the matters of promotion, but keep in mind that not always can you confide in this judgment. If the conviction exists that the teacher might be wrong, a trial promotion should be made in order to see the results. (2) Every promotion, be it regular or of any other kind, must be approved by the principal. This is one of the important means at his disposal for the supervision of teaching. (3) All the students whom the teacher considers unquestionably prepared for their promotion, shall as usual approve the grade. (4) In all the doubtful cases consideration shall be given to the educational importance of the subjects in which deficiencies exist. The different subjects have different promotional values in the diverse grades; and the promotion conditioned to the correction of deficiencies might at times be convenient. (5) The promotion shall not be based on the results of the final tests. Instead the daily work should be considered as the principal factor. A student may obtain a low grade in a written test of one or more subjects and nevertheless, he should be promoted for his own good. (6) The ability to perform the work of the subsequent grade is more important than the approval of the finished grade. (7) Any student who on the fixed date has not been promoted has the right to appeal to the principal; and then objective tests may be given in order to settle the question. (8) Only in very special cases - never, would be the answer of many experienced principals should a student be suspended in 101

T.§ 31-153 

Ch. 3

PUBLIC SCHOOLS 

the commonly established emotional age, for reasons of bad conduct. Frequently the best remedy for indiscipline or bad conduct is a promotion in the work, that requires greater efforts. This is particularly true of children with greater ability. (9) For the students of middle intelligence one year of advanced work is of greater value than the repetition of a grade. 

The failures in school are a means for preparing the student for the failures in life. The teachers may object to a promotion, and the principal should decide what is more convenient. § 31-154. Unjustifiable promotions

The school superintendents shall be responsible for the promotions unjustifiably made. The general superintendents shall be instructed to investigate these matters in their inspection visits. § 31-155. Accumulative reports

The reports inherent to the progress of the students in the school work should be accumulative. 

An accumulative report is that which is carried in a continuous manner during the whole school history of the child. Such report shall follow the child from grade to grade and from school to school. Said report shall contain as many details as necessary in order to give the teacher a complete picture of the ability, inclinations and aptitudes of the child. 

§ 31-156. Cards 

The accumulative report may be done in the form of a card. 

The material to be used should be of sufficient durability so that it may resist the constant use during the school life of the child. 

When the school life of the child ends, the card should be sent to the office of the superintendent. In case the child should go to high school the card should follow him. In special cases, any additional detail may be added to the accumulative report. The accumulative reports shall be inspected by the officials of the department in their visits to the districts.

Source. §§ 31-171 to 31-177: Rules and regulations of

Authority. Act Mar. 12, 1903, p. 60, §§ 2, 66; 18 L.P.R.A. 

§§ 31, 32 (3 L.P.R.A. §§ 141, 142). 

§ 31-172. Rules 

The following given rules shall serve the teachers as a guide: (1) In the rural schools a child may be suspended by the teacher. 

The child should be sent to his home immediately and the parents or tutor should be notified giving the reasons for the suspension and informing them that a consent must be obtained from the superintendent before the child can return to the school. The teacher should also report the fact to the superintendent, including a copy of the letter sent to the parents. (2) In school buildings in charge of principals or assistant principals the students may only be suspended by the officials. 

The teacher shall send the student to the principal or assistant principal, who may suspend him after an investigation. In such cases the child shall be sent home immediately, notifying the parent or tutor of the suspension, the reasons for the suspension, and that in order to return to school it is necessary to obtain the consent of the superintendent. (3) After investigating the case, the superintendent shall notify the parent or tutor in writing, the conditions under which the child may return to school. (4) Copies of all the documents hereinabove mentioned shall be filed in the office of the superintendent. 

§ 31-173. Corporal punishment 

The Department of Education does not approve of corporal punishments in the public schools of Puerto Rico. This method of punishment is hereby absolutely prohibited. 103

T.§ 31-174 Ch. 3 

§ 31-174. Student strikes - Forbidden 

Any student of the public schools of Puerto Rico who believes himself a victim of some injustice should complain to his professor, and if the complaint is against his professor, assistant principal or principal, he shall address his complaint to the school superintendent of the district and if necessary an appeal may be taken of his decision to the Secretary of Education; but under no circumstance may the student leave and at the same time maintain his standing as student in said school.

The students of the public schools of Puerto Rico shall have the right to complain and to protest with due respect and decorum, of acts of their professors and principals, or assistant principals, but shall remain in the school until such complaints or protests have been investigated and settled; and while still in the school they shall conduct themselves with respect and obedience. 

§ 31-175. Attitude of department 

The Department of Education shall not acknowledge any strike or public demonstration organized by the students in order to intimidate their professors and force them to settle any difference under conditions imposed by the same students. 

The superintendents, principals, assistant principals and professors are hereby directed that under no circumstances should they come to terms with the students on strike. 

§ 31-176. 

Punishment 

Any student of the public schools of Puerto Rico who voluntarily or on behalf of another person or persons should leave school as a sign of protest or takes part in a school strike shall through his own action be removed from the public schools of Puerto Rico for an indefinite period. If a sufficient number of students take part in a strike which would disorganize the classes, the professors shall prepare themselves to take over any other tasks which the Secretary of Education may assign, but under no condition shall their salaries be subject to discounts because they have been unable to teach due to the absence of the students on strike from their classes. 

§ 31-177. Aid by school officers 

The school superintendents, principals, assistant principals and professors of the public schools who render material or moral aid to the school strikes or who knowingly readmit any student who 104

Ch. T.18 § 31-203 

has not been attending the schools which are on strike, shall be subject to dismissal.

§§ 31, 32 (3 L.P.R.A. §§ 141, 142). 

§ 31-202. 

Expense; dress

Graduations should never be given such an exaggerated importance as will cause inconveniences to the parents, especially to those who are poor, and are compelled to perform the greatest sacrifices in order to spare their children from humiliations. The school should not only contribute to this end but is obliged to avoid it. It is not necessary to dress the students as if they were to attend a wedding. A clean uniform or a simple dress if possible, made by the same students, in case of girls is sufficient for the decorum and solemnity of the act. 

§ 31-203. Political propaganda; neutrality

The public school is neutral and shall remain neutral; therefore, all the school authorities should be constantly on guard to prevent that their school grounds be invaded by party zeal and their schoolrooms converted into tribune for political propaganda. 

A great deal of care should be taken in the selection of speakers for the commencement exercises in order to avoid disagreeable consequences.

Sectarian or party propaganda of any sort is out of the question in the public schools. The commencement programs should be approved by the school authorities of each municipality, when pre- 105

T.18 31 Ch. 3 

pared in harmony with the spirit of impartiality, which unquestionably proves that the school, belonging to everyone, shall not belong to anyone in particular. If at any time a conflict should arise between the different elements that prepare and approve the commencement program, the festivities should be stopped and the awarding of diplomas should be carried out in the same normal manner as the giving of promotion cards. § 31-204. Gifts to teachers

Certain provisions should also be included in these rules on the gifts that the students bring their teachers at the end of the school year. The intention is justifiable as long as it implies an acknowledgment on the part of the student of the anxieties of the teacher who during a whole year has served as a parent, but should be abolished when used for censurable purposes. The gift is justifiable when it represents the efforts or sacrifice of the student; that is when the student has made it himself or has bought it with his own savings or by depriving himself of candies in order to give his teacher a proof of his esteem. The gift is no longer justifiable when it represents a sacrifice to the parents; and it becomes a great threat when it brings out rivalry between the students, when they compete among themselves to see who brings the teacher the most expensive gift. Therefore wherever the teachers and the students are unaware of this undesirable aspect, this custom should be abolished. 

§ 31-205. Festivities 

In the public schools all should be alike. The extravagant festivities, made through the spending of money, serve to destroy this equality, to deeply hurt the proper character of the school, to develop waste and ostentation, not in keeping with a public school of a poor country, and therefore the teachers should vigorously oppose them. 

§ 31-206. Commencement Neutrality 

The public school is neutral. In it, there is no place for the propaganda of any creed. Furthermore, no greater discourtesy may be conceived than that of inviting the parents of different political beliefs to a school activity, and compel them to hear, under the guise of a commencement speech, a long tiresome discourse, against this or that political idea. The school should not tolerate such situations which tend to deprive them of the respect from that part 106

Ch. T.18 § 31-221 

of the community aggrieved through the lack of the proper consideration. 

§ 31-207. 

Time; approval of program

The commencement exercises should be held during the day, preferably in the same school, with the assistance of the graduates, their parents and the school authorities who are, mainly the persons really interested in the school aspect of the festivities. 

Every act which shall be held under the auspices of the school shall be subject to the approval of the school authorities. The superintendents shall approve the commencement programs, since they are responsible to the Secretary of Education that the school festivities do not conflict with the school neutrality. 

SECTIONS DIVISION 8. COMMERCIAL PROPAGANDA 

31-221. Distribution of samples and commercial propaganda § 31-221. Distribution of samples and commercial propaganda (a) The distribution of samples of products of any kind and the propaganda of commercial material is absolutely prohibited in the public schools. The use of the schoolrooms by any person whose intentions are the fostering of any particular interest incompatible with the general interests of the community is also prohibited. (b) The school, which belongs to the whole community, shall be maintained neutral in all respects, commercially, politically and religiously. The distribution of illustrative sample material of any product in the school is by its own nature forcefully accompanied or followed by a particular propaganda, therefore creating a privilege in favor of a particular interest against the general interests of the community. No school propaganda permit shall be granted to any one product without granting equal privileges to its competitors. Through the use of such means the school would lose its teaching characteristics to be turned into a market place, its mission being quite different. (c) The petitions that are frequently received from commercial agencies or industrial enterprises of different classes and categories soliciting permission to distribute in the schools, through the teachers, free samples of manufactured products and of the corresponding descriptive and illustrative material shall not be permitted according to these rules, even when the petition is based 107

T.§ 31-221 Ch. 3 EDUCATION ― 

PUBLIC SCHOOLS 

on the intrinsic merits of the products and on its utility as a teaching material.

§ 46-1. Admission to examinations — Eighth grade diploma 

In order to become candidates for examination, applicants must have at least an eighth grade diploma or its equivalent. An applicant who does not fulfill this requirement must apply to the Bureau of School Extension for the corresponding examination. 

This privilege is granted only to individuals past legal school age.

Text references. The Bureau of School Extension and the 

Bureau of Free Studies and Examinations mentioned in this subchapter appear to be the same. 

Regular students

No person enrolled as a regular student in a public school may be admitted as a candidate to examinations except in special cases provided for in this title. The term "regular student" is hereby defined as meaning a public school student taking the regular school courses prescribed for his school term or year in the regular school curriculum. 

§ 46-3. Irregular students 

Irregular students may be permitted to take courses with the Bureau provided that the total number of courses, including intramural plus extramural courses, does not exceed the number of courses prescribed for the term or year in which they may be enrolled. 

§ 46-4. 

Special cases 

Regular students who have need of specific subjects but are not to take them in the regular school in which they are enrolled, because the school does not offer them, or for some other justifiable reason, may be permitted to take said subjects with the Bureau. 

§ 46-5. 

Twelfth grade students

Regular twelfth grade students who need one or two units of credit for graduation may, on the recommendation of their high school principal, be admitted to examinations on the corresponding courses; provided, such recommendation adheres to the rules of the Department of Education in respect to high school students. § 46-6. Application for admission to examinations

Individuals desiring to become candidates for examination should file formal application to the Bureau. Said application should be addressed to the Director. This application should consist of: (1) Application blank duly filled out; (2) Two passport size photographs of applicant taken not earlier than a year previous to the date of application; 109

T.§ 46-6 Ch. 3 

(3) An eighth grade diploma, or its equivalent; or (4) A certified transcript of credits of high school work in the case of students who have approved work beyond the eighth grade. 

Applicants for the eighth grade certificate should file with the Bureau their official birth certificate, the application blank duly filled out and the two photographs mentioned heretofore. 

§ 46-7. Number of subjects 

According to law any number of examinations corresponding to any number of courses in any number of terms or years may be taken by any one person. 

§ 46-8. Application dates and enrollment cards 

Applicants may file their applications at any time during the year but applicants accepted after April 30 and November 15 will not be considered candidates for the subsequent examinations, June and December examinations respectively. Such applications will be filed and the applicants will become candidates for the coming year's examinations.

Formal application is filed only once with the Bureau. After the applicant has been accepted once as a candidate for examination, admission to successive examinations may be secured through the utilization of the printed renovation blank form, indicating the examinations desired.

Candidates should state the time at which they desire to be examined.

Candidates will receive enrollment cards indicating specifically the subjects in which they may take examinations. This card should be carefully read and kept if entirely correct. If errors or omissions are noted, the card should be returned to the Bureau with pertinent remarks on it. 

§ 46-9. Acceptance of applications 

Applicants shall be notified of the results of their applications.

§ 46-10. Admission card 

(a) Some time previous to examination time, an admission card will be sent to each candidate. This card will authorize the candidate to be admitted to the examination room. (b) An admission card is valid only for such examinations as it was issued for. The subjects or courses for which examinations may be taken are specifically indicated on each card. The admis- 110

Ch. T.18 § 46-11 

sion card which contains further identification details must be presented at the entrance of the examination center and to each of the examiners as well. This card should be kept until the candidate has taken all the examinations specified therein; then turned over to the examiner. (c) Any person who deliberately alters admission cards or any other of the documents issued by the Bureau will forfeit his rights to take or continue taking examinations. The final decision in such cases will rest with the Director's judgment. 

§ 46-11. Examination dates; subjects 

Examinations for eighth grade to twelfth grade subjects will be held in June and December of each year following an examination schedule that will be published previous to examination date. 

Such examinations will cover the following courses or subjects:

 § 46-12. Place of examinations 

Examinations will be held in San Juan, Ponce and Mayagüez during the months of June and December. Candidates will be notified beforehand of any changes in the places where examinations are to be held. 

§ 46-13. Selection 

The place where a candidate is to take the examinations is assigned by the Office of the Director, but candidates may express their preferences, making a choice from the list of towns where examinations are to be held, if they so desire. Such preferences will be considered provided notice is received by the Bureau not later than 15 days previous to the date fixed for the first examination. § 46-14. Order in which examinations will be scheduled

Examinations will be scheduled in such order that it will be possible for any one candidate to take as many examinations as he desires and is officially admitted to. 

§ 46-15. Examination schedule 

Each candidate will be provided with an examination schedule. including days and hours at which examinations will be held. 

§ 46-16. Examination results 

Candidates will be directly notified of examination results. § 46-17. Music examinations

The Bureau will hold music examinations twice a year. They will adhere strictly to the information below: (1) Examinations will be held on: (A) Any musical instrument. (B) Voice (singing). (C) Solfeggio and general theory. 

(2) In the case of candidates for examinations on percussion instruments drums, cymbals, etc. special emphasis will be given to general theory and particularly solfeggio. No credit will be given on percussion instrument playing to anyone who is not able to read at first sight. (3) We do not recommend any special text or method. The candidate will be trained in accordance to his teacher guidance and 112

Ch. T.18 § 46-18 

advice, but he will be held responsible for one specific method selected among the current books which are accepted and used by competent teachers. (4) Plans for the examination will proceed as follows: 

(A) The candidate must prove reasonable mastery of general music theory terms, significance, use of symbols, nature and kind of scales, chords, kinds and use of keys, beats, etc. 

After this phase of the examination the candidate must prove his skill in music reading by reading both printed and handwritten musical exercises. In this part of the examination, special attention shall be given to intonation. A candidate failing this second part will forfeit his right to proceed with the test. (B) Practical examination. (i) Sight reading. The candidate will be required to perform at first sight, some musical work, selected according to the grade of difficulty he has attained in his studies. This musical selection will be chosen by a committee. The music will be provided by the examiner. (ii) Memory exercise. The candidate will play a classic piece corresponding to the level difficulty of the last music grade he has studied. This selection will be played from memory for the committee. The candidate will bring with him his own music, scales, exercises, etc. which correspond to the music, grade or year he is studying. Besides any other necessary material, the candidate must bring with him to the examination room all the exercise books, pieces, etc. which he has used during his period of study. (5) The maximum amount of credits in music granted will be two credit units to such candidates as evidenced having finished a complete course on their chosen instrument. Candidates who may have approved only half of said course will receive only one credit unit. (6) In order to be accepted as a candidate for examination in music, the applicant must have followed a course of study in music according to a recognized method and under the guidance of a professional in music teaching. 

§ 46-18. Credit cards 

Credit cards will be issued for all subjects approved by the candidates. 113

Ch. 3

 § 46-19. Revision of examination papers 

No application for the revision of examination papers will be considered. 

§ 46-20. Issuance and validity of diplomas 

On satisfactory completion of and approval of all the courses, subjects, etc., prescribed, candidates will be issued a high school diploma. By law, in Puerto Rico, said diploma "will be as valid as a diploma issued by the regular secondary schools of the island". 

Said diploma will be signed by the Secretary of Public Education and the Director of the Bureau. 

§ 46-21. Transfer of credits Credits granted by the Bureau of Free Studies and Examination of the Department of Education are transferable and should be accepted in full and for all legal purposes by the regular public high schools of the Department of Education and other schools under its direction. 

§ 46-22. Science notebooks 

Before credit is granted for examinations in physics, chemistry and biology, a laboratory notebook must be submitted by the candidate and accepted by the Bureau. These notebooks should be prepared in accordance with instructions proffered and should contain :

§ 46-23. 

Preparation Candidates may use any one of the methods suggested below to prepare their laboratory notebooks: (1) By making arrangements with the regular science instructors in the public high schools, working at special hours; (2) By providing their own laboratory equipment; (3) Attending special courses held during the summer. These summer courses are held to aid those candidates who have already prepared for the science courses, to complete both laboratory and theory requirements in either physics, chemistry or biology. 114

Ch. T.18 § 46-27 

Public high school laboratories 

§ 46-24. 

Candidates are permitted the use of laboratories in science and vocational courses in the public high schools, provided the high school principals authorize it. In case said authorization is refused, the subject may be submitted to the Secretary of Education for final decision. 

§ 46-25. Books, materials, etc. 

The Bureau of Free Studies and Examinations will provide free guides, courses of study and other materials for the use of the students.

The purpose of mentioning textbooks in relation to courses is to help students prepare themselves efficiently for the examinations and they will be held responsible for the work outlined in the programs of studies. The Bureau generally uses the same textbooks as the regular high schools but when the nature of the work requires it, other textbooks or references are used occasionally. 

§ 46-26. Issuance of diplomas 

Candidates who complete their high school requirements under the Bureau will be issued high school diplomas by the Bureau. 

Irregular students admitted to examination under the provisions of section 46-4 of this title will be issued high school diplomas through the schools in which they are officially enrolled. 

Rules and regulations of the Department of Education in reference to regular students in the public high schools apply to candidates taking courses with the Bureau except in such cases specially provided for by law or by this title. 

No diploma will be granted to persons who have not approved the Bureau examinations in at least one subject. § 46-27. Preparation for examinations; number of subjects; acceptance of credits

Regular students enrolled in public high schools in Puerto Rico under the direct supervision and help of their teachers, are permitted to take a maximum of five school subjects. This program is considered a difficult one; four subjects being considered enough. 

Experience has shown that those who take more than five subjects either fail or obtain unsatisfactory grades in the end. Undoubtedly, students preparing for examinations without the benefit of a teacher and the stimulus of a classroom situation must 115

T.§ 46-27 Ch. 3 

encounter great difficulties unless endowed with exceptional judgment and responsibility. Such being the case, it is undoubtedly prudent for a student doing his work alone not to try to do more and harder work than the regular student unless he considers himself mentally apt for it or has had special preparation in the corresponding subject matter.

Credit granted by regular or private secondary schools officially recognized by the Department of Education will be accepted by the Bureau.
