Letter of transmittal. Memorandum No. 7 of the director of school lunchroom division addressed to school superintendents, dated Oct. 18, 1954, provided: 

"Ladies and Gentlemen: 

"Under separate cover you will soon receive sufficient copies of the manual of procedure 'Procurement and Receipt of Products in School Districts.' 

"This manual will form part of the property of each school lunchroom, and it shall be included in the inventory receipt which each one of these feeding units has. "It is expected that the instructions contained in this manual will be thoroughly studied and assimilated by those groups concerned with the accounting that must be used in school lunchrooms. "If any doubt arises in the interpretation of these rules we invite you to submit the case to us and it will be taken care of according to the request made in that respect. "We wish to emphasize that the purpose of the instructions herein offered, as well as of the system propounded by this manual, is to canalize the accounting procedure so as to bring it in keeping with the best practices accepted by the 

Controller of Puerto Rico. 

"We suppose that each school district has already received a notebook with ruled yellow pages suitable for the accounting work. "This notebook shall be used to keep the Registry of Partial Orders, whose model is inserted in the said manual. [Section 

183-11(b) of this title]. "We wish to avail ourselves of this opportunity to enclose a sample of the letter which shall be used when seeking procurement of products in the open market [see § 183-9 of this title]. "We expect your usual cooperation toward the utmost efficiency in this aspect of the administrative work of the program in behalf of the school lunchrooms of your district."

Circular Letter No. 13 of the Secretary of Education ad dressed to school superintendents and school lunchroom supervisors, dated Aug. 25, 1954, read as follows: "Complying with the official regulation in force providing that the Government of the Commonwealth shall acquire through bids the products it may require, we are sending you herewith an account of the procedure governing the purchase of foodstuffs and supplies for the School Lunchroom Program. "The first step preparatory to establishing the said regulation must be the conscientious study thereof. “As we are moved by the desire of improving more and more this procedure, we shall be very grateful if you will consult the School Lunchroom Division on any doubt you might entertain, and at the same time, suggest your ideas for the achievement of this purpose." 

§ 183-2. Board of awards - Constituted 

The board of awards of each school district shall be composed of three public officials, to wit: the chairman, who shall be the school superintendent, or his authorized representative; a secre- 152

Ch. T.18 § 183-4 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

tary, who shall be the local school lunchroom supervisor; and a member, who may be the medical officer of the Department of Health; and an alternate, who may be the agricultural extension agent of the locality. 

§ 183-3. Duties of members 

(a) Chairman. The chairman shall convoke, preside over, and conduct the meetings of the board. The chairman shall, furthermore, see to the strict enforcement of the resolutions adopted and the procedure established. (b) Secretary. The secretary shall, on petition of the chairman, prepare and process the calls to regular and special meetings and shall be responsible for the preparation, processing, and general handling of the office work as established in this procedure. The secretary shall participate, as member of the board, in all its deliberations and decisions, prepare the minutes and keep a journal of the proceedings and resolutions. (c) Member. The member shall attend as member of the board all regular and special meetings, take part in all deliberations and decisions, and act as the orienting member thereof. 

§ 183-4. Administrative operation 

(a) The board shall hold its regular meetings as resolved and agreed upon at the first meeting of each school year. It is hereby established that the first meeting shall be held in the course of the month of July of each fiscal year. (b) The decisions of the board shall be by a majority vote and shall not take effect if they disagree or are in conflict with the procedure herein established. (c) The board shall hold its special meetings as determined by its chairman upon considering the necessity and importance of the matters to be discussed, for their inclusion in the call. (d) In the preparation and processing of the calls for bids, the following requirements shall be complied with: (1) A register shall be opened or a potential bidders' list shall be authorized in each school district. (2) Upon authorization of the chairman of the board, the secretary shall prepare the calls for bids in the form "Invitation and Offer" [§ 183-5 of this title]. There shall be included a list of the products requested (if not found in the permanent printed list), and the required conditions and specifications. Of these docu- 153

T.§ 183-4 

Ch. 11

veg- ments two copies shall be sent to each accredited bidder and the third copy shall be kept for the record of the bidding in the files. (3) Bidders shall review and analyze each item according to the conditions and specifications required and shall make their offers for the total, according to the groups in which the board may decide to classify the products to be purchased. (Example: 

1st. group bread; 2nd. group - charcoal; 3rd group etables; 4th. group - fuel). Bidders shall keep a copy of the form for their files and shall submit the other copy with their offers, duly signed and in a sealed envelope, to the office of the school superintendent, at the time fixed for the opening of bids, or sooner. Each envelope containing bids shall be sent to the office of the secretary and on the outside thereof shall be stated the number of the call for bids and the date and time for the opening thereof. (4) Bidders are free to attend at the act of the bidding and may take notes as the bids are announced aloud, and examine any proposal, if they so request. (5) Once the opening of the proposals has been completed, the secretary of the board shall prepare an abstract of the offers in the enclosed form "Abstract of Bid Offers" [§ 183-8 of this title], shall make her recommendations in accord with the lowest acceptable bids by groups or items and shall submit same to the consideration of the board.

The board reserves the right to reject or accept the offers submitted and to award the same by items, as it may best suit the interests of the Commonwealth. (6) Once the abstract of bids has been approved by the board of awards, the secretary thereof shall notify all bidders of the corresponding awards made by means of the form "Notice of Contract Award" [§ 183-7 of this title], which shall be prepared in duplicate. The Secretary shall keep the copy on file for the record of the bidding and shall send the original to the contractors for the performance of the contract upon receipt of Form No. 205, "Purchase and Receipt Orders". (7) In case no offer is received for one or various indispensable articles, the school superintendent is hereby authorized to make the purchase of said items in the open market. (8) In those cases in which the successful bidder is unable to supply, in whole or in part, the articles offered, the school 154

Ch. 11

T.18 § 183-4 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

superintendent, as chairman of the board, is hereby empowered to purchase in the open market, at the lowest prices obtainable and for the account of the contractors, the products not supplied under the contract. (9) Any difference in cost over the price and the amount which the Commonwealth must pay, shall be for the account of the contractor, and to this effect, the corresponding claim shall be made. If the bidder refuses to pay the difference in price as claimed by the board, the latter may suspend him temporarily or permanently from the list of authorized bidders. (10) If a successful bidder declares himself unable to perform his contractual obligations, the school superintendent shall ask him to submit his reasons in writing and, while the case is under study, the school superintendent is hereby empowered to purchase in the open market, that is, directly from a merchant chosen as the lowest bidder among the three or more that he may consider.

This open-market procedure shall be of an urgent nature and, to such effect, the superintendent shall use the model herein included, entitled "Open Market Offer Letter" [§ 183-9 of this title]. 

(11) If a bidder complains before the board and the latter is unable to solve the case to the satisfaction of both parties, the matter shall be submitted to the consideration of the central office of the school lunchroom division, with all necessary details to afford a clear idea of the case.

The decision of the lunchroom central office shall be final. (12) The school superintendent shall be responsible for the expeditious processing of settlement vouchers, so as to maintain the credit of the school lunchroom program.

It shall be the school superintendent's responsibility to see that the settlement vouchers processed in payment for total or partial deliveries of the products purchased conform to the contract prices and to the amounts received as shown by the Purchase and Receipt Orders Form No. 205. 

For the sake of information, the chairman of the board may explain to the bidders at the opening of the bids the conditions and specifications of the proposal. All explanations on the matter shall take place before the opening of the bids received. (13) After considering the means of supply for the lunchrooms of the district, the board of awards shall classify the lunchrooms in one or more groups, and shall form as many groups as may be necessary. 155

T.§ 183-4 Ch. 11 

Example: Lunchrooms A, B, C and D (urban zone), may form group I. Lunchrooms F, H and J (semi-urban zone or close to the urban zone) may form group II. Lunchrooms M and Z, close to each other but located in almost inaccessible rural zones, may form group III. Lunchroom N, in the farthest rural zone of the district, may form by itself group IV. 

The call for bids shall be held for each of the lunchroom groups and for each of the groups of products. 

All calls for bids may be held on the same day if the board deems it advisable, in the following manner: from 8:30 to 9:00 a.m., bids for bread for the lunchrooms of group I; from 9:00 to 

9:30 a.m., bids for vegetables for the lunchrooms of group I; from 

9:30 to 10:00 a.m., bids for fuel for the lunchrooms of group I; from 10:00 to 10:30 a.m., bids for bread for the lunchrooms of group II; from 10:30 to 11:00 a.m., bids for vegetables for the lunchrooms of group II; from 11:00 to 11:30 a.m., bids for fuel for the lunchrooms of group II; from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 M., etc.

§ 183-10. Purchase and receipt order 

(a) Instructions for its use 

(1) This document [Form No. 205] shall be prepared in quadruplicate. The copies shall be distributed as follows: (A) 

original merchant; (B) copy-person in charge; (C) person in charge; (D) local supervisor.

The second copy, duly executed, shall be returned by the person in charge to the supervisor, at the end of the school month. (2) This purchase order shall be made for a school month divided into four weeks. It shall be filled out by weeks, fortnights or months, as the school direction may deem more advisable, according to the amount of products to be purchased. (3) The other spaces shall be filled out following the directions given below. (A) If the purchases are made weekly, the spaces corresponding to the four weeks shall be filled out. (B) If the purchases are made fortnightly, the spaces corresponding to the 1st and 3rd weeks shall be filled out, leaving in blank those of the 2nd and 4th weeks. (4) The purchase order shall originate in the office of the local supervisor of school lunchrooms, but under the direction and responsibility of the school superintendent. (5) It shall include only those foodstuffs, cleaning material, etc., not supplied by the division warehouses and whose purchase is not prohibited by the regulations in force promulgated through memoranda and circular letters addressed to the school superintendents. 161

T.§ 183-10 

Ch. 11

(6) The order shall be made well in advance of the date of purchase and of the period of consumption, on the basis of the requirements disclosed by the menus prepared beforehand. (7) The requirements shall be indicated separately, according to the classification appearing from the order, in the columns for foodstuffs, cleaning material, and fuel. That is, the name of the product shall be entered in the corresponding column according to its classification. (8) A separate order for each lunchroom shall be issued monthly, but in the case of foodstuffs, said order shall be filled by weeks or fortnights and not by months. (9) Orders shall be numbered correlatively beginning with the number "one" for each merchant. (b) Instructions for executing the form: (1) Over the broken lines on the upper left corner shall be written: (A) name; (B) address of the merchant. 

(2) Over the line "Delivery Place" shall be written the name of the lunchroom to which the order belongs. (3) On the upper righthand corner, on the space "Order No. "fill in the number corresponding to this order. (4) On the space provided for the number of the voucher of the special disbursing officer shall be written the corresponding voucher numbers, inasmuch as a settlement voucher shall be made for each class of items, that is, one for foodstuffs, another for cleaning material, and another for fuel. 

(5) In "Document Number 

shall be stated the number corresponding to this form in the filing order established by the person in charge of the lunchroom. (6) Over the lines "Municipality" and "School Month" shall be written the name of the municipality and the school month to which the order corresponds. 

(7) In the column "Foodstuffs" shall be written the articles classified as such. (8) Ditto in the column "Cleaning Material". (9) Ditto in the column "Foodstuff". (10) In the column "Amount" shall be stated the amounts of the products called for. (11) In the column "Unit" shall be stated the unit, weight, or measure corresponding to the product. 162

Ch. T.18 § 183-10 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

(12) In the column "Price per Unit" shall be stated the price at which the unit, pound, etc., is being bought, according to the price agreed upon. (13) In the column "Amount Received" shall be stated the amount actually received of the product. In case the product is not received, it shall be so indicated with the word "No" in this column. This column shall be left in blank at the time of making the order. The person in charge of the lunchroom shall complete it upon receiving the product. It is essential to check up the merchandise at the time of receiving same, so as to note the exact amount received in the space provided therefor. (14) The columns "Total Cost" shall be left in blank and only in the last column at the extreme right shall be stated the total cost of the product received. (15) The column to the right, "Total Received", shall be filled out when all the products requested have been received and shall represent the sum of the amounts received. The amounts resulting from the addition of the columns "Amount Received" and which were carried over to the column "Total Received" shall be entered upon the Registry of Partial Orders, which shall be kept for the purpose and which we shall discuss later. (16) The column "Total Cost" shall be filled out with the product of the column "Total Received" multiplied by the price per unit. (17) On the lines marked "Superintendent or Local Supervisor and Date" shall be inserted the signature of either of these two officials and the date on which the order is made. (18) On the back of this form are inserted four delivery certificates and four receipt certificates. (A) If the purchases are to be delivered and received weekly, the person in charge and the principal or teacher in charge shall sign the certificates in that same form and on the corresponding date of delivery and receipt. (B) In case of fortnightly delivery and receipt, the first and third weeks shall be signed and dated upon delivery and receipt of the products, leaving in blank the second and fourth weeks. 163

T.§ 183-10 Ch. 11 

(C) No foodstuffs shall be ordered or received by monthly deliveries. (19) The amount of the purchase and receipt orders must at at all times agree with the amount of the vouchers to which they correspond. Preferment and special attention shall be given to this aspect of accounting. (20) No information whatsoever given in this purchase and receipt order shall be erased, deleted or altered. 

(c) Handling and review of form: 

(1) To avoid accounting errors, operations shall be reviewed as many times as may be necessary. Thus shall it be done, so as to prevent errors from affecting the proper distribution of funds and thus give a false impression of the state of accounts. (2) The form shall be prepared clearly, legibly, and neatly, so that any person who can read may easily interpret it. 

It shall be carefully executed and reviewed so as to make sure that no information has been omitted. (3) In ordering products sold in containers, such as powdered soap, salt, etc., it shall be necessary to specify the contents in weight and the brand of the product. (4) Once the last delivery has been received, the person in charge shall return, properly executed, to the local supervisor, one of the copies of the partial order. Once in possession of the copy of the order sent by the person in charge, the supervisor shall proceed to collate it with the copy she originally retained, afterwards destroying the latter. These documents shall then be properly arranged so that the supervisor may fill out the columns "Total Received" and "Total Cost", appearing at the right.

After these columns have been duly filled out and collated, the contents thereof shall be carried over to a registry of purchase and receipt orders, in which registry shall appear each one of the merchants. Afterwards, these orders shall be placed in a folder bearing the name of the merchant who filled them and shall be arranged in correlative order by using a serial number beginning with the number "one" for each merchant.

§ 183-12. Voucher registry 

The voucher registry shall be kept as shown in the model for the purpose appearing on the cover of the book of Form N.S. 779 "Special Disbursing Officer's Voucher". This form is self explanatory and very easy to keep, more so if we consider that it is being used for a long time.

The present form differs from the previous one in some respects, such as the title, etc. This one shall be called voucher registry and not order registry, because hereafter a separate special registry of purchase and receipt orders shall be kept [§ 183-11 of this 167

T.§ 183-12 

Ch. 11

title]. The same shall be filled out as heretofore, except that there are separate columns to note foodstuffs and supplies. Which means that the corresponding quantities according to the item shall be entered in that column. Each voucher for foodstuffs shall be entered in the column "foodstuffs" and each vouched for supplies shall be entered in the column "supplies". Fuel shall be entered in the column "supplies". Fluid gas shall be entered in the column "foodstuffs". 

The Accumulated Total Expense is very important inasmuch as by a single glance at it one may know at any time the total amount expended. In this column shall be entered any amount entered in either of the columns "foodstuffs" or "supplies". 

This shall be done by adding each amount entered to the total appearing in the column "accumulated total expense". At the end of each month, the two columns "foodstuffs" and "supplies" shall be added, and the total of these two columns must be equal to the last amount shown in the "accumulated total expense". If they are not equal, then there is an error somewhere, which should be easy to locate. The following month, the same operation shall be made as in the preceding month, but bearing in mind that the "accumulated total expense" this time will not be the total expended during the latter month, but the total expended in the two months.

To determine the exact expense in any one month, all you have to do is add the columns "supplies" and foodstuffs" for the corresponding month. 

To verify the correctness of said amounts, you subtract the accumulated total expense of the preceding month from the "Accumulated Total Expense" of the present month, and the result must necessarily be equal to the sum of the columns "supplies" and "foodstuffs" for the present month.

The procedure is easy and will prove to be very useful in any case. Guided by this voucher registry, Form 204 shall be filled out; and once this is done, the correctness of the amounts must be verified to see that they are in all cases identical. 

On the right hand margin of this registry may be noted monthly the total expenditure for each month. Thus, at the end of the year, you add the ten amounts appearing on the margin. The total must be equal to the last accumulated total expense appearing at the close of the year. For a better orientation, see the enclosed Form "Voucher Registry". This registry shall be filed together with all corresponding vouchers. 168

 § 183-13. Instructions regarding special disbursing officer's vouchers Auditor's Form N.S. 779 

(a) These vouchers shall be numbered in correlative order and by program, that is: a numeration beginning with the number one for each one of the programs of the Division. (b) They shall be prepared in sextuplicate. The copies shall be disposed of as indicated in said form on the upper left hand corner. (c) They shall always be prepared on the basis of the amounts appearing in the registry of purchase and receipt orders. (d) The prices indicated shall be those stipulated in the purchase and receipt order. These prices shall be the same as those appearing in the bid specifications of the merchant who was awarded the contract; provided, that if the system of open market is used, it shall be so indicated in the copies. (e) They shall be processed after having been reviewed as to required signatures and possible omission, composition, or computation errors. (f) The settlement voucher shall contain the exact information appearing in the corresponding partial receipts, as shown by column "Amount Received". Practices such as the following shall not be accepted: 

Ex.: Charcoal sacks at 704, 80¢ and 90¢ each were bought. 

For the sake of brevity, the average price of 80¢ is indicated. (This is incorrect.) 

Ex.: There were bought 25 pounds of yams and 20 pounds of sweet potatoes, both at $0.06 a pound. In the settlement voucher it is recited 45 pounds of yams or 45 pounds of sweet potatoes. (This is incorrect.) (g) The registry of settlement vouchers shall be used at all times. The use of this registry will redound in an improved organization of these documents and in the expeditious obtainment of any information desired to be verified. Special care shall be taken to have each and every sheet of the settlement voucher signed by all persons involved in the transaction, before they are distributed.

§ 183-15. General rules 

(a) The bidding procedure shall be used to obtain all necessary products. As a rule, the Government does not recognize any other means. (b) The administration of the funds in both items shall be such as to preclude overdrafts. (c) Under no circumstances shall money be accepted in lieu of a product not served. (d) There shall be no difference between the balance shown on the stock book of the lunchroom and the quantities actually in stock therein. The personnel of each lunchroom shall be specifically instructed to that effect, so as to avoid at all times any discrepancy in this respect. (e) A registry shall be kept of the credits extended (remittances) by the central office and the corresponding charges against the same. If the local management desires any orientation in this respect, we shall give it with pleasure. In due time, we shall send a model of this registry. (f) The funds for an item belong solely to that item. A difference in any one item may imply the necessity of a readjustment in the method used in the disposal of the said funds. In extreme cases, we may consider a request for the transfer of funds from one item to another, especially for food supplies; but such request must be made beforehand to the central office, whose authorization in writing must be had before taking action. (g) You must review and become familiar with the contents of Memorandum No. 44 of February 12, 1952, which refers to the 172

Ch. T.18 § 183-101 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

prohibition of the use of funds for the purchase of certain products, such as insect sprays, rat traps, locks, mops and accessories therefor, etc. (h) Cleaning material shall be used in the lunchroom in accordance with the instructions received to that effect from the technical section of this division. (i) Errors may be avoided in the posting of amounts from one document to another, by careful reviewing. (j) Only one person, the one in charge of the lunchroom or the teacher in charge, may take products out of the storeroom of the unit. Thus will but one person be responsible for the quantities in storage and those taken out.

§ 183-101. Status of equipment 

All equipment sent to school districts shall be considered as expendable property charged to the account of the school superintendent. The superintendents shall in turn charge same to the schools using it, in the same manner as in the case of regular school equipment. The responsibility for the custody and maintenance of this equipment is the same as is prescribed by the rules and regulations for all other school property. It is convenient to clarify that all china and glassware of school lunchrooms is considered as unexpendable property.

"To: "June 1, 1955

"SUBJECT: Revision of Memoranda of July 30, 1947, 'Use of School Lunchroom Equipment' and of August 11, 1947, ‘Responsibility as to Maintenance of School Lunchroom Equipment' 

"Every year, the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the municipalities and other entities invest considerable amounts of money in the equipping of school lunchrooms. To insure the proper use and protection of this equipment, as well as to replace the pieces lost or broken, we have revised the regulations as it appears in the enclosed bulletin. "We hope that these new rules be duly observed by all concerned so as to insure the proper use and duration of the equipment." 

§ 183-102. Inventory notebook 

This Department sent an inventory notebook to each school lunchroom for the purpose of striking a new inventory of the equipment available, as well as the new one acquired and the deductions authorized by Law. See Memorandum No. 12 of April 

21, 1955. 

Text references. Memo. No. 12 of April 21, 1955, referred to in text, is not included in this compilation. 

§ 183-103. Replacement of equipment 

Every piece of equipment lost or destroyed shall be replaced as soon as possible by another of like use, quality and price, by the person responsible for its custody, so that the school lunchroom equipment be maintained the same always. § 183-104. Count of individual pieces 

To avoid unnecessary losses, it is recommended that a teacher, employee or student be assigned, during lunch period, to take care of the return of each piece of equipment used by the children. 

Likewise, the person in charge of the lunchroom shall count all small pieces such as: tumblers, tableware, etc., at the close of the day's operations. 174

Ch. T.18 § 183-110 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

§ 183-105. Negligent destruction

Any diner who negligently destroys any piece shall replace it with another of like quality and price, or pay its cost, within the term of one month. 

§ 183-106. Transfer of equipment 

Once the equipment is delivered to a lunchroom, it shall not be transferred to another lunchroom without the previous authorization of the central office, and neither shall it be transferred to another school nor be used for other than school lunchroom purposes. 

§ 183-107. Retention of pay checks 

School superintendents are hereby authorized to retain the pay checks of the persons responsible for the equipment until they have delivered the same as they appear in the inventory and in receipts signed by them or until they have paid the cost price of the pieces not delivered. § 183-108. Changes in personnel; inventory

As soon as the person responsible for the equipment resigns or is transferred, a check-up of the inventory shall be made. Any missing piece shall be replaced or its cost price paid before the last pay check is delivered to said person. Likewise, when a new appointee to a position entailing responsibility for the equipment enters in the discharge of his office, the equipment shall be delivered to the new employee through inventory. The school director or teacher in charge of the school lunchroom shall be present at the time of making the inventory and shall sign the same. 

§ 183-109. Re-check of equipment 

It is advisable to re-check the school lunchroom equipment at least once each semester, or with such frequency as deemed necessary to insure its maintenance. 

§ 183-110. Storage 

At the end of the school term, the school lunchroom equipment shall be stored in a safe place, according to the following instructions: (1) The inventory of the equipment shall be properly checked and certified by the school director or teacher in charge. 175

T.§ 183-110 

Ch. 11

(2) Those pieces made of brass, cast iron, etc., which tend to oxidize through disuse or exposure to dampness and air, shall be oiled. To oil the equipment common vasoline and a paint brush may be used, and then the pieces may be wrapped in newspaper. 

Bundles shall be made, labeled with the name of the article and the number of pieces in each bundle. The following articles shall be oiled: spoons, knives, teaspoons, forks, kitchen, bread and peeling knives, meat grinders, can openers, mixers, iron pots and any other oxidizable material. (3) It is not necessary to oil articles made of porcelain-coated iron, stainless steel, galvanized zinc, china, glassware, wood, aluminum and plastic material. (4) Those articles consisting of more than one piece, such as: meat grinders, can openers, of the table or wall type, shall be carefully oiled and wrapped. It is advisable to secure all small pieces by tying them together with a fine wire before wrapping them. (5) Bulky equipment such as: wash basins, washtubs, kettles and the like, need not be wrapped to be stored. § 183-111. Stoves; hot utensils

The cooking stoves shall be cleaned once they cool off every day with a wet cloth. Hot utensils shall not be cleaned with cold water, for the sudden change in temperature may crack cast iron and damage aluminum. § 183-112. Draining equipment

It is recommended to drain all pieces of equipment before putting them away. § 183-113. Cleanliness; disinfectants

The cabinets, drawers and tables where the equipment is kept shall be maintained completely clean. The use of disinfecting water is advisable for the last rinse of the equipment. § 183-114. Instructions for the use of individual pieces (a) Scales shall be kept, as far as possible, in the lunchroom storeroom. To preserve scales in good condition, they shall be kept clean, and foodstuffs shall be weighed carefully and not roughly thrown on the pans of the scale. It is not advisable to leave any object on the pan while this equipment is not in use. (b) Service trays shall be used in the cafeteria-style service to 176

Ch. T.18 § 183-114 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

arrange on the counter milk glasses, bread, fruits or any other foodstuff. They may be used also to carry tumblers, plates, etc., from one place to another. (c) Galvanized sinks shall be used for the washing of utensils and to store water in lunchrooms lacking running water and good metal drums. (d) Sterilizing vessels shall be used exclusively for the sterilizing of equipment. (e) Boxes for tableware shall be used to keep tableware so as to facilitate handling during the cafeteria-style service. In order to insure proper handling of tableware and preclude its contamination, the same shall be placed in the box shortly before beginning to serve the food, seeing to it that all handles are placed in the same direction. (f) Baskets to sterilize tumblers and china are used for the sterilization of utensils (tumblers and plates). Plates shall be placed on edge, so that all surfaces may be sterilized; tumblers shall be placed sideways and all in the same direction so as to allow the water to penetrate down to the bottom and the tumblers may be easily drained when taken out of the water. The water shall cover all utensils placed in the basket. (g) Metal strainers shall be used to strain canned vegetables, in the preparation of milk, etc. Special care shall be taken in cleaning this piece of equipment so as to avoid the accumulation of food in the grooves and edges, especially on the lower edge. The use of filter brushes is recommended to clean this kind of strainer. (h) Tablespoons shall be used exclusively on the table. They shall never be used to cook or to serve. (i) Perforated kitchen spoons shall be used in serving salads and other dry dishes. (j) Two- and eight-ounce kitchen ladles shall be used in serving meats, grains, milk, juices, etc. (The eight-ounce ladle filled with milk is the ration of this food for a child.) (k) Kitchen knives shall be used exclusively to cut foodstuffs in the kitchen. (1) Bread knives shall be used exclusively to cut bread. (m) Aluminum bowls shall be used in the preparation of salads and other similar dishes, and to facilitate the serving of food. (n) Grinding machine shall be used to grind meat, vegetables, 177

T.18 183 Ch. 11 

etc. Care shall be taken in the cleaning and maintenance of each of the pieces of this equipment, especially before storing it away. (0) Aluminum pots shall be used in the preparation of milk, stewed grains, thick soups, desserts, etc. (p) Caldrons shall be used in the preparation of rice, scrambles and other like dishes. (q) Sectional trays shall be used to serve foods, including thick soups. (r) Deep china plates shall be used to serve food in lunchrooms lacking as yet sectional trays. (s) Can opener shall be adjusted so that it is always level with the cans to be opened. Thus will it last long. Special care shall be taken in the cleaning and maintenance of can openers by oiling them regularly. In so doing, the lubricant must be poured in the holes thereof. It is recommended that this piece of equipment be oiled for the vacation period. (t) Garbage can shall be placed in the most appropriate place in the kitchen and shall always be kept closed. It is recommended to cover the bottom and the inside with newspaper. This piece of equipment shall be cleaned daily, and if possible, washed with a disinfectant at least once a week. (u) Wash basins shall be used to wash utensils (small equipment such as tumblers and tableware) or to serve salads. (v) Mixer shall be used in the preparation of milk, scrambles, etc. In cleaning it, special care shall be taken not to leave any residue adhering thereto. § 183-115. Disinfectant 

Note: There may be used as disinfectant, the chemical agent supplied for the sterilization of utensils. § 183-116. Storage of infrequently-used equipment 

Those equipment pieces of infrequent use shall be stored away in a safe place, where they will not hinder the work of the lunchroom.

Employees shall have up to date their health certificates, issued by the Public Health Unit.

Employees shall observe all rules of personal hygiene required for the task of food handling. 

Before beginning to prepare and serve food, they shall see to it that their hands are thoroughly clean. 179

T.§ 183-205 Ch. 11 

 § 183-205. Sterilization 

The sterilization of utensils shall be carried out following the recommendations made in our Memorandum No. 23, of January 

13, 1954, on "Use of Chemical Agent in the Sterilization of Uten sils in School Lunchrooms and Child Breakfast Centers". 

We wish to remind you that the correct proportion to prepare the sterilizing solution is one level teaspoonful of the chemical agent for each five gallons of water. Utensils shall be dipped in this solution for three minutes. § 183-206. Preparation and use of products; reconstitution of milk 

Kitchen equipment used in the preparation of milk, such as pots, strainers, mixers and spoons, shall be previously sterilized and drained.

The reconstitution of milk shall be begun after 10:00 A.M., it being, therefore, the last food to be prepared. As you know, milk is a product in which bacteria may propagate easily and rapidly, and it is for this reason that we take the above precautions. § 183-207. Canned meat

Under no circumstances shall leftovers of canned meat be left to be consumed next day. § 183-208. Cheese and orange juice

Products such as cheese and orange juice shall, because of their perishable nature, begin to be consumed as soon as received, regardless of whether or not they are included in the menus. To that effect, the pertinent substitutions shall be made on the menus. § 183-209. Peanut butter 

Peanut butter shall be served on consecutive days. This will prevent left-overs from remaining for a longer time in the open can. You must make certain that after the can is opened, any leftover be kept well covered. At the proper time, this office will send plastic covers for this purpose. § 183-210. Purée, paste or canned tomatoes

Left-overs of purée, paste or canned tomatoes shall be kept in glass containers well covered. Containers used shall be sterilized properly before using them. 180

Ch. T.18 § 183-215 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

§ 183-211. Storage; use of foodstuffs according to date of receipt

Beginning with the next foodstuffs distribution for consumption during the month of April, truck laborers shall clearly mark on each container the date of receipt, upon delivering the products to the units. These products shall be put on the lower part of the stands or place designated for storing, removing to the upper part those in stock in the unit, for the purpose of using the latter first. § 183-212. Cooperation of laborers in organizing storerooms

Truck laborers shall cooperate in removing and arranging food supplies in storerooms, according to the existing space limitations. 

§ 183-213. Spoiled foodstuffs Spoiled foodstuffs shall be reported in Section No. 5 of the Monthly Report of Food Stock and Distribution (Form 510). In those cases in which it may be determined by local or area supervisors, or any other authorized official, that supplies have been spoiled through negligence in not using them in due time, the employee in charge of the dispatch and use of foodstuffs shall replace the quantities thereof which have been spoiled. We expect the employees' cooperation in complying with the instructions received on the proper use of foodstuffs, so as to render unnecessary the application of this measure. § 183-214. Monthly discussion with employees 

Local supervisors shall avail themselves of the employees' visit to their offices the last day of each school month to deliver the reports, for the following purpose: (1) Discuss any deficiencies observed during their visits and adopt measures to correct the same. (2) Explain the notes appearing on the menus to be served during the month, as well as circular letters or memoranda received from the central office, related to the program. (3) Clarify any doubt the employees may have in relation to their work. 

§ 183-215. Sketch of topics for discussion

Monthly Report of Visits and Activities of the Local Supervisor 

(Form 602) and with the voucher of travel expenses (Form 722);

§ 183-216. Compliance 

It is asked that school superintendents, school directors, teachers in charge, area and local supervisors, and personnel of school lunchrooms and child breakfast centers, get fully acquainted with the contents of this division and that they not spare any effort in complying with these provisions which are of vital importance for the proper operation of these programs, so beneficial to our children. 

SECTION DIVISION 4. SAFETY MEASURES AGAINST ACCIDENTS 

§ 183-241. Safety measures indicated 

For the purpose of avoiding unfortunate accidents among children and personnel attending school lunchrooms and milk stations, the following safety measures are indicated: (1) Children shall only be permitted to enter the lunchroom but never the kitchen. (2) Children shall be precluded from playing with or handling knives or other cutting objects. (3) Children shall be warned of the danger entailed in climbing windows, balconies or other high places. (4) The use or storing of insecticides or rat poisons in the unit is prohibited. (5) All fruit and vegetable peels shall be emptied into a container provided for that purpose. (6) The floor shall be free from cracks and kept completely dry. (7) The walls in the units shall be free from protruding nails or other objects endangering the safety of children and adults. (8) The surroundings of the units shall be kept completely free from broken glass, cans, or other cutting objects.

It is suggested to make and post in conspicuous places on the road posters such as: "Precaution - Milk Station" or "Slow Down 

Milk Station". Thus will motor vehicle drivers be warned of the proximity of a milk station or school lunchroom. 

This latter recommendation may well be an activity of the parents, or of the sponsors of the milk stations. 182

Ch. T.18 § 183-251 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

We have no doubt that the local school authorities and the personnel of these units will realize the importance of these rules and will see to it that they are observed for the sake of the personal safety of our children.

§ 183-252. Denomination 

The establishments to which secs. 183-251 to 183-282 refer shall, on and after the operative date thereof, be officially known as "child breakfast centers" instead of "milk stations". These child breakfast centers shall be an integral part of the school lunchroom program, and as such, shall operate under the jurisdiction of the Department of Education and the immediate supervision of the School Lunchroom Division of said department. § 183-253. Government and management

The government and management of the child breakfast centers shall be in charge of the supervisory and field personnel appointed for the purpose by the Secretary of Education, according to the nature of their functions. The supervisory personnel shall consist of the officials charged with the general direction and management of the program in the central offices or in specified locations and of any other officials to whom the Secretary of Education may entrust direction or supervisory works or activities. The field personnel shall consist of the employees charged with preparing and serving of food in each child breakfast center and who receive compensation on the basis of salary or emolument. 184

Ch. T.18 § 183-256 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

§ 183-254. Personnel; appointment, qualifications, status

Officials and employees of all categories at the service of the child breakfast centers shall be subject to the same training, experience and fitness requirements as the personnel of the school lunchroom program. Said officials and employees shall be comprised within the exempt service and their appointment shall be governed by the following provisions: the field personnel shall be appointed by the Secretary of Education on proposal of the school superintendent and upon recommendation of the School Lunchroom Division, the technical, administrative and all other personnel shall be appointed by the Secretary of Education on proposal and recommendation of the School Lunchroom Division. § 183-255. School superintendent as chief executive

The school superintendent shall be the chief executive of the child breakfast center program in each district, in representation of the Secretary of Education and the School Lunchroom Division. 

§ 183-256. Sponsors or other voluntary workers

The Commissioner of Education may appoint sponsors or other voluntary workers to collaborate, without any compensation whatsoever, in the work of the child breakfast centers. These appointments shall be made on proposal of the district school superintendent and must fall on persons who have evidenced their love for children, enjoy a high moral standing, are influential in the community, are apt to guide and direct, have enough free time to devote to the breakfast centers, and reside in or near the locality where is located the center in which they are to render their voluntary services. The functions and responsibilities of sponsors and other voluntary workers may involve primarily, although not exclusively, the following activities: (1) Diffuse the program in the community by circulating information material on the various aspects of the work of the child breakfast centers. (2) Enlist the cooperation of the public toward the improvement of the program and especially of the physical plant of the unit and of the discipline and order in its operation. (3) Publicize for general knowledge the rules and standards governing the program, thus furthering their observance. (4) To tender, at all times, love to children and treat them always with a spirit of understanding and diligent attention in the different phases of their physical development. 185

T.18 183 Ch. 11 

PUBLIC SCHOOLS 

(5) Organize recreational programs such as songs, stories, games, figure making, etc., in behalf of the children enrolled in the child breakfast centers. (6) Help instruct children in moral principles and good habits and in the rules of feeding, hygiene and preservation of health in general. (7) Promote the collective organization of parents and other persons concerned with the common-weal through the holding of gatherings and lectures, exhibition of educational films, and visits to child breakfast centers to observe their operation. (8) Take note of any deficiencies or irregularities noticed in breakfast centers and report them to the district school superintendent. (9) Take the proper steps with the aqueduct and sewer authority for installation of water service in the child breakfast centers lacking it. (10) Ask commercial establishments, family homes and civic institutions to donate toys, books, films, pictures, and other articles fit for use in the recreation program of child breakfast centers. § 183-257. Volunteer workers; functions; instruction

The functions and activities of sponsors, voluntary workers or other collaborators in the work of the child breakfast centers shall be understood to be principally directed to give help and cooperation to the personnel in charge of the direction, supervision and management of the program and shall, therefore, exclude any intervention in the government thereof. The sponsors and other voluntary collaborators may be gathered in assembly to inform them about the various aspects of the program and the nature of their functions and activities, and to encourage them to lend their cooperation with growing efficiency. In these assemblies must be present the school superintendent and the local and area supervisors of the school lunchroom program and of the child breakfast centers. Furthermore, the Central Office shall make the necessary arrangements to send its representation to each such assembly, if so requested. 

§ 183-258. Organization of program 

The child breakfast center program in each school district shall comprise all centers heretofore and hereafter established. 186

Ch. T.18 183-261 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS § 183-259. Enrollment 

The enrollment of each center shall consist of 75 commensals as a minimum and of 100 as a maximum. This enrollment may be increased or decreased on petition of the school superintendent, upon approval of the School Lunchroom Division. In case of increase, the approval of the School Lunchroom Division must be had before admitting the new commensals. Said enrollment shall consist entirely of needy children who do not share the benefits of any other feeding program supported in whole or in part by the insular or federal government. The age for enrollment in the child breakfast centers shall be from 2 to 7 years, but children between 

7 and 10 years old, not attending school, may also enroll. Provided, however, that children between 2 and 10 years old who are enrolled in schools lacking school lunchroom service may share the benefits of the child breakfast centers. For a child to be enrolled in the child breakfast centers, an application shall first be filed to that effect, signed by the father or guardian and approved by the proper authority.

Amendment. Section was amended by Circ. Letter No. 22 

of Oct. 6, 1952. 

§ 183-260. Attendance 

In each center shall be kept in the appropriate form a record of the daily attendance of the children enrolled therein. Using this record as a guide, every effort shall be made toward achieving constantly the highest attendance possible, eliminating from the list, where necessary, those children who persistently and without justified cause, attend irregularly, and admitting in their stead other children through the enrollment requirements and procedure established by regulation. § 183-261. Reduction in enrollment

Requests for reduction in enrollment shall be sent by the school superintendent to the School Lunchroom Division and shall be effective as soon as they are received therein. When the average attendance in any center is quite consistently below the authorized enrollment, the School Lunchroom Division may motu proprio carry out the pertinent readjustments in the serving of food, even without receiving the request for reduction of enrollment from the school superintendent. 187

T.18 183 Ch. 11 

§ 183-262. Schedule 

The child breakfast centers shall operate every day, except Sundays and legal holidays, according to the following time schedule: 

From 8:00 A.M. to 9:00 A.M. Period for the preparation of of food. 

From 9:00 A.M. to 10:00 A.M. Period for serving food to children. 

From 10:00 A.M. on Period for cleaning purposes and 

preparation of reports.

This time schedule shall be strictly followed in each and every one of the centers, both by the children and by the administrative personnel. § 183-263. Time for arrival, leaving

Children must be instructed to be present at the centers all working days at 8:00 A.M. and to stay therein as long as necessary after breakfast in order to participate in the recreation programs. § 183-264. Source of food and supplies

In the preparation of breakfasts shall be used the foodstuffs and supplies acquired with the resources available to the program and of the kind and in the amount from time to time prescribed by the School Lunchroom Division. These foodstuffs shall be sent monthly to the centers from the central warehouses of said Division in sufficient quantities for the service during one month, according to the maximum authorized enrollment and the types of distribution established. In the daily use of these foodstuffs the chronological order in which they have been received in each center shall be strictly taken into account. § 183-265. Left-overs and waste

Food left-overs or wastes in the breakfast centers shall not be sold or donated for any purpose whatsoever, except for use as feed for animals in Government establishments or institutions, when they may be donated upon express authorization from the central office of the School Lunchroom Program. 

§ 183-266. Purchase of fuel and cleaning materials 

In addition to the foodstuffs supplied by the central office, the breakfast centers shall have an assignment of funds for the pur- 188

Ch. T.18 183-269 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

chase of fuel and cleaning materials, the amount to be related to the size of the enrollment and attendance. The school superintendents shall follow, for these purchases of fuel and cleaning material, the same procedure established for school lunchrooms for similar purchases. 

§ 183-267. Inventory 

The employees in charge of the child breakfast centers shall have the custody of all the equipment, supplies and foodstuffs, of all of which they shall keep a complete inventory. Upon ceasing in office, these employees shall deliver through inventory to their successors or to any other competent authority, the property for which they are responsible, and any shortage through loss or destruction due to negligence shall be replaced with another of the same kind and quality, or paid at the current price in the market, by the person responsible therefor. 

§ 183-268. Establishment 

The establishment of new child breakfast centers may be authorized only upon application of an interested party, upon compliance with the requirements prescribed therefor by secs. 183-251 to 183282 and provided there are funds available for their support. Every application for a new center shall be submitted to the district school superintendent, who shall transmit it with his recommendation to the School Lunchroom Division of the Department of Education. Said application must be authorized by the Mayor of the municipality where the establishment of the new center is desired, or by a civic institution of recognized responsibility, or by one or more persons who present satisfactory evidence of being willing and able to assume and fulfill the duties and obligations inherent in the establishment of a new child breakfast center. 

§ 183-269. Premises - Responsibility 

The party applying for or sponsoring a new child breakfast center shall provide, at his own expense, a site of the size and conditions specified below, the complete equipment therefor, the total cost of water consumption for the cooking of foods and for cleaning purposes, and shall preserve at all times the physical plant in the minimum hygienic condition permissible for this kind of establishment according to the rules and standards of the Department of Health. 189

T.§ 183-270 

Ch. 11

§ 183-270. 

Condition 

The premises for a breakfast center must meet the requirements established for the Department of Health for premises devoted to the use of school lunchrooms and, furthermore, shall offer all safety conditions required for the protection of the equipment and foodstuffs against theft, burglary, etc. Said premises must be of the size, structure and all other conditions specified in sec. 183-283, 

§ 183-271.- Construction 

In case of the construction of the premises offered for the new child breakfast center, the applicant or sponsor shall not undertake the works without having first obtained from the School Lunchroom Division of the Department of Education the formal promise of the grant of the new unit. 

§ 183-272. Equipment 

The equipment of every new child breakfast center shall be sufficient in quantity and quality as to guarantee a satisfactory and speedy service. 

§ 183-273. Inspection 

The premises as well as the equipment shall be inspected by competent officials of the School Lunchroom Division, whom the applicant shall notify for the purpose, as soon as it is ready for use. § 183-274. Census to determine enrollment

In all cases of application for a new child breakfast center, the local supervisor of school lunchrooms of the respective municipality or school district shall carry out a census among the inhabitants of the locality to be served thereby, so as to determine the present and potential enrollment of children meeting the requirements established by secs. 183-251 to 183-282. For this census the forms prescribed for the purpose shall be used and the result thereof shall be informed to the School Lunchroom Division for proper action. 

§ 183-275. Moving 

Any child breakfast center may be moved from one site to another within the same ward or demarcation, and with the same enrollment, provided such moving is requested from the School Lunchroom Division well beforehand, accompanying the application 190

Ch. 

T.18 § 183-278 

SCHOOL LUNCHROOMS 

by the proper form for the purpose of the inspection of the new premises so as to determine whether it meets the conditions established by secs. 183-251 to 183-282 and by the rules and standards of the Department of Health. 

§ 183-276. Moving tantamount to closing 

The moving of a child breakfast center from one ward to another, with a different enrollment, shall be deemed to be tantamount to the closing of the unit so moved and to the establishment of a new unit in the new location, and in such case, the provisions of secs. 183-251 to 183-282 relative to the closing of units in operation and the establishment of new units shall be adhered to. 

§ 183-277. Reasons for closing 

Any child breakfast center may be closed for any one or more of the following reasons: 

(1) Reduction of the enrollment to a figure so negligible as to justify discontinuance of the unit. (2) Extremely unhygienic conditions of the premises or the surroundings, or both. (3) Premises lacking adequate safety conditions for the protection of the foodstuffs and equipment. (4) Shrinkage of the resources available for the support of the program. (5) Nonperformance of the conditions of the agreement. (6) Nonperformance of the obligations contracted by the sponsors upon applying for the establishment of the unit. 

§ 183-278. Closing inventory 

Upon closing a child breakfast center, an inventory shall be taken of the foodstuffs, equipment and any other property existing therein. This inventory shall be sent or delivered to the district school superintendent, who shall immediately report the closing of the unit to the School Lunchroom Division and also to the warehouse charged with the supplying of the closed center, said warehouse to be furnished with a copy of the inventory of foodstuffs so that the same may be recovered and returned to the warehouse. The equipment shall be recovered by the school superintendent himself and kept in a safe place until returned to the School Lunchroom Division or assigned to other units. 191

T.§ 183-279 Ch. 11 

 § 183-279. Safety measures 

All necessary or advisable safety measures shall be put into practice in the child breakfast centers so as to prevent accidents among the children attending them. To this end you may be guided by sec. 183-141 of this title. 

§ 183-280. Instruction, training 

The School Lunchroom Division shall from time to time organize training and instruction courses for the personnel of the child breakfast centers. Although attendance at these courses will be voluntary, it is advisable that employees be especially interested in participating therein with a view to fit themselves for rendering a more efficient service. § 183-281. Burglary, theft

In case of burglary or theft in any child breakfast center, the fact shall be immediately reported to the chief of the insular police in the locality and to the School Lunchroom Division. All reports relating to happenings of this nature shall be as complete and detailed as circumstances will permit and shall contain a list of the articles stolen, as well as a statement of the precautionary measures taken or proposed to avoid a repetition of the case. § 183-282. Effectiveness 

Sections 183-251 to 183-282 shall take effect on the date of its promulgation.

Likewise, the school superintendent shall be appointed director on the local level, and he shall delegate to the local supervisor of school lunchrooms the responsibility of conducting the food subcommittee in each locality.

§ 183-353. Disaster classification The following organization shall govern in cases of disaster: 

The three following classifications shall be considered: (1) Disaster in a sector of the municipality

All school lunchrooms in the vicinity of the disaster area shall render service to the victims, as it becomes necessary. (2) Disaster in the municipality

All lunchrooms of the municipality shall be used, as it becomes necessary. (3) Disaster on State level (general) 

All school lunchrooms in Puerto Rico shall render service, as it becomes necessary. 

The service offered in this emergency shall follow, as far as possible, the standards and patterns governing at present the school lunchroom program. 

§ 183-354. Food 

(a) Menus

Menus specially prepared for disaster cases by the School Lunchroom Division shall be used. (b) Preparation and service of food in the lunchrooms The lunchroom shall supply the foodstuffs it may have; and the 

Red Cross, the supplies lacking to prepare the special menus for disaster cases.

As the supplies of the lunchroom become exhausted, the Red Cross shall provide the necessary supplies to carry on the service, unless they are received from the storerooms of the School Lunchroom Division. In this latter case, the storerooms shall be directly instructed from the central office of the Division, unless communication means are not available, in which case, the storerooms shall proceed to deliver the necessary foodstuffs, notifying, in due time, the central office. 196

§ 212-1. Introduction 

The Department of Education has on repeated occasions announced its intention of placing the numerous and difficult tasks of the vast educational program in the hands of the most capable persons. Thus, a few years ago it initiated a critical study of the standards and procedures governing the selection of the teaching and directive personnel of the system. As a result of these efforts, the educational system is governed today by standards of selection comparable to the best of a good system of public personnel administration.

The Teachers' Certification Act of May 11, 1945, which regulates the granting of certificates for the holding of instructional positions, represents another effort to improve the recruitment and retention of personnel.

Elementary and secondary teachers and those of other categories are selected on the basis of regulations drawn up for that purpose and from lists of eligibles prepared in accordance with the general and professional preparation, experience, and other indices of merit of each candidate. Occasionally, and when circumstances so require, the regulations for the selection of personnel are amended with the purpose of improving the system of selection. 201

T.§ 212-1 Ch. 13 

Finally, a system for the selection of persons dedicated to school administration and supervision has been prepared. Circular Letter

No. 5 of July 24, 1951 [§ 212-12 of this title] established the pro cedures for the selection of school principals. This effort constitutes the starting point in the development of a valid system for the selection of such personnel. At present various means are being utilized to determine the capacity of candidates. Among the methods thus employed are the interview, the study of the service records, and the written examination. 

The satisfactory results attained through the use of this method point to the advisability of creating and putting into practice a systematic procedure for the selection of all administrative and supervisory personnel of the school system. Hence, the standards which are described in the following pages have been prepared and adopted.

: All Instructional Personnel of the School System 

January 19, 1954 

SUBJECT: STANDARDS FOR THE SELECTION OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND SUPERVISORY PERSONNEL OF THE SCHOOL SYSTEM Ladies and Gentlemen: 

One important responsibility in the administrative spheres of government is the continuous improvement of the procedures for the selection of personnel. This responsibility is of great importance at present owing to the rapid expansion of the school system in recent years and to the resulting complexity of the educational work. 

Among the aspects of the organization and administrative methods in our school system which have been revised are the procedures for the selection of teaching personnel. Similarly, it has become necessary to examine the methods for the selection of administrative and supervisory personnel. 202

Ch. 

T.18 § 212-3 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

The standards set forth in the accompanying pamphlet represent the culmination of a series of efforts designed to place that selection at the level of the soundest standards of public service. Its purpose is to encourage good administration and give proper direction of the educational effort, both at the local and at state levels. Similarly, it is hoped that it will encourage and guide the efforts to excel of all who are dedicated to public service in the educational field. 

Therefore, we hope that these standards will be duly brought to the attention of the teaching and directive personnel in the districts. 

§ 212-2. Purposes 

The purposes of the procedure which has been adopted are the following: 

(1) To establish the bases of a system for the selection of administrative and supervisory personnel which compares favorably with the best standards of a competitive system. The selection will be based on eligibility and merit and will utilize a competitive process in order to choose public servants who are best qualified for the management of the school system. (2) To establish an auxiliary means which will facilitate forecasting the needs for competent and properly trained personnel, and which at the same time, will orient and promote the development of the capacities and skills required to insure the progress of public education. It will be a means for the orientation of preand in-service training. It will be useful in the preparation and the supplying of candidates to fill vacant as well as newly-created positions. (3) To facilitate the integration of the procedure for the selection of administrative and supervisory personnel in the generally favorable atmosphere prevailing in other aspects of the school system. Thus, the selection will be in accord with the democratic spirit governing supervision in particular and the objectives and practices of the public school in general. In this sense the procedure will be in harmony with the system of certification, the salary schedule, the classifications, the retirement system, and other aspects of school administration. 

§ 212-3. Basic principles 

The following premises were taken into consideration in developing the procedure: (1) That there is a need for a clear and definite written procedure that will orient and stimulate candidates who follow a public career in the field of school administration. 203

T.§ 212-3 

Ch. 13

(2) That it is necessary to provide ample opportunity for the consideration of all eligible candidates. (3) That the selection should be made on a competitive basis which will permit the discovery of the best administrative and educational talent. (4) That there is not at present a single instrument which by itself, is capable of measuring all characteristics of the candidate. 

Similarly, no single trait of an individual can by itself serve as a criterion for predicting professional success. Therefore, the system described here establishes a variety of criteria and measures to determine in the aggregate the relative fitness of the candidate. 

Thus, the decision in favor of a given candidate will be governed by due consideration of the diverse factors. The experience, general and professional preparation, civic and professional activities, personality, reputation, leadership and other factors will receive the proper recognition or weight corresponding to each. 

§ 212-4. Scope 

(a) The procedure adopted will be applicable to all eligible candidates who apply for appointment or promotion to the following positions: 

(1) Elementary school principal 

(2) Secondary school principal (junior or senior high school) (3) Vocational senior high school principal (4) Rural second unit principal (5) Assistant superintendent of schools (6) Superintendent of schools (7) Zone supervisor (A) of English (B) of health (C) of art (D) of music (8) Curriculum technician (b) For purposes of these standards promotion may include, in addition to an increase in the classification and change of title, changes in category and transfers to more highly populated zones. 

Thus, for example, the following will be considered promotions:

The change from Superintendent I to Superintendent II; that from 

Principal to Assistant Superintendent; and other, similar changes that involve an increase in salary. 204

Ch. T.18 § 212-7 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

§ 212-5. Eligibility 

(a) Every applicant to the previously mentioned positions should make sure in advance of his eligibility; that is, he should be sure that he meets the legal requirements and those established as administrative standards. Regularly, in Puerto Rico, the eligibility to occupy a position in the school system is acquired as soon as the requirements specified in the Teachers' Certification Act have been met. Every person who fulfills such requisites acquires a certificate, which confers on him legal authority either to teach or to direct a school as the case may be. Another section of this division contains a summary of the requirements established by law for each position. (b) In those cases for which the Certification Act does not establish requirements, the Department sets them up in its administrative standards, as will be explained later. Therefore, every candidate to administrative and supervisory positions within the school system should, for their own guidance, read carefully the section of these standards referring to the requisites. The law specifies the following general requisites: To be not less than 

18 nor more than 55 years of age; to observe irreproachable moral conduct; to be physically fit; and to be a citizen of the United States.

Text references. Teachers' Certification Act, see note under § 212-1 of this title. 

§ 212-6. The application 

The mere fact that one has applied either verbally or in writing, or has obtained a certificate, does not of itself constitute a valid application in the system of selection. The candidate must submit another application by means of Form No. 401 which the Department will supply upon request. This application must be accompanied by Form OP-12 (Medical Examination) signed by an authorized physician. These documents should be sent to the Department of Education. 

§ 212-7. The examinations 

Every candidate who is eligible and who has submitted the corresponding application, will be required to take a series of examinations which will furnish the Department the greatest possible amount of information about applicants. Following is a brief description of these examinations. 205

T.§ 212-7 Ch. 13 

EDUCATION · - PUBLIC SCHOOLS 

(1) Written examinations. The selecting committee will give a series of written examinations, including general examinations for all, as well as special examinations corresponding to the different positions. Such examinations will be standardized and will be of recognized validity and reliability. 

At present the Department is utilizing the National Teacher 

Examinations administered by the Educational Testing Service of 

Princeton, New Jersey, through the Division of Research and 

Statistics of the Department of Education. These examinations have an excellent standing nationally in professional and university circles. School systems employ them as auxiliary means of evaluation and prediction. (2) Interview examination. The personal interview which also constitutes a competitive examination will be another means to supplement the information about the candidate, and by this means it will be possible to appraise the candidate's personality traits. In the interview the candidate will have the opportunity to demonstrate his ability to concentrate on and intelligently to discuss situations relative to his present work or to the position he has applied for, as well as cultural and social situations or problems. 

§ 212-8. Date of the written examinations 

At opportune times the Department will announce the dates of the written examinations and will advise candidates of the date and place of the interview examination. § 212-9. Other sources of information about candidates 

With the purpose of supplementing the information which the previously mentioned examinations furnish about candidates, the 

Department of Education will make use of the following means: (1) Official transcript of credits from the college or university at which the candidate studied. (2) The record of service of the candidate, including professional references, record of civic and professional activities and a complete record of his experience. 

(3) Application form (No. 401). 

(4) Information supplied by superintendents of schools. In cases of vacant positions in the school districts, the superintendents may send information about eligible candidates. When there is a vacancy in the position of a principal, the superintendent shall send 206

Ch. T.18 § 212-11 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS a report as specified in Circular Letter No. 5 of July 24, 1951 [§ 

212-12 of this title], which should contain the following: (A) A brief description of the educational situation in the school where the vacancy exists. The report should include, besides up to date information on enrollment, organization, physical plant and projects or plans being developed, special factors affecting the work of this school. (B) An explanation of the specific functions of the position in the light of the educational situation set forth. The work to be done should be described and adequate attention should be paid to the general and special factors affecting the principal's work. (C) A list of the eligible candidates who work in the district where the vacancy exists. (D) An objective description of the merits of the candidates whose names are included. In this part, the superintendent should present facts which will help the Department in reaching a decision in the selection and appointment of school principals. § 212-10. Recommendation of candidates (a) The selection committee will carefully study and evaluate the reports on each candidate and will select, on a comparative basis, and taking into consideration the relative weight of each factor, the candidate or candidates who will be recommended for appointment. (b) It should be understood that the mere fact that a candidate is not selected for a particular position, does not disqualify him from competing for other vacancies. Nor does it in any way affect the rights he has already acquired in the fulfillment of his functions. § 212-11. Requisites for the various positions

Duties of superintendents to report candidates for position of principal (a) The present administration of the Department of Education from the very beginning has publicly announced its firm intention of placing the numerous tasks and responsibilities of the vast educational program of the Government of Puerto Rico in the most capable hands. Since then we have begun a careful study of the standards governing the system of selection and appointment of the teaching and administrative personnel. The result of this study is the new regulation governing the selection and appointment of teachers whom the central office contracts directly. The regulation covering the selection and appointment of elementary teachers has also been revised.

With regard to administrative and supervisory personnel in the districts, the Department is now working on the improvement of the standards governing their selection and appointment. The new system has the following characteristics: (1) Ample facilities to insure that all who are interested in holding administrative and supervisory positions in the districts may learn of opportunities for appointment as soon as they occur. (2) Careful study of all information relative to candidates, including their preparation, professional and civic activities, etc. (3) Use of the interview as a means to become better acquainted with the candidates. 210

(4) Ability of the candidate to adapt to the conditions and circumstances affecting the situation with which he will be confronted.
