§ 212-52. Definition of terms 

The following terms or phrases used in this division shall have the meaning indicated in each case: 

(1) Regular certificate. Certificate issued pursuant to the Act to Regulate the Certification of Teachers, which authorizes its holder to work as teacher in the public schools and in the private schools accredited by the Department of Education of Puerto Rico. 

(2) Permanent teacher. The teacher who has satisfactorily completed the two years of continuous practice on probation provided by Act No. 312 of May 15, 1938, known as the Permanent

Appointment Act [18 L.P.R.A. §§ 214 to 218]. 

(3) Probationary teacher. A teacher contracted to practice for the probation period provided by the Act. (4) Substitute teacher. The teacher appointed to fill a vacancy during a specified period, because its incumbent is on leave without pay. To fill the position, the candidate has to hold a regular teacher's certificate. (5) Temporary teacher. The teacher appointed to occupy a position for a specific period. The candidate must hold a regular teacher's certificate. (6) Provisional teacher. The teacher appointed to occupy a position without holding the corresponding regular certificate. (7) List of eligibles. A list containing, in order of merits, the names of all the candidates who applied for appointment, transfer or reallocation and who possess the regular certificate required to occupy the position they apply for. 213

T.§ 212-52 

Ch. 13

(8) List of provisional teachers. A list containing, in order of merits, the names of all the candidates who applied for appointment or reallocation, and who do not possess the corresponding regular certificate. (9) Transfer. The transfer of a teacher (permanent or probationary), within the same or another class of position, from one school district to another. (10) Reallocation. The transfer of a teacher (permanent or probationary) from one class of position to another, within the same school district; and the transfer of a teacher (permanent or probationary), from the rural to the urban zone, within the same class of position and the same school district. (11) Personnel division. The personnel division of the Department of Education. (12) Residence. The bona fide place of residence.

Text references. The act on certification of teachers in effect on the date of promulgation of this division is Act June 21, 1955, No. 94, p. 488; 18 L.P.R.A. §§ 260 to 273. Former provisions on this subject appeared in 18 L.P.R.A. §§ 219 to 244. 

§ 212-53. Applications 

(a) Any person interested in filing an application to enter, or reenter, the teaching profession, must meet the following general requirements: (1) To be not less than 18 nor over 55 years of age. (The 

55 years of age is applicable only to teachers entering for the first time the teaching profession. It does not apply in the case of teachers who reenter.) (2) To be a citizen of the United States of America. (3) To observe unimpeachable moral conduct. (4) To be physically able to practice as teacher. (b) For the purpose of the list of eligibles and the list of provisional teachers, the applications received from the first to the 

28th or 29th of February of each school year shall be taken into consideration. (c) The names of the candidates whose applications are received after the last day of the month of February of each school year shall be interpolated in the list of eligibles or of provisional teachers. The turns of the candidates appearing in the list of provisional teachers and who obtain the normal school diploma or the Bachelor's Degree in Education in May, shall be likewise 214

Ch. T.18 § 212-54 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

interpolated in the corresponding turns of the list of eligibles as soon as the list of graduates from the teachers' institutions that prepare students for the teaching profession is received, as indicated in sec. 212-59 of this title.

The interpolations of new turns in the lists and the adjustment in turns once the candidates have completed the requirements for obtaining the normal diploma or the Bachelor in Education, shall be effective on the date the superintendent of schools and the school director receive them: Provided, that the interpolation of new turns or the readjustment of turns from the lists of provisional candidates to the lists of eligibles once the candidates have completed the requirements for obtaining the normal diploma or the Bachelor in Education, under no condition shall render void the right already acquired by candidates to whom the school superintendents and school directors have already made an offer of appointment. (d) The information required in the application shall be furnished with accuracy and precision. Any alteration of truth or false information which, in the opinion of the Secretary of Education, is included in the documents submitted, or in the application, in violation of this division, shall be sufficient cause for the temporary or permanent elimination of the name of the candidate from the list or to render void any appointment, transfer or reallocation obtained thereby.

§ 212-54. Preparation of the lists 

In the lists for each district there shall appear in the first place the candidates holding a regular certificate for the position they are applying for (list of eligibles), and, in the second place, those who do not hold that certificate (list of provisional teachers). 

Provided, that the teachers with probationary or permanent contracts, candidates for transfer from one school district to another or for reallocation from the rural to the urban zone within the same category of position, shall be certified in order of preference; and that there shall be a single group of provisional teachers, and in said group the residence of the candidate shall not be considered for the purpose of giving him preference; the lists shall be made as follows: 

(1) Candidates who are residents of the school district.

The capital comprises the school districts of San Juan and Río 215

(2) Candidates who are not residents of the school district. In those groups, the candidates shall be placed in the following order: (A) Academic preparation and experience combined, according to the table of qualifications appearing in sec. 212-55 of this title; provided: (i) That in the preparation of the lists for secondary schools, candidates shall appear in order of their specialization. (iii) That the candidates who qualify for science and mathematics positions without having completed their specialization on those subjects, shall appear in order of the number of credits which they have completed thereon. (iv) That in case of candidates for home economics positions there shall be added to the total points for academic preparation, the number of points corresponding to the experience in their specialty. Computation of preparation and experience for the purpose of turn § 212-57. 

(a) A minimum of nine school months in the public schools or in recognized private schools within a school year, shall be considered as one year of service. (b) Fractions of uncompleted years may be added for the determination of full years of 10 school months. (c) Additional credits will be computed taking as basis the number of credits required in the institution where they complete the studies leading to the normal school diploma or the Bachelor's degree on the graduation date of the applicants. § 212-58. 

University, government employees

The names of the candidates who worked in the elementary and secondary schools of the University of Puerto Rico or as teachers in other departments of the Government of Puerto Rico shall appear in the lists in the corresponding groups, their experience being considered as having been acquired in the public school, after certification by the appointing authority. § 212-59. 

Assignment of turns

The order of turns in the lists to which the present section refers shall be fixed on the basis of the experience and the official, verified information concerning the preparation of the candidate, until the 31st of December of each school year. This must be set forth in the transcript of record filed in the Personnel Division not later than the 28th or 29th of February of each school year; provided, that the candidates who graduate from normal school or from the College of Education with a Bachelor's degree in May shall be allowed the university credits they have received up to that date.

For the purpose of assigning them a turn, the Personnel Division shall use the list of graduates that the universities or colleges of Puerto Rico generally submit in May. Those who graduate from normal school or who receive a Bachelor's degree in 

Education, on a subsequent date, shall have their turns readjusted as soon as the Personnel Division receives the lists in question. 219

T.§ 212-59 

Ch. 13

This provision does not relieve the interested parties from the obligation of sending their official transcript of record to the 

Personnel Division. To that effect the following is provided: 

(1) May graduates shall submit their transcript of credits no later than June 30. (2) July graduates shall submit their transcript of credits no later than August 30. (3) December graduates shall submit their transcript of credits no later than January 30.

Therefore, it shall be the responsibility of the candidates to keep their records up to date insofar as academic and professional preparation is concerned.

Upon receipt of the pertinent official information, the provisional teachers who meet the requirements for issuance of a regular certificate, subsequent to the preparation of the lists, shall be entitled to a readjustment in their turns pursuant to the provisions of secs. 212-53 (c) and 212–54 to 212-63 of this title.

Teachers pensioned for physical disability

Whenever a teacher, pensioned on account of physical disability, wishes to return to practice, he shall file an application for employment attaching thereto a letter from the retirement board of school teachers where it is certified: (1) That the cause which originally motivated his retirement for disability has disappeared. (2) That his pension has been suspended.

This application shall be taken into consideration as long as the candidate meets the other requirements demanded by this division at the time he files his application. His name shall be submitted to the superintendent of schools and school directors of the districts where he has applied, with instructions that he be given the first turn in the list in the category of position for which he holds a regular certificate. § 212-62. — Teachers pensioned for years of service

Teachers pensioned for years of service who wish to return to 220

Ch. T.18 § 212-67 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

the practice as public school teachers may file an application for employment provided they meet the following requirements: (1) To be less than sixty (60) years of age. (2) To be of sound mental and physical health in order to practice as teacher. (He shall attach to his application the corresponding medical certificate.) (3) To hold a regular certificate valid for the position he applied for. (4) Satisfactory personal interview.

The application shall be considered if the candidate meets the other requirements set forth in this division. His name shall be submitted to the school superintendents and school directors according to the turn which applies to him pursuant to the provisions of secs. 212–54 to 212-63 of this title. 

§ 212-63. Rural certificate holders 

Teachers who possess a rural certificate only shall not be reallocated to the urban zone. 

§ 212-64. Challenge of the lists; examination 

The school superintendents and school directors shall have in their offices copies of the lists accessible for examination by the teachers, the school authorities and any other entity or individuals with genuine interest in such lists. § 212-65. Time for challenge 

Any person who introduces evidence to the effect that the turn. of a teacher in the lists was not fixed according to the rules established in this division, may challenge said procedure before the Secretary of Education. The challenge must be filed not later than 

30 days after the date of approval of the lists by the Secretary of Education. 

§ 212-66. Selection of candidates 

Time The school superintendents and school directors shall commence with the selection of candidates as soon as they receive the lists ordered by this division, to fill vacancies, or newly created positions, upon commencement of the school year in August of every year. § 212-67. 

Selection by superintendents and directors

Once the lists described in secs. 212-54 to 212-63 of this title 221

T.§ 212-67 

Ch. 13

are sent to the school superintendents and to the school directors they shall select from those lists, following the order of preference therein, the teachers whose appointment is to be proposed to the Secretary of Education for vacancies and for new positions at the commencement of the school year according to their specialty in the case of secondary school teachers. Once the list of candidates becomes exhausted, the school superintendents shall send a telegram to the Personnel Division in order for the latter, in turn, to submit new candidates.

The names selected according to the lists shall be set forth in 

Form 409-R2 (Proposal for Teaching Personnel), and shall be sent to the Secretary of Education. These papers must be signed by the school superintendent and the school director. The Secretary of Education, in turn, shall return to said officials a copy of those documents with his approval or remarks. § 212-68. . Provisional candidates for first grade 

The superintendents of schools are given power, in selecting provisional candidates for elementary school positions to teach first grade, to offer the position to the first candidate appearing on the lists and who has the academic preparation to teach elementary grades regardless of the fact that the first candidate with academic preparation to teach elementary school is not the candidate in strict order of preference. Provided, that in the cases where the superintendent of schools uses that power, the teachers so appointed shall not be reallocated to teach other grades during the period for which they were thus appointed.

May 14, 1957. § 212-69. Direct appointment 

If the school superintendent and the school director should fail to send within the term of five work days as of the date when the vacancies occur the corresponding proposal, the Secretary of Education shall proceed to fill the vacancy by direct appointment. 

In case that the aforesaid officials fail to agree as to the selection of any candidate, each one of them may address the Secretary of Education in writing, setting forth their points of view, within a term of three work days, as of the date the vacancy occurs. The 

Secretary of Education shall decide the case pursuant to the provisions in this division and to the best convenience of the public interest. 222

§ 212-70. 

Rejection by candidate

When the candidates with highest points in the lists do not accept a position or fail to answer the offer, said position shall be offered to the candidate next in turn. The superintendent of schools and the school director shall so set forth in the proposal retaining in their offices the corresponding evidence. § 212-71. 

Right to reallocation and transfer

The teachers reallocated within the same school district and in the same category of position, from the rural to the urban zone, or those transferred from one school district to another, on a temporary basis, and who hold a valid regular certificate in the category of the position they applied for, shall be entitled to reallocation or permanent transfer, upon arrival of their turn, pursuant to the provisions of this division. § 212-72. Challenge of the selection of candidates 

Any appointment, transfer or reallocation made in contravention with this division may be challenged before the Secretary of Education by any person considering himself aggrieved. The corresponding evidence must be attached to the complaint.

81, May 14, 1957. § 212-77. Vacancies in categories of direct appointment

When vacancies occur in the categories of direct appointment, the superintendent of schools shall so inform the Personnel Division by immediate remittance of Form 409-R3 (Vacancies of Teaching Personnel) to which the corresponding documents have been attached. § 212-78. Application for direct appointment 

Candidates for direct appointment must file the application for change or for employment every year in order to preserve the right to compete with the other candidates to fill permanent positions within the different categories. 

§ 212-79. Exchange Same category 

Teachers with the same category, whether permanent or on probation, may exchange their positions according to the following provisions: (1) Teachers seeking exchange shall address the superintendents of schools and school directors of the corresponding district asking their consent to the exchange. The petition shall be sent to the 

Secretary of Education for his approval. The category of the 

225

T.§ 212-79 Ch. 13 

positions involved in the exchange shall be set forth therein. The petition submitted must be signed by the superintendents of schools, the school directors and the applicants. (2) It shall be an essential requirement for the approval of the exchange that the applicants be in active service or in condition to qualify immediately for the positions object of the exchange. (3) If any of the teachers affected by the exchange should ask for leave without pay or retirement with pension, or resign his position within the school year when the exchange is effected, said exchange may be declared null and void by the Secretary of Education. The teachers in question will be bound to occupy the original positions should it be proved that the exchange was not made. in good faith. (4) Exchanges of a temporary nature may not be made for a term exceeding one year. The teachers who wish to extend the exchange, once this term has elapsed, may only do so on a permanent basis. 

§ 212-80. Rural zone 

A teacher who in exchanging positions with another would have to teach in a rural zone, shall be entitled to reallocation to the urban zone of that school district after petition to that effect. 

(Form 401-R2.) § 212-81. Removal from employment by reason of elimination of positions Preferences 

When by reason of a reduction in the number of positions assigned to a school district, it is necessary to order the dismissal of one or more teachers, the more recently appointed teacher, within the category of position that is eliminated, shall be dismissed in each group, as follows: (1) Provisional teachers (2) Substitute teachers (3) Temporary teachers. (4) Probationary teachers (5) Permanent teachers. § 212-82. Listing of removed teachers

The names of the teachers removed from service by reason of the elimination of positions, shall be included in the corresponding lists as follows: 

226

Ch. T.18 § 212-85 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

(1) During the first school year that the teacher ceases in office. by elimination of positions, his name shall be included in order of preference in the lists corresponding to the school district where he applied. That is to say, his name shall be automatically included at the head of the group corresponding to him, as provided in sec. 

212-54 of this title. (2) The first year in which the teacher ceases in office through elimination of positions having elapsed, his name shall be included in the corresponding list and turn pursuant to the provisions of this division as long as he files a petition to that effect. § 212-83. Refusal of teaching offer

The fact that a teacher three times refuses offers for appointment, or fails to answer such offers within a term of 48 hours after having been notified, shall be sufficient cause to eliminate his candidacy in the school district where the offer was made. § 212-84. Reallocations; permanent or temporary

Reallocations of a permanent nature will be made within the same school district and category of position, from the rural to the urban zone, or transfers of a permanent nature from one school district to another at any time of the year with the exception of the tenth school month (May) only in cases of positions where there are permanent vacancies, or in new positions. The reallocations and transfers referred to in this section will be made on a temporary basis during the school month of July (before commencement of the school year) when the vacancies are to continue for the rest of the school year.

When a teacher accepts a transfer or a reallocation from one school district to another, he will not be entitled to another transfer or reallocation during the same school year. § 212-85. Transfer of probationary, substitute, temporary or provisional teachers

Teachers who receive new appointment at the beginning of the school year in August, under a probationary, substitute, temporary or provisional contract, will not be entitled to another appointment in another school district during the rest of the school year, provided: that once their turns arrive, they may be "transferred" or "reallocated" from one district to another at any time of the year, except in the 10th school month (May), as long as they are 227

T.18 212 Ch. 13 

going to occupy permanent positions in the school district where their permanent residence is located. 

§ 212-86. Issuance of probationary contracts 

At any time of the school year, probationary contracts will be issued to new candidates and to teachers in active service entitled thereto (following the order of preference in the lists) to fill vacancies in permanent positions as follows: (1) Upon being contracted (2) On a subsequent date to the contract: (A) In the school district where they work (B) In the school district where their permanent residence is located pursuant to the provisions of sec. 212-85 of this title. § 212-87. Transfer under same contract

When transfers are made from one school district to another, or reallocation within the same category of position and school district (from the rural to the urban zone) of teachers under a permanent or probationary contract, the incumbents shall occupy these positions with the same contract they had in their original position. (It is the action of transfer or reallocation which has a temporary or permanent nature according to the status of the vacancy.) 

§ 212-88. Effect of transfer on right of tenure 

A teacher under a permanent or probationary contract who pursuant to regulations goes to fill a new position, of a different category than the one he has as a substitute, temporary or provisional teacher, will retain his right of tenure, with respect to the original position.

The teacher who occupies a position under a permanent or probationary contract and accepts a position of a different category permanently, shall lose his right of tenure to the original position. § 212-89. Transfer of teacher under probationary contract

When a teacher, under a probationary contract, passes to occupy a position of the same category, from the rural zone to the urban zone or vice versa, or from one school district to another, his experience in both places shall be considered for the purpose of the probation period. 228

Ch. T.18 § 212-93 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS § 212-90. Probationary teacher taking leave 

Teachers with probationary contract who interrupt the probation period to go on leave without pay shall be issued the same contract as the former year; provided, that if they worked for at least 9 school months out of the 12 comprised in the probation period (per year) without counting the months of June and July, they will be issued the new contract to which they are entitled. § 212-91. Teacher on leave seeking appointment

When a permanent or probationary teacher on leave without pay wishes, prior to its expiration, to be considered for appointment in another position, he must ask for the consent of the Secretary of Education. If his petition (Form 401-R2) is approved, his name shall be included in the turn which corresponds to him in the list of eligibles of the school district where he lives and/or works. He shall be considered for appointment pursuant to the rules provided in this division. § 212-92. Health certificate of teacher receiving appointment

Any teacher (under new contract) who receives an appointment as such, shall submit a medical certificate (Form OP-12) issued by an authorized doctor, or by a medical official of the Health 

Department, within 10 days following the date he is contracted.

The examination in question will not be valid if made before six months from the date he qualifies for the position. This document will be sent to the Personnel Division through the office of the superintendent of schools. The Secretary of Education may require the teacher, besides, to submit a health certificate at any time he deems it convenient. § 212-93. Resignation; new application 

The teacher who resigns his position once the school month of August has commenced shall have to wait a month as of the date his resignation is accepted in order to receive another appointment. Upon filing a new application his name will be included in the list of eligibles according to the corresponding turn. 

Teachers under a permanent or probationary contract who file an application for transfer in the calling which is effective until 

February 28 or 29 of each school year and who resign their positions in May or June, will be entitled to have their names included 229

T.§ 212-93 Ch. 13 

in the list of eligibles, in the corresponding turn, as long as they notify the Personnel Division of their decision. § 212-94. Substitute teacher; extension of appointment; unsatisfactory work

When a teacher is granted leave and a substitute teacher is appointed for the first semester and the permanent teacher has his leave extended, or is reinstated in another position for the rest of the school year, the appointment of the substitute will be immediately extended to the second semester, as long as his work has been satisfactory.

When the work of the substitute teacher during the first semester has not been satisfactory, the superintendent of schools shall immediately report it to the Secretary of Education. The latter will notify in writing to the teacher in question, after investigation of the case, letting him know the reasons on which the report is based. In this case, a candidate appearing in the list of eligibles will be selected to fill the vacancy in the manner set forth in this division. Provided, that the teachers who were appointed for the first semester and were left out upon reinstatement of the holders of the positions which they held, will be considered for new appointment in their original turns as long as their work is classified as satisfactory. In case that the position in question is occupied by a provisional teacher, he may continue in that position as long as no candidates with regular certificates are available and as long as his work has been satisfactory. 

§ 212-95. Vacancies 

When during the first semester there occur vacancies for the rest of the school year, the appointments of those teachers with a regular license who have been contracted for the rest of the semester or for an indefinite term within the year, will be changed to these positions following the order of turns in the list of eligibles.

If the vacancies for the rest of the year should occur during the second school semester, the appointments of those teachers contracted for an indefinite term within that year shall be changed in the same manner. This will be so, in both cases, as long as there are available qualified candidates who accept the original vacancy for the remaining period of the semester in question. 

§ 212-96. Change of residence 

The teacher whose name appears in any list of the school dis- 230

Ch. 13

T.18 § 212-100 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

trict where he lives, and who transfers his residence to another school district wherein he has filed no application, shall be entitled, with the consent of the Secretary of Education, to transfer his application to the new school district sending the pertinent documents to the Personnel Division through the superintendent of schools and the school director. This application approved, his name shall be included in the list of candidates, in the corresponding group, and he shall be considered for appointment pursuant to this division. 

§ 212-97. Powers of the Secretary of Education 

No clause in this division shall be construed in the sense of limiting or rendering void the powers of the Secretary of Education to reject the appointment, transfer or reallocation of any teacher in furtherance of the public interest or other justified reasons. § 212-98. 

Elimination of names from list 

The Secretary of Education may eliminate any candidate from the lists of eligibles or provisional teachers, in furtherance of public interest or for any other justified reasons. § 212-99. 

Suspension of provisions

The provisions of this division shall be suspended by the Secretary of Education when the needs of the school service render necessary the appointment, transfer or reallocation of teachers (by direct appointment) to work in special educational services, or in furtherance of public interest or for justified reasons. § 212-100. Effectiveness

This division shall take effect as of the date of enactment [March 1, 1956].

§ 212-201. Application for leave 

Any teacher with a permanent or probationary appointment who wishes to retire from service on leave without pay, shall address the school director and the superintendent of schools. The principals, assistant superintendents, and zone supervisors shall address their communication to the Secretary of Education through the superintendent of schools. The curriculum technicians, the school superintendents, and the general supervisors will do so directly to the Secretary of Education. 

The application for leave without pay shall be made in writing and must include: 

(1) The reasons for the petition 

(2) The date on which the leave without pay is to be effective (3) The duration of the leave asked.

Any petition for sick or maternity leave must be accompanied by the corresponding medical certificate. 

Any petition to pursue higher studies connected with the teaching profession must indicate the program of studies which the applicant intends to follow. As soon as he enters the institution where he will pursue his studies, he will send the Secretary of Education an official record of the academic courses in which he has enrolled.

§ 212-202. Grounds for leave 

Leave will be granted only for the following reasons or the following grounds: 

(1) Applicant's illness; 232

Ch. T.18 § 212-205 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

(2) To pursue higher studies for professional improvement as teachers; (3) To accept appointment as substitute in a position of another category with the Department of Education; (4) To broaden his culture through travels abroad; (5) To accept an appointment in the faculty or the University of Puerto Rico, or another institution of university standing recognized by the University of Puerto Rico; (6) To appear as candidate to a position of popular election; provided, that if he wishes to defend his candidateship he must resign his position pursuant to section 52 of the School Act [18 

L.P.R.A. § 249]; 

(7) To discharge the duties of mayor or legislator; (8) To become a school director; (9) To enter into active service in the Armed Forces of the 

United States of America; (10) To married teachers, by reasons of pregnancy or childbirth, as hereinafter provided. § 212-203. Requirements to the petition for leave

Every petition for leave without pay must have the previous authorization of the Secretary of Education and must be filed at least 15 days before the date on which it shall become effective.

No teacher will abandon service on leave without pay until such leave has been duly approved, except in case of sudden sickness. § 212-204. Procedure after approval

The school director and the superintendent of schools are authorized to grant leave without pay to the teachers, after approval by the Secretary of Education, in those cases provided for in this subchapter, through communication addressed to the petitioning teacher, signed by both officials. The superintendent of schools must immediately send the original petition for leave together with copy of the letter he sends to the applicant and the corresponding notice of change (Form 409). In case of discrepancy between the school director and the superintendent of schools, the matter shall be submitted for final decision to the Secretary of Education. § 212-205. Length; time

Leaves without pay will be granted for a semester or for a school 233

T.§ 212-205 Ch. 13 

year; provided, that no leave of that kind will be granted for the first semester on a date subsequent to the termination of the first school month (August), unless there are available candidates who accept the position for the corresponding period of the first semester. Should there be no candidates available, leave will be granted for the rest of the school year. 

§ 212-206. Pregnancy 

Suspension of work

Any pregnant teacher must suspend her school work no later than on her eighth month of pregnancy, at her own initiative, that is to say, without need of any requirement on the part of the school authorities for such suspension. She must send to the Secretary of Education, through the office of the superintendent of schools, a medical certificate establishing the childbirth, within a term of 20 days after delivery. 

Failure to retire; false report

Whenever a pregnant teacher fails to retire from service within the stipulated period, or fails to submit the medical report within the term provided in sec. 212-206 of this title, or knowingly produces a false medical report, or in any other way should be guilty of transgression of these rules, it will be informed to the 

Secretary of Education, who in such cases shall take the pertinent measures pursuant to the provisions of sec. 212-216 of this title; provided, that when a pregnant teacher continues attending classes without taking into consideration the provisions of this division, the superintendent of schools and the school director will grant her leave without pay for the corresponding period as prescribed by regulation. § 212-208. 

Maternity leave

All maternity leaves shall be granted as follows: 

(1) For the rest of the first school semester when the teacher's 30 days after childbirth have elapsed no later than at the end of the first school month (August) pursuant to sec. 212-205 of this title. 

(2) For the rest of the school year in all other cases.

Amendments. Section was amended by Memorandum No. 7 

of August 3, 1954. § 212-209. Permanent appointment, effect of pregnancy

When a teacher, at the beginning of the school year (August), 234

Ch. T.18 § 212-214 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

is entitled to permanent appointment for a position of any category, and is in her seventh month of pregnancy, the appointment to which she is entitled shall be made and she will be granted leave without pay for the rest of the first school semester, pursuant to the provisions of sec. 212-205 of this title. § 212-210.- Permanent appointment of teacher on maternity leave When a teacher, upon commencement of the school year (August) is entitled to permanent appointment for a position of any category, but the 30 days after childbirth have not elapsed, the appointment to which she is entitled shall be made and she will be granted leave without pay for the rest of the first school semester; provided, that if the appointment would become effective after the school year has begun, said appointment shall be extended and she will be granted leave without pay for the rest of the school year. § 212-211. Prolonged illness

If on account of prolonged illness a teacher is not able to continue in the practice after the 20 days of absence with pay to which he is entitled are used up, he will be granted leave without pay for the rest of the semester in which he becomes ill, pursuant to sec. 212-205 of this title. § 212-212. Maximum leave

In no case shall leave be granted for a term exceeding two years except in those cases provided for in clauses (3), (7), (8), and (9) of sec. 212-202 of this title. § 212-213. Leave to study

Every teacher on leave to study shall submit an official transcript of the credits obtained at the end of the period during which the leave was granted. § 212-214. Sick leave; reinstatement

Every teacher who has been granted a sick leave shall submit, upon expiration thereof, a medical certificate establishing his satisfactory health condition in order to become reinstated to his school work. 235

T.§ 212-215 Ch. 13 EDUCATION - ― 

PUBLIC SCHOOLS § 212-215. Notice of intention to return 

Teachers on leave without pay during the first semester shall inform the superintendent of schools of their intention to return to service no later than at the end of the first week of the fifth school month (December). Those who are on leave during the second semester or for the school year will follow the same procedure; they will inform of their intention of returning to service no later than at the end of the first week of the 10th school month (May). 

The Secretary of Education, after investigation of the facts, may declare vacant the position of any teacher affected, who fails to comply with the provisions of this section. 

§ 212–216. Report of recovery from illness or finishing school 

When a teacher on leave without pay on account of sickness recovers his health or if on leave without pay to pursue higher studies, finishes school before he thought or is bound to abandon his studies for justified reasons, he must notify the superintendent of schools in order to retain the right to his position. The teacher so affected may seek reinstatement in the service, according to the provisions to that effect set forth in the Regulation for the Selection of Teachers [secs. 212-51 to 212-100 of this title]. 

§ 212-217. Leave to travel 

Every teacher on leave without pay to travel must submit a detailed report of his trip, explaining how this activity contributed to the broadening of his general culture. § 212-218. Non-compliance; declaration that position vacant 

The Secretary of Education, after investigation of the facts, may declare vacant the position of any teacher who has been granted leave without pay, if he has failed to comply with the terms thereof, or with the provisions of this division. 

§ 212-219. Other cases of leave 

Any other case of leave not provided for in this division shall be decided by the Secretary of Education according to the merits. thereof. 

§ 212-220. Effectiveness 

This division shall take effect on the date of its approval [July 1, 1954]. 236

§ 218a-1. Teacher defined 

The term "teacher" as defined in Act June 30, 1965, No. 117 [18 L.P.R.A. § 218a], will include all teaching personnel with a probationary or permanent contract, which embodies teachers in charge of education and special services directly related to educational work, as well as officials and employees performing technical work or school supervision and administration; all teaching personnel having probationary, permanent or substitute status under contract with the Board of Vocational Education, and those teachers under contract as such with other departments or agencies of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.

"During said period of eight weeks teachers will receive half-pay; "Teachers can be replaced in their positions at the end of the fourth week following childbirth, but not before; and "The Secretary of Education will promulgate the necessary rules and regulations to enforce these provisions." 

§ 218a-2. Maternity leave The period of rest authorized by said Act No. 117 [18 L.P.R.A. 

§ 218a] and by this subchapter will be known to all effects as "Maternity Leave". 

§ 218a-3. Application for leave 

The teacher will take the initiative in requesting a maternity leave, by submitting her application therefor to the superintendent of schools of her district immediately upon completion of her seventh month of pregnancy. The teacher will attach to her application a medical certificate stating both her condition and a prognosis of the approximate date of childbirth. 

§ 218a-4. Change report 

The superintendent of schools will, as soon as he receives a properly documented application for maternity leave, prepare and forward to the Division of Personnel of the Department of Education, together with the application and medical certificate, the respective change report Form 409R, making the leave effective for a period extending from the four weeks before the set date of childbirth to the four weeks following the same date. § 218a-5. Readjustment of change report

In case of prematurity of childbirth or of its occurrence on a date other than that medically predicted, the necessary readjustment will be made in the change report. § 218a-6. Leave without application

Whenever the superintendent of schools takes notion of a teacher showing ostensible signs of advanced pregnancy that makes her presence in the classroom or in any other work in her charge unbecoming, he shall request from her a medical certificate; and if the teacher would fail to comply with such request, the case will be referred to the Regional Director and finally to the Assistant 

Secretary of Personnel for proper action. 

Aug. 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 7 236.2

Ch. T.18 8 218a-10 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

§ 218a-7. Application through other officials

In the case of teachers who are not under the jurisdiction of a superintendent of schools, the application for maternity leave will be submitted to a regional director, chief of division, program, agency or department, with jurisdiction over the applying teacher; and any one of these officials receiving the application will transmit it to the Division of Personnel of the Department of Education in the same manner as provided with reference to the superintendent of schools, except when the teachers dealt with are employed by departments or agencies unrelated to the Department of Education. In this latter instance the application and the change report must be forwarded to the respective agency or department. 

§ 218a-8. Report on date of childbirth 

Every teacher on maternity leave shall submit through the superintendent of schools or through her immediate supervisor (regional director, chief of division, program, agency or department) not later than fifteen days after childbirth, a birth certificate issued either by the delivery physician or by the demographic registry. This document is absolutely necessary to determine the date of replacement of the teacher in her position, as well as to justify the half-salary payment for maternity leave. 

§ 218a-9. Computation of rest period 

Half-salary payment to teachers on maternity leave will be computed on the basis of either school month or calendar month, in conformity with whichever way the teacher receives payment of her salary. Whenever any part of the period of maternity leave coincides with the month of annual vacation leave which all teachers are by law entitled to, those teachers on said maternity leave shall not receive during such period of coincidence other compensation than that pertaining to vacation leave while receiving payment resulting therefrom. 

§ 218a-10. Replacement and leave extension 

Teachers on maternity leave will have the right of replacement and will be replaced in the position they held when they were granted such leave, as soon as the four-week rest period following childbirth has elapsed, provided they have submitted in due time the document referred to in section 218a-8 of this title. However, any teacher who would desire to continue out of active service, Aug. 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 7 236.3

T.§ 218a-10 Ch. 13 

EDUCATION-PUBLIC SCHOOLS 

for the remaining of the school semester or year, as the case may be, can do so by submitting to the superintendent of schools or to her immediate supervisor a written application for proper leave, specifically stating therein her relinquishment of the right to replacement granted by law. 

§ 218a-11. Appointments to fill vacancies 

Vacancies that occur as a result of maternity leave or of any leave extension will be covered by the appointment of teachers for an indeterminate period within the school year, according to the needs of the service. Candidates for said appointments will be selected from the list of eligibles established under the provisions of the Rules and Regulations for the Selection, Transfer and Re assignment of Teachers. 

§ 218a-12. Extension of appointment of substitute teacher 

Whenever an extension leave is granted to a teacher on maternity leave, her substitute teacher's appointment shall immediately be also extended, provided the latter has performed satisfactory work. If the substitute teacher has not performed satisfactory work, the superintendent of schools will report the case to the Secretary of Education immediately. Under the circumstances a candidate to fill the vacancy shall be selected from the list of eligibles, following the procedure prescribed by rules and regulations. Substitute teachers who become unemployed as a result of the replacement of incumbent teachers will be considered for new satisfactory work. 

§ 218a-13. Effectiveness 

This subchapter shall take effect 30 days after the filing of an original and two copies of its Spanish and English texts in the office of the Secretary of State of Puerto Rico, pursuant to the provisions of Act No. 112 of June 30, 1957, as amended [3 L.P.R.A. 

§ 1041 et seq.].

§ 249-1. Preamble 

The school is nonpartisan and shall be free from any party or sectarian influence. It shall be the duty of the teachers to see that the most strict fulfillment of this neutrality is observed in the schools under their supervision.

Source. §§ 249-1 to 249-9: Rules and regulations of the 

Department of Education, app. by the Secretary of Education,

Vol. I, pp. 8 to 11, Regulation of teachers in political campaigns, promulgated Oct. 13, 1944, eff. upon promulgation. 

Filed with Secretary of State, Sept. 28, 1957; File No. 344.

Authority. Act Mar. 12, 1903, p. 60, § 2; 18 L.P.R.A. § 31. 

Repeals. Section 8 of regulation repealed regulation of 

Nov. 10, 1939, as amended Sept. 20, 1944, and all rules, provisions or orders in conflict with this regulation. 

§ 249-2. General prohibition 

The teachers in active service, as officials or public employees, pursuant to section 52 of the Compiled School Law [18 L.P.R.A. 

§ 249], shall not take part in any way in the political campaigns. 

§ 249-3. Active duty 

For the purpose of this subchapter, every teacher practicing in the public schools, under contract or appointment duly signed by the Secretary of Education, shall be considered to be on active duty. § 249-4. Meaning of "teacher"

The term "teacher", for the purposes of this subchapter, shall not only comprise the teachers practicing in the public schools, properly speaking, but also all the officials appointed by the school system for administrative or technical positions under the juris diction of the Secretary of Education. 

§ 249-5. Political activities 

It shall be understood by political campaign, every effort and every act directed to encourage, aid or help the interests of 237

T.18 249 Ch. 13 

specific political parties or specific group or candidacy of a political nature, that is: 

(1) Every form of oral or written propaganda. 

(2) The recruiting, registration and instruction of the voters. (3) Directly or indirectly soliciting contributions or aid of any kind to defray campaigns or political nominations. (4) Making use of the influence or official authority with the purpose of hindering an election or producing a desired effect thereon. (5) Directly or indirectly promising employment, work, retribution or other benefit as recompense for political activities in favor or against any candidate or political party. (6) Depriving or threatening to deprive or influence so that any person may be deprived of employment for reasons of political affiliation. (7) Using political badges in any way within the schoolrooms, offices and school grounds. (8) Being a part of the directing committee of any political party. (9) Taking active part in meetings, conventions, boards, assemblies or other political acts, as delegate, assessor, official or speaker or in any other capacity that implies active participation therein; however, it being understood, that the presence of the teachers in such places, as mere spectators, shall not constitute a violation of this subchapter. (10) Using the schoolrooms, school lunch rooms and the school property in general, in any way, for political purposes. (11) Any other means of propaganda for the benefit of a specific political party or that might have as an object the opposition of candidates, programs or political party ideals. 

§ 249-6. Resignation 

Every teacher in active service shall present his resignation, through precept of the law, in any of the following cases: (1) When nominated for an electoral public office and wishes to defend his candidacy; (2) When for any other reason he wishes to take active part in political campaigns. 

§ 249-7. Rights of teachers 

Nothing contained in this subchapter shall be construed in the sense of 238

Ch. T.18 § 249-9 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

(1) Preventing teachers in the fulfillment of their educational mission to impart to their students such teachings inherent to the civic culture and to the proper exercise of citizenship in all its forms, as long as said teachings are developed within a high educational level and in keeping with the courses and programs of study duly authorized to that effect; (2) Limiting teachers in any way in the free calling of their political ideas, not hindering them in offering their opinions in the exercise of the rights and privileges guaranteed by the Constitution and the laws, as long as their conduct in such cases is tempered to the most perfect licitness or lawfulness and does not interfere with the principle of school neutrality; (3) Prohibiting teachers in active service from acting as inspectors and secretaries in the polls, where the persons doing so shall be in the role of public officials appointed by competent authority; however, it being understood, that the teachers shall not be permitted to act as challengers or observers at the polls, since these officers are politically designated and their fulfillment requires essential party activity; (4) Restraining the right of teachers to voluntarily contribute for the support of any political party, as long as said contribution is not solicited nor given within the schoolrooms, offices or school grounds. 

§ 249-8. Complaint 

Every dispute, denunciation or complaint which does not originate from the school directors or officials of the Department of 

Education, brought before the Secretary, in relation to essential facts of transgression to these rules, shall be presented in writing and under oath and shall contain a clear, complete and specific statement of such facts, and the pertinent evidence which in each case shall be examined and considered. $ 249-9. Publication; effectiveness

This subchapter shall be published in the Spanish and English language, pursuant to the provisions of the law, and shall become effective on the date of its promulgation [Oct. 13, 1944].

§ 261-40. Definition of terms 

For the purposes of this subchapter, the following terms are defined: 

(1) "Secretary" -The Secretary of Public Education of Puerto 

Rico. 

(2) "Law" Law No. 94 of June 21, 1955 (Law for the Certi fication of Teachers) [18 L.P.R.A. § 260 et seq.]. 

(3) "Rules and regulations” — The present subchapter. (4) "Teacher" 

Supervisory, technical and teaching personnel in the school system. This definition excludes personnel in the competitive and noncompetitive services which the Office of Personnel of the Commonwealth regulates and in the exempt non-teaching services. (5) "Teacher's certificate" - A document issued by the Secretary of Education authorizing the holder to perform the technical or teaching tasks in the category and for the period of time specified in the same. (6) "Provisional teacher's certificate" - A document authorizing the holder on a temporary and transitory basis to perform the teaching tasks, although he does not meet the requirements with respect to academic preparation or experience or both as required by law and by this subchapter. (7) "Accredited" - Refers to Normal Schools, Colleges of Education, Colleges of Liberal Arts, Colleges of Science, Faculties of Social Sciences, Faculties of Humanities, or of Natural Sciences and universities accredited by the University of Puerto Rico, or by regional or professional associations of the United States of America, established for the official accreditation of university studies. (8) "Accredited private school" Elementary, intermediate, or 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 

240

Ch. 13

T.18 § 261-40 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

high schools accredited by the Secretary, whose courses receive academic credit equivalent to that given by public schools. (9) "Elementary school" - Includes grades from the first to the sixth. (10) "Secondary school" Comprises the junior high school; consisting of grades seven, eight, and nine, and the high school, consisting of grades ten, eleven, and twelve. (11) "Major" The combination of university courses in a definite field of learning, in which the student has obtained the minimum number of credits required for that major by the institution which confers the degree or diploma. 

(12) "Minor" The combination of university courses in a definite field of learning in which the student has obtained the minimum number of credits required for that minor by the institution which confers the degree or diploma. 

(13) "Field of specialization" The series of pertinent or related courses up to the minimum number of credits required for that field of specialization by the institution conferring the degree or diploma. (14) "Equivalent of practice teaching" 

Satisfactory experience as a teacher for a period of two years in the regular program of the public schools or of the accredited private schools of Puerto Rico, or in accredited schools of the United States of America will be considered equivalent to the course in practice teaching required by accredited colleges and universities. (15) "Year of experience" - Eight months of satisfactory teaching experience within a given school year, or ten months of satisfactory teaching experience in different school years; in neither case the school months of June and July will be counted.

Application for and issuing of teachers' certificates 

According to art. 7 of the law [18 L.P.R.A. § 266], the Secretary will not make or approve appointments of teachers for the public or accredited private schools who do not hold a valid teacher's certificate for the category involved. (1) Every applicant for any teacher's certificate described in this subchapter will submit the following to the Secretary: (A) An application for a teacher's certificate, using the form prescribed by the Secretary. (B) A transcript or official certification of the applicant's college credits. (C) A birth certificate. (D) A health certificate certifying the applicant's satisfactory condition to work as a teacher, and issued within three months of the date of application for the teacher's certificate, using the official form of the Department of Public Education.

applicants meeting the general requirements established by law and such additional requirements as are established by this subchapter.

(4) The Secretary may issue provisional certificates, valid for the school year in which they are issued and for the duration of the appointment, to teachers who do not meet the requirements for certificates listed in this subchapter. In all cases a high school diploma will be the minimum requirement for a provisional certificate. The provisional certificate will be issued effective the day the teacher takes up the duties of the position. § 261-44. General provisions 

(a) College credits, courses, diplomas and degrees required by this subchapter for the various certificates must have been taken at accredited colleges, as set forth in sec. 261-40 of this title. (b) College credits and courses required by this subchapter for the various certificates must have been taken with a minimum grade index of 2.00, equivalent to a general average of “C”. § 261-45. EDUCATION-PUBLIC SCHOOLS § 297b-1. Delegation Rule 1. (a) The Secretary of Education hereby delegates to the Assistant Secretary of Personnel of the Department of Education the function of contracting services bound by this subchapter. (b) The Assistant Secretary of Personnel may in turn delegate said functions to other Department officials.

Source. Sections 297b-1 to 297b-10: Regulations Governing Contracts for Additional Service to be Rendered by Government Officials and Employees Outside of Their Regular Work ing Hours or During Their Vacation Leaves, app. by the

Authority. Act June 25, 1965, No. 90, p. 226; 18 L.P.R.A. 

§ 297b. 

Purpose. Regulation File Nos. 1133 and 1147, set out in this subchapter, contained the following note: "The present regulations are promulgated by the Secretary of Education with the purpose of regulating the employment personnel working for the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or its political subdivisions to render additional services as teachers or in any other capacity, outside of their regular working hours or during their vacation leaves in educational programs financed totally or partially by Federal funds or by grants made by foundations or any other such entities for educational purposes." 

§ 297b-2. Requirements 

Rule 2. (a) Projects requiring services bound by this subchapter must have the approval of the Secretary of Education prior to the engagement of any personnel to render such services. (b) Applicants for teaching positions under any of the programs covered by this subchapter must possess a teacher's certificate issued by the Secretary of Education in accordance with the Law for the Certification of Teachers [18 L.P.R.A. §§ 260 to 273] or must fulfill the necessary requirements to obtain such a certificate. 

Rule 3. Candidates for positions other than teaching must fulfill the requirements for similar positions or their equivalents in the Department of Education. 

§ 297b-3. Application 

Rule 4. (a) Candidates for positions covered by this subchapter must fill in and submit Application Form (401-R3) to the Super- March 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 3 

254

Ch. T.18 § 297b-5 

TEACHERS' QUALIFICATIONS 

intendent of Schools of the district in which the project is in effect or directly to the Assistant Secretary of Personnel in case of projects ascribed to the Central Office of the Department of Education. (b) In case the applicant is a teacher or an employee of the Department of Education he must also submit the form Authorization for Extra Employment duly filled in and signed by the corresponding official. (c) Candidates who are employees of other agencies must likewise accompany their application with the form Authorization for Extra Employment duly filled in and signed by the head of the corresponding agency. 

Rule 5. Order of applications. (a) The school superintendents will set up a roster of applicants in their respective districts on the basis of ability, experience and date of application in said order. (b) The Assistant Secretary of Personnel will likewise set up a roster of applicants for projects ascribed to the Central Office of the Department of Education. 

(c) Evaluation of the ability and experience of applicants will be made by the Superintendent of Schools or the Assistant Secretary of Personnel as the case may be. 

§ 297b-4. Contracts 

Rule 6. (a) Contracts will be drawn up only on the basis of rosters of applicants eligible for employment in each specific project and for the duration of that project, on the recommendation of the Superintendent of Schools in the case of district projects or of the Assistant Secretary of Personnel in the case of projects for the 

Central Office. 

(b) No person shall be employed for consecutive periods unless the roster of eligible candidates is exhausted in the corresponding district or at the Central Office. 

§ 297b-5. Compensation and other stipulations 

Rule 7. Compensation on each individual contract shall be as authorized by the corresponding Federal agency or foundation, in default thereof, the compensation shall be fixed by the Department for the employment of personnel payable from federal funds. 

Rule 8. No leave of absence for vacation or sickness under the provisions of this subchapter.

Rule 9. No payment will be made for services not rendered; therefore, all absences shall be deducted from salary agreed upon. 

Rule 10. Contracts for services to be rendered outside of regular working hours, except in the case of teachers shall be subject to the approval of the Bureau of the Budget as specified by law. The procedure to be followed for such approval shall be by mutual agreement of the Bureau of the Budget and the Department of Education.

§ 297b-6. Rule of conduct 

Rule 11. The Secretary of Education may abrogate any contract for services covered by this subchapter before its termination because of improper conduct or inefficiency on the part of the employee. 

§ 297b-7. Termination of contract 

Rule 12. (a) Any teacher or employee who wants to rescind his contract before its termination may do so by giving the Secretary of Education notice 5 days in advance of cancellation of the contract. (b) The Secretary of Education may for any reason abrogate a contract before its termination by giving notice 5 days in advance. 

In such case compensation shall cease on the date of termination. § 297b-8. Appointment of unemployed personnel 

Rule 13. (a) No contract for services bound by this subchapter shall be drawn as long as there is qualified unemployed personnel willing to serve as prescribed by law No. 90 of June 25, 1965 [18

L.P.R.A. § 297b] as amended. 

(b) For appointment of qualified unemployed personnel rosters will be set up by the Superintendents of Schools or by the Assistant 

Secretary of Personnel as specified in Rule 4 of section 297b-3 of this subchapter. (c) The appointment of unemployed personnel shall be done in compliance with the laws and regulations governing employment with the Government of Puerto Rico.

299-4. Remittances to Department of Education § 299-1. Remittance of deductible sums 

The total amount of the deductible sums of the teacher's salary shall be remitted immediately on effecting the deductions. These remittances shall be accompanied by a report indicating the town, name of the teacher, the class, the number and dates of the absences and the deducted amount. 

Source. §§ 299-1 to 299-4: Rules and regulations of the

§ 299-2. Checks or money orders 

The checks, which shall be certified, or the money orders, covering the exact value of the remittances, shall be made payable to the Secretary of the Treasury of Puerto Rico and not to the Secre tary of Education. 

§ 299-3. Basis of deduction; violations 

Every deduction shall be carried out on the basis of the full salary and not on the net salary. The deductions for pensions shall form part of the full salary. Any money order or check issued in violation of these rules shall be immediately returned to be corrected. 

§ 299-4. Remittances to Department of Education 

The remittances shall be sent directly to the Department of 

Education.

331-44. Amendment § 331-1. Introduction 

In accordance with section 12, clause (b) of Act No. 218, approved May 6, 1951 [18 L.P.R.A. § 331], which provides that the 

Retirement Board for the School Teachers of Puerto Rico shall have the power: 1962 Vol. 1, No. 3 257

T.§ 331-1 Ch. 17 

"To approve Regulations for the proper enforcement of this Act which after having been approved by the Governor of Puerto Rico and promulgated by the Retirement Board, shall have the force of law;" and for the purpose of clarifying and establishing the provisions of this Act, as well as facilitating the functioning of the system, the Teachers' Retirement Board does hereby approve the following regulations which shall take effect and shall have the force of law after having been approved by the Governor and promul gated by the Teachers' Retirement Board. 

Source. §§ 331-1 to 331-44: Regulations of the Teachers' 

Annuity and Pension System, promulgated by Teachers Retirement Board, May 17, 1956; app. by Governor, June 5, 1956, eff. June 5, 1956; amended Dec. 6, 1957, and Feb. 12, 1959. Filed with Secretary of State, April 21, 1959; File No. 565.

§ 331-2. Definitions 

The following words and phrases used in this subchapter shall have the meaning set forth below, unless another meaning is clearly expressed in their context: (1) "Act" shall mean Act No. 218, approved May 6, 1951, as amended [18 L.P.R.A. §§ 321–366]. 

(2) "Director of the system" shall mean the executive secretary of the Board. (3) "Mortality table" shall mean the table of mortality standard adopted by the Teachers' Retirement Board to be used for the computation of annuity values, actuarial evaluations or cost determinations of the system in accordance with the recommendations of the actuary. (4) "Accumulated assessments" shall mean the sum total of amounts deducted from the salaries of the teachers, or otherwise contributed by them and entered into the fund as contributions to the system. (5) "Age" shall mean age at last birthday. (6) "Military service" or service in the "Armed Forces" shall mean the services in the United States Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines or Coast Guard or in any women's auxiliary thereof. 1962 Vol. 1, No. 3 258

Ch. T.1-8 § 331-4 

TEACHERS' BENEFITS 

())) (7) "Fiscal year" shall mean the period from July 1, of one year to June 30th of the next following. (8) "Borrowing capacity" shall mean that amount which the teacher could pay for in loans with 50% of his net salary after lawful deductions provided for by law. (9) "Superseded fund" shall mean all pension funds as provided for by the different pension laws enumerated in Act No. 218 

of 1951 [18 L.P.R.A. §§ 321-366]. 

(10) "Actuarial value" shall mean: The value, at a given moment, of probable future benefits, computed in accordance with the methods prescribed by the Act and with the actuarial indexes in force for the system. 

§ 331-3. Administration generally The Annuity and Pension Fund for the School Teachers of 

Puerto Rico, created by Act Number 218 of 1951, as amended [18 L.P.R.A. §§ 321–366], shall be considered a trust to be administered and maintained exclusively for the benefit of the members of the system, in accordance with the provisions of the laws of Puerto Rico. The system established by this Act for the administration and operation of the Annuity and Pension Fund shall be known as "The Annuity and Pension System for the Teachers of 

Puerto Rico".

The general responsibility for the proper and effective operation of the system and for the enforcement of the provisions of the Retirement Act shall be vested in the Board. 

All assets acquired by the system, of every kind and character whatsoever, including the funds and assets of the Pension Fund for the Teachers of Puerto Rico, created by Act Number 161, approved May 10, 1945, shall be held in the name of the Teachers' 

Annuity and Pension System, and all the investments or expenses made by the system shall be made in the name of the system and shall be registered under said name. 

§ 331-4. Office The Secretary of Education shall provide suitable quarters for the meetings of the Board and for the office of the system. All accounts, records, files, books, reports, correspondence, and other data, or documents reflecting the operations of the system and belonging to the same, other than cash, securities, or other items which, by law or by the rules of the Board, are to be in the cus- 259

T.§ 331-4 Ch. 17 

tody of the Secretary of the Treasury, shall be kept in the office of the system. 

§ 331-5. Officers and their duties (a) Secretary of the Treasury. The Secretary of the Treasury of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico shall be the official custodian of the cash and securities belonging to the system, and shall provide adequate deposit facilities for their preservation and safekeeping. He shall receive from the executive secretary all monies received at the office of the system and all other monies paid or transferred to the system, including principal and interest payments not obtainable through salary deductions, and shall deposit the same in a special trust fund maintained in the name of the system. He shall make payments from that fund for the several purposes specified in the Act governing the system upon warrant duly certified by the executive secretary. 

Likewise, the Secretary of the Treasury shall be the financial counsellor of the Board and as such shall give his advice on everything related to the investments to be made by the system. 

He shall also execute the purchase of stocks or bonds as authorized by the Board.

He shall submit to the Board a quarterly report on the investment transactions of the system as well as the recommendations which he deems advisable for the better administration of the funds of the system.

The Secretary of the Treasury shall also submit any other financial statements which the Board may request from time to time. 

(b) Secretary of Justice. The Secretary of Justice shall be the legal counsel and as such shall perform his duties as provided for in the Constitution and laws of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. 

Subject to the functions pertaining to the Secretary of Justice, the Retirement Board may employ special counsel from time to time as necessary for the better operation of the system. (c) Executive secretary. (1) The executive secretary shall serve as secretary of the Retirement Board as well as director of the system. In the capacity of secretary of the Retirement Board he shall have the following duties: (A) Give timely notice, as ordered by the president, of each meeting of the Board, including an agenda showing the nature 260

(B) Serve as secretary of the committees created or authorized by the Board, attend the meetings of these committees and keep a record of the proceedings thereof. § 331-6. Oath 

Each person becoming a member of the Board, whether exofficio, appointed, or by representation, shall take a written oath before the Secretary of State of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico in the sense that he will administer, diligently and honestly, the affairs of his office as a member thereof and that he will not knowingly violate or wilfully permit to be violated any of the provisions of the Act or any of the bylaws which govern the operations of the system. Said oath shall be subscribed by the person taking it and acknowledged before the aforesaid official. A person

shall be considered to qualify as member of the Board after taking said oath and the same has been filed as herein provided. 

§ 331-7. Committees 

The Board may create special committees for the purpose of making studies, investigations or performing special functions in connection with the operation of the system. The work of these committees shall be exclusively that assigned by the Board at the time the committees are created. 

§ 331-8. Records, accounts, files, statistics 

The system shall have the records, accounts, files and statistics necessary to fulfill the requirements of the law and to assure the proper operation of the system. These documents shall be kept in such a form as to provide rapid, complete, and exact information in relation to the economic conditions, status of members and such references corresponding to the members of the system as shall be necessary for the periodic analyses on the result of operations, for actuarial evaluations, and for other surveys. 

A separate account shall be kept for each member of the system showing the amount of assessments, interest, credits and any other contributions made by the teacher to the system or to any superseded fund. These accounts shall, at all times, reflect all the contributions and interest accredited to the members of the system. 

§ 331-9. Coordination of records and accounts 

All the records and the methods of administrative procedures shall be integrated, as far as possible, to the functions, records, and methods of procedure of the Department of Education and other agencies of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico whenever possible.

The books and accounts shall be coordinated to the extent practicable with the accounts kept by the Secretary of the Treasury of Puerto Rico, giving effect to the specific requirements of the law. and to the rules and procedures governing the administration of the office of the Secretary of the Treasury. 

§ 331-10. Financial statements and reports 

The Board shall submit to the Governor and to the Legislature of Puerto Rico not later than November the 1st of each year, an annual report covering the operations for the preceding fiscal year. 263

T.§ 331-11 

Ch. 17

 § 331-11. Contracts and agreements 

In accordance with the authorization received from the Board in each case, the executive secretary shall settle and prepare for the Board all the contracts or agreements which represent liabilities for the system. 

§ 331-12. Deposit of funds 

All the monies which enter into the system shall be accredited to the system on the books of the Secretary of the Treasury. Any direct payments made by the teachers to the system for contributions covering services rendered in the Teachers Association of Puerto Rico, in federal agencies, military service, service in the states or territories of the United States, or other types of service for which direct contributions are required, shall be deposited with the Secretary of the Treasury within twenty-four hours following the receipt of such payments in the office of the system. 

§ 331-13. Members of the system 

The following persons shall or may become members of the system and shall be subject to all the provisions of the law applicable thereto. (1) Teachers in active service in the public schools of Puerto Rico. (2) Certified teachers holding positions as employees of the system. (3) Pensioned or retired teachers. (4) The members of the Legislative Assembly having valid licenses to practice the teaching profession. (5) Teacher-members of the system who are transferred to positions of an administrative character in the Department of Education, or in any department of public education of the municipalities of Puerto Rico, or in any institution of public education of the government except in the University of Puerto Rico, provided they state their intention to continue subject to this Act by letter addressed to the Retirement Board. (6) Teachers employed by the Teachers Association of Puerto

Rico and in private schools of the island, whose curriculum has been approved by the Department of Education, provided they ask for it, in writing, to the Board. (7) Teachers on approved leave of absence with or without pay, or receiving scholarships to study for professional improvement. 264

Ch. T.18 § 331-15
