§ 331-14. Pensioners re-entering service 

Life annuity payments shall be suspended to any former teacher who had been granted a life annuity or pension under this Act or under any other Teachers' Pension Law in force in Puerto Rico prior to July 1st, 1951, holding a position for which he receives payment, in the Government of Puerto Rico, or in any of its agencies, instrumentalities, political sub-divisions, accredited private schools, in the Teachers Association of Puerto Rico, or as soon as he begins to receive payment for services rendered to the Government of Puerto Rico, or in any of its agencies, instrumentalities or political sub-divisions after the effective date of retirement. 

Such life annuity payments shall be suspended during the period for which he is earning salary or compensation; provided that those teachers pensioned under laws prior to July 1951 who were working as of June 30 of that year, and continued working without interruption in governmental agencies or in accredited private schools, or in the Teachers Association of Puerto Rico shall keep the rights which they had acquired by the provisions of the laws under which they were pensioned. No service credit shall be granted to said teacher for the period of reemployment, nor shall he be allowed to make any contribution to the system during that period of reemployment. He is not eligible either to receive personal or mortgage loans. Upon termination of employment life annuity payments shall be resumed at the rate paid at the time the teacher reentered service, to take effect at the end of the month following the date of termination.

In case the teacher dies before repaying the amount due or any other overpayment, said amount shall be deducted from the insurance benefits payable to his beneficiaries.

Amendments. Section was amended by amendment approved by Governor February 12, 1959. 

§ 331-15. Financing the system 

Each teacher participating in the system shall contribute an amount equal to 7 percent of each monthly salary earned, which amount shall accrue to his credit in an individual account including also the contributions accumulated in the previous pension fund. These amounts shall draw an interest as provided for in sections 19 (a), 31, and 33 of the Act [18 L.P.R.A. §§ 338, 350, 352]. 265

T.§ 331-15 

Ch. 17

Codification. The Spanish and English texts of this section differ. The Spanish text contains the following additional sentence: "The rate of interest upon the amount contributed shall be that which is determined by the Board". 

§ 331-16. Employer's contributions The Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico shall con tribute, for services rendered thereto, an amount equal to 6 percent of each salary paid. Moreover, the Government of the Commonwealth shall contribute any other additional sums necessary to pay its proportionate share of any other benefit to be granted for services rendered, and the accrued assets for services rendered by the teachers prior to July 1, 1951, in accordance with actuarial determinations. These benefits shall consist of the amounts covering disability annuities, death benefits, widow's annuities, children's annuities and administrative expenses.

The other employers shall contribute an amount equal to that contributed by the teacher-member of the system, which shall be paid concurrently with the payment of salaries. This contribution shall never be lower than that corresponding to a public school teacher of the same category. 

§ 331-17. Service credit 

Service in the public schools

Credit shall be granted to any teacher becoming a member of the system as of July 1, 1951 or at any subsequent date for all prior teaching service in the public schools of Puerto Rico. 

Service for which a member received a refund of contributions from this or from any other superseded pension fund shall be recognized as creditable service after a year has elapsed since repayment was made to the system of said refund or refunds, plus an interest of 4 percent per annum covering the period from the date of refund to the date of reinstatement. Said repayment shall be made within a period of three years from the date the application thereto was accepted and the same shall be paid in full before credit can be granted for the services rendered during the periods covered by the refunded contributions. 

§ 331-18. Period of service 

Members shall receive retirement credit for each full year of service as defined below. Any period of service which is less than a full year shall be considered upon computing the retirement annuity and a proportionate credit shall be granted for each fractional period of service. 266

§ 331-19. 

Service in private schools or in the Teachers Association

Service in the Teachers Association of Puerto Rico, or as a teacher in the private schools of Puerto Rico, accredited and subject to inspection by the Department of Education of Puerto Rico, shall be credited, under the following conditions, as though the service was rendered in the public schools of Puerto Rico: (1) Service rendered prior to July 1, 1951. Such services rendered by teachers, now in active service, shall be credited, as of the date on which the Act shall become effective, upon application thereto by the teacher and payment of contributions in amounts equal to those paid by other members of the system plus an interest of 4 percent per annum beginning as of July 1, 1951. These amounts shall be paid in periods not greater than three years. 

In case the teacher is an employee of the Teachers Association of Puerto Rico, the latter shall also pay a contribution equal to 267

EDUCATION — - PUBLIC SCHOOLS 

the actuarial value of the credits for prior service, which will not impair the economic solvency of the fund. (2) Service subsequent to July 1, 1951. Such services shall be creditable upon application presented by the teacher to the Retirement Board within a period of three months after date or appointment as teacher. The Teachers Association or the private school shall also sign a written agreement accepting the obligations set forth in this Act, and agreeing to make the requested contribution in the time and manner prescribed by the Board, as follows: The teacher shall contribute to the system an amount equal to 7 percent of his current salary, which amount shall not be lower than the one corresponding to a teacher of the same category in the public schools. The Teachers Association, or the private school, shall contribute an amount equal to that contributed by the teacher. 

The contributions of the teacher and the employer shall be remitted by the latter to the office of the system within a period of thirty (30) days following the close of the pay period for which the contributions were due and payable. In the event remittance of such contributions is not made the Board shall consider this failure as a breach of contract. 

§ 331-20. 

Credit for military service

Service in the armed forces of the United States shall be creditable in the case of any teacher, upon his discharge from military service and reinstatement into the service of the public schools of Puerto Rico provided that (1) the teacher applies for such credit; (2) the teacher contributes for the period of military service on the basis of the rate of contribution and the salary in effect on the date he entered military service; (3) the teacher submits to the system a certified copy of his enlistment and discharge or a certificate of service. 

§ 331-21. Methods and procedures for filing claims applications 

Filing of 

Every person who applies for benefits shall file his application as soon as he becomes eligible to receive benefits. (1) Disability annuity. The application for disability annuity shall be filed as soon as possible after the occurrence of disability. 

Should the application be approved, the annuity payments shall begin to accrue as of the date of termination of compensable service. If the application for disability annuity is not filed within the 268

Ch. 17

T.18 § 331-21 

TEACHERS' BENEFITS 

60 days following the date of termination of compensable service, the annuity payments shall begin to accrue 60 days prior to the date on which application was filed. 

Any member filing an application for disability annuity shall furnish the system a complete description and the diagnosis of the disability made by the physician or physicians who attended him upon the occurrence of said disability. The teacher eligible to receive a disability annuity shall be the one whose incapacity is of such a nature as to prevent him from performing adequately the teaching duties he used to perform regularly. 

Should it be alleged that the disability occurred due to occupational causes, and the teacher does not have five years of accredited service he must submit a complete statement of all the facts to support such allegation, including a report from the superintendent of schools showing a complete description of the conditions which caused said incapacity.

The executive secretary shall order the physician appointed by the Board to make a physical examination of the teacher applying for a disability annuity, and submit a report which shall be considered by the Board. 

Every teacher receiving a disability annuity shall be examined periodically by the physician designated by the Board during the first five years in which the annuity is in effect, and thereafter, at least once every three years. No medical examinations shall be made after the teacher attains the age of 55. When the physician certifies that the incapacity is total and permanent, the periodical medical examinations shall be practiced subject to the Board's discretion. If the examination reveals, to the satisfaction of the Board, that the teacher is no longer disabled and can resume work, the payment of the disability annuity shall terminate after a period of six months reckoning from the date of the medical examination which revealed that the teacher had recovered from his incapacity. 

Periodic checks shall be made on the activities of teachers retired due to disability. If such a teacher is found to be working in any remunerated position, and that this remuneration exceeds the amount of the disability annuity, the teacher will cease to receive annuity payments from the date he started working. (2) Widow's annuity. The widow of a retired teacher who applies for a widow's annuity shall file in addition to the application, proof of her husband's death consisting of a death certificate and documental evidence of her marriage to the deceased member. 269

T.§ 331-21 

Ch. 17

The annuity in such a case shall begin to accrue as of the date the annuity payments on behalf of the teacher ceased, irrespective of the date on which the application was filed. 

The system shall investigate periodically the status of the widow. 

If the widow remarries the annuity shall terminate as of the date of remarriage, and a pro rata amount of the last month's payment shall be given to the widow. Such termination shall be permanent and shall not be affected by any subsequent change in the marital status of the widow. (3) Children's annuity. Application for a child's annuity shall be filed by the surviving parent as the natural guardian of such child, unless a legal guardian has been appointed. If none of the parents survives, the application shall be filed by a court of justice. Payment of the children's annuity shall be made to the surviving parent or to the legal guardian.

The application for annuity to minor children shall be accompanied by a death certificate of the deceased member, a birth certificate of each child who is to partake of the benefits, and proof of the appointment of the guardian.

The proportion of the benefit pertaining to each minor child shall terminate when the child attains the age of 18. The proportion of the benefit applicable to the child for the month in which he attains said age shall consist of the full benefit payment for that proportion of the month prior to the child's birthday. Benefit payments for succeeding months, until another child attains the age of 18, shall consist of the original amount of the annuity less the proportions applicable to the children who have attained majority since the benefit was originally granted. (4) Death benefit. The application for such death benefit shall be filed by the designated beneficiaries of the member. Said beneficiaries must have been designated by the member on a form supplied by the executive secretary and filed in the system. If no such designation has been filed, the legal heirs of the deceased member shall file an application for the benefit, to which they shall attach evidence of such relationship. All applications shall be accompanied by proof of the death consisting of a death certificate. 

At the death of a retired teacher, the annuity payment corresponding to the month in which said teacher died, shall be paid in full to his beneficiaries. Said payments shall cease the month following the date on which death occurred but the beneficiaries of the deceased teacher shall receive the excess, if any of the total 270

Ch. T.18 § 331-23 

TEACHERS' BENEFITS 

contributions made by the teacher, after a deduction is made of annuity payments made by the system, and in no case shall they receive less than $300 in only one payment. (5) Refunds. Each teacher requesting a refund of accumulated assessments shall file an application stating that he has become permanently separated from government service. This application must be supplemented by a report from the Department of Education or other employer certifying that the teacher has become separated from service and does not occupy any position in the Government of Puerto Rico. The application shall stipulate that the teacher resigns and forfeits all the rights and benefits which he had at the date upon which application was filed. This refund shall consist of all the amounts contributed to this system or to any other superseded pension fund including the interest to be accredited as determined by the Board in accordance with section 

31 of the Act [18 L.P.R.A. § 350].

§ 331-22. Investments and loans Operating cash balance 

The cash balance to be maintained by the system for current expenses, including payments to the different types of beneficiaries, refunds, administrative expenses, and loans to the teachers, shall never exceed the amount which has been estimated as necessary for such purposes for a period of 90 days. Monies accumulated by the system shall be kept fully invested and cash balances shall, at all times, be maintained at a minimum consistent with the current operating needs of the system, so that the system may obtain the maximum amount of interest income on its accumulated reserve. § 331-23. Procedure 

The executive secretary shall submit recommendations to the

Board on the investment of the reserve of the system in eligible securities authorized by law. These recommendations shall be accompanied by full statistical and financial data of the securities recommended, and, among other things, a complete description of the securities and their purposes, prices thereof, rate of interest, 271

T.§ 331-23 Ch. 17 

names of vendors, and the amounts already invested in securities of the agency represented. His recommendations shall include an analysis of each type of security recommended for investment, stating the reasons underlying the recommendation. He shall supply the Board with any other information concerning said securities as will facilitate a proper valuation thereof, and that which may be requested hereafter by the Board. 

The executive secretary shall also compile information in relation to the applications for the different kinds of loans authorized by law, which shall consist of a detailed description of the sureties, and collateral security given in support of said loans, and any other necessary data for a proper determination of the responsibility of the applicant and his sureties or for a fair appraisal of the value of the property subject to a mortgage loan. 

§ 331-24. Purchase of bonds 

The executive secretary shall recommend to the Board from time to time the purchase of general obligation bonds of the types prescribed by law for investment by the system. The purchase of bonds shall be authorized and approved by the Board. To the extent possible and practicable these bonds shall be registered in the name of the system. The purchases shall be made upon the basis of the information compiled by the executive secretary and of any other data as may be available to the Board in relation to the bonds which are being considered for purchase. 

§ 331-25. Sale or exchange of securities 

The Secretary of the Treasury shall, upon previous authorization by the Board, sell or exchange securities pertaining to the system; likewise he shall recommend to the Board from time to time to sell or exchange its securities or to foreclose mortgages submitting at the same time a report showing the impaired status of such investments or loans and shall file facts or conditions to support his recommendations, as well as the basis upon which such sales, exchanges, or foreclosures shall be made. The proceedings for the foreclosure of mortgages on investments or loans shall be carried out in accordance with the laws of Puerto Rico governing such foreclosures and shall be authorized by the Board. 

All expenses incurred in foreclosures shall become a part of the indebtedness of the borrower under the mortgage or loan, to be reimbursed to the system upon the final disposition of the security 272

Ch. T.18 331-26 

TEACHERS' BENEFITS 

representing the loan or investment. The executive secretary shall submit to the Board from time to time reports on the progress of foreclosures and on the consummation of such proceedings so that the Board shall be kept fully informed on the status of all such investments. 

§ 331-26. Investment of funds in loans to the teachers Loans guaranteed by contributions (a) Loans not greater than a monthly salary. Any teacher, member of the system under contract as substitute, provisional or temporary teacher, who does not have a permanent contract in any other category, shall be entitled to receive a loan, after 12 months of service, for an amount not exceeding one month's salary, provided he has contributed to the fund an amount not less than that of the loan applied for. This loan shall be repaid during the remaining period of the applicants annual contract. (b) Loans not greater than two monthly salaries. Any teacher, member of the system, holding a permanent, probationary, or 1-year contract, provided this last contract has been renewed for 3 or more consecutive years, shall be entitled to receive a loan after 12 months of service for an amount not to exceed 2 months' salary which shall be repaid in twelve monthly installments. These loans shall not be renewed and shall be granted provided the teacher has contributed to the fund an amount not less than that of the loan applied for. (c) Contributions loans. Any teacher, member of the system, with permanent, probationary or 1-year contract, provided this last contract has been renewed for 3 or more consecutive years, may be granted a loan, after 12 months of service, for an amount not to exceed 80 percent of his contributions and not less than $300. Teachers holding a substitute, temporary or provisional contract who have contributed to the system for 3 or more consecutive years, shall be granted a loan not exceeding 80 percent of his contributions, provided that the amount of the loan is not less than $300. This loan shall be repaid in monthly installments equal to at least 3 percent of the amount of the loan. The same shall be repaid in 34 months and may be renewed after 12 months from the date granted, provided that not less than 12 installments have been paid.

§ 331-27. 

Rate of interest

All loans guaranteed by the member's contributions which shall be granted according to subsecs. (a), (b) and (c) of sec. 331-26 of this title shall pay an interest of 6 percent per year, which shall be deducted in advance from the amount of the loan, with an additional amount to cover the cost of the premium for the payment of a life insurance on the debt. 

Amendments 1963. An additional amount to cover cost of premium for payment of a life insurance on the debt was established by amendment File No. 879, cited in 1963 amend ment note under § 331-5 of this title. 

§ 331-28. 

Mortgage loans

The funds of the system shall be invested in loans to the teachers for the purchase, construction, payment of first mortgage, repairs or improvement of real property. All teachers holding permanent or probationary contracts shall be eligible for these kind of loans, provided they have contributed to the system during 36 months of service and have attained 21 years of age. 

Amendments 1963. Number of months that teachers need to have contributed to system, in order to be eligible for mortgage loans, was increased from 24 to 36, by amendment File No. 879, cited in 1963 amendment note under 

§ 331-5 of this title. 

§ 331-29. 

Loans for the purchase of real property (homes) (a) The loan shall be guaranteed by a first mortgage on the real property for the purchase of which the loan is made; it shall also be guaranteed by the accumulated assessments and the ones which shall be accumulated by the borrower in the Teachers' Annuity and Pension System, and by the benefits which the beneficiaries of the teacher shall receive in case the latter dies, as provided for in secs. 33 and 43 of Act No. 218 of 1951, as amended [18

L.P.R.A. §§ 352, 362]. 

(b) The loan shall not exceed the amount which the teacher will be able to pay with 40 percent of his net salary after all provided lawful deductions are made, nor shall it exceed the amount

that the borrower will be able to pay with the estimated annuity at the optional age of retirement. The teacher shall not bind, in any kind of loans deducted through payroll, more than the 40 percent above stipulated nor more than 60 percent as specified in the following subsec. (c). In any instance the loan shall not exceed $20,000, nor shall it exceed the value of the property which is to serve as a security for the mortgage. The value of the property which is to serve as security shall be determined by the Board in its internal bylaws, specifying the proportion of the total value of the property, as this value shall be determined by the official appraiser which shall be considered for the purpose. (c) Joint mortgage loans shall be granted on a basis of 60 percent of the salary exclusively to a married couple, members of the system, who have contributed to the fund not less than 3 years of services, and who shall hold permanent or probationary contract. 

Both husband and wife shall become joint debtors for the total amount of the loan. (d) The maximum term for repayment of the mortgage loan shall not exceed 25 years nor shall it exceed the difference in years between the teacher's age and the age of 65, if the house offered in guarantee is all made of concrete, roof inclusive. (e) The basic type of interest for mortgage loans shall be equal to 1/4 of 1 percent less than the basic type of interest authorized by FHA, (interest plus insurance) never over 6 percent, with an additional amount to cover the cost of the premium for the payment of the life mortgage insurance. Payments for the amortization of principal, interest, insurance and taxes shall be included in one amount to be deducted from the monthly salary of the teacher. (f) In case a teacher becomes separated from service, he shall be bound to make direct payments to the system. Three installments being due and not repaid, the Board shall consider the mortgage due and shall proceed to its foreclosure. The contract of the loan shall provide for the conditions and limitations to be declared effective in case the borrower becomes separated from service. (g) In order to receive the loan, the borrower shall be bound to insure the property. If it is all concrete the insurance coverage shall provide for earthquake hazard in an amount equal to 100 per cent of the value of the property, for fire hazard 80 per cent, and 50 per cent for hurricane hazard. In cases of mixed construction an insurance coverage of 100 per cent of the value of the property shall be required for fire, hurricane, and earthquake hazards; and 

Jan. 31, 1964

Vol. 3, No. 1 275

T.§ 331-29 

Ch. 17

in the case of wood construction 100 per cent of the value of the property for hurricane and fire hazards and 50 per cent for earthquake hazard.

In order to determine the amount of the insurance, the value of the property at the time of insurance shall be considered and the price of the lot shall be excluded. The mortgagee's clause of the insurance policy shall be indorsed on behalf of the Board. 

A life mortgage insurance to be paid by the mortgagor will be established after previous approval of the Secretary of the Treasury and the Insurance Commissioner covering the unpaid balance of the mortgage loan, and which said administration will be in the charge of the Teachers' Retirement Board in accordance with the contract signed with the insurance company. (h) Before a mortgage loan is granted, the executive secretary shall make the necessary investigations to determine the moral and economic responsibility of the applicant and he may recommend the disapproval of the loan should the case be not meritorious. (i) The house offered as security for the loan must be made of concrete, or concrete blocks, with the columns, beams, and roof made of concrete. Houses made of wood with zinc roofs, and houses of mixed construction shall be accepted as security for the loans, but the maximum term for repayment of said loans shall not exceed 10 years. If the house is all concrete with a zinc roof, a maximum term of 15 years may be granted for repayment both cases within the age under regulations. in (j) The property subject to loan shall be situated in an urban residential zone. Loans for properties in the rural zone shall be considered, provided that the property is a good risk and complies with the conditions for development determined by the Planning Board as to the utilities of energy and water supplies and access to the highway. (k) Mortgage loans for commercial, industrial, or similar purposes shall not be considered. The applicant shall also remit the receipt of the last payment on property tax, or a letter of tax exemption in case no

§ 331-30. Loans for the construction of real property (resi dence) (a) Should a loan be granted for the construction or repair of a house, the borrower shall furnish, while the work is being done, a bond endorsed to the Teachers' Retirement Board, issued by an insurance company certified by the laws of Puerto Rico and authorized to do business in the Island, or by guarantors sworn before a notary. Such guarantors shall not exceed two, and shall be those 

Jan. 31, 1964

Vol. 3, No. 1 277

T.§ 331-30 Ch. 17 

who have property recorded in the Registry, the total or partial value of which property guarantees the amount to be loaned, as verified by a certification issued by the Registrar. Loans for construction shall be granted only for concrete houses, or houses of concrete blocks with the columns, beams, and roof made of reinforced concrete. (b) The applicant shall attach to the application the following 

(1) Title to the lot on which the house is to be built. (2) Certification from the Registrar to the effect that the title is completely clear. (3) Plans and specifications for the house. 

(4) Construction permits approved by the Board of Permits of the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and a cost estimate of the construction. (5) Receipt of property tax on the lot corresponding to the last year. (6) Birth certificate. (7) Copy of the contract if the construction is under contract. (c) Loans for construction shall be delivered in partial payments as construction progresses. In case a contract has been negotiated by the applicant for the construction of the residence, the payments shall be made as provided for in the contract, subject to the report of the appraiser on the progress of the construction. Upon authorization of first payment, the mortgage deed, on the lot and residence to be built, shall be executed on behalf of the Board. (d) If the construction is to be made by force account and not under contract, and the amount of the loan is less than $6,000, the money shall be advanced in two installments, depending on the recommendations and report of the appraisers. If the loan is from $6,000 to $9,000, payment shall be made in three installments; if it exceeds $9,000, payment shall be made in four installments, always subject to the report of the appraiser. (e) Loans for construction on lots belonging to the municipality shall be approved, but payment thereof shall not be made effective until the construction is finished depending on the report of the appraiser, since the lot cannot be burdened. 

Codification. In the Spanish text the items under subsection (b) are not numbered or separated.

§ 331-32. General dispositions 

(a) Should a personal loan be granted to a teacher who is already indebted to the system, he shall be required to repay such debt from the amount of the loan. (b) Mortgage and personal loans are not inconsistent when applying for a mortgage loan. A teacher to whom a mortgage loan is granted for the first time may be eligible for a loan on his contributions (paid in 34 installments) up to the amount permitted by his borrowing capacity to the point the debt is liquidated and shall not be entitled to renewal.

§ 331-34. Hiring of engineer 

The executive secretary shall contract the services of an engineer experienced in appraisals of real property and home construction, who shall perform the following duties: To study the application, drawings and specifications; to set the estimated value upon the property as security for the mortgage loan; and to inspect the construction work as it progresses. 

The expenses incurred in examining the drawings, in inspection, and appraisement shall be paid by the applicant. 

§ 331-35. Hiring of notary public 

The executive secretary shall contract the services of a notary public who shall make the necessary investigations as to the title to the property in the Registrar's Office, prepare the deeds and register them and perform any other functions which may be compatible with those delegated to him by the Board and the executive secretary. 

§ 331-36. Appraisal, title investigation 

Should an application for mortgage loan be filed and all the requirements prescribed by this chapter fulfilled, the executive secretary shall request immediately the appraiser of the system to make the corresponding investigation of the case. The appraiser shall submit a report thereof within 15 days from the date on which the investigation was requested from him. Likewise, the

After the loan has been approved and the teacher-borrowers have appeared at the granting and signing of the deeds in the offices of the Board, the special disbursement officer shall write the corresponding check. 

§ 331-40. Conflict of interest 

(a) The executive secretary, the members of the Board or the employees of the system shall not have direct or indirect interest in the profits or income on any investment or loan granted by the Board, nor shall any of them receive payment or profits for services in relation to a loan or investment. The executive secretary, the members of the Board and/or any employee of the system shall not become guarantors or sureties for any loans granted by the system. (b) Mortgage loans can be granted to the executive secretary or the members of the Board if they are members of the system. 

In such cases the borrower must not participate in the voting to be held by the Board. In those cases in which the borrower should be the executive secretary, the loan must be evaluated and approved directly by the Board.

§ 331-41. Appeal 

(a) The decisions and rulings of the executive secretary shall be made in the name of the Board. (b) Any appeal in relation to a decision of the executive secretary from any teacher shall be filed before the Board. The appeal shall be filed before the Board in writing and shall set forth fully the problem in controversy and the reasons for the appeal. The 

Board shall review the facts presented by the member at any regular or special meeting and the complainant may attend such meeting while the appeal is being reviewed. The decision of the 

Board on any appeal shall be considered final, and subject only to review by the corresponding court of justice. 

§ 331-41a. Various expenses 

(a) The documentation and registration fees shall be paid by the borrower. Likewise it shall be up to the borrower to pay a year's premium on the insurance policy, a proportional deposit for taxes, interest from the time of the granting of the loan up to the first payment, and a deposit for mortgage insurance. (b) All the expenses of the loan shall be charged against the borrower and may be discounted from the payment voucher. It shall be understood that any increase in the amount of the loan shall not be considered, unless the borrower has a sufficient mortgage margin and the property placed as security has a value, as estimated by the Board, equal to or greater than the total of the loan, including such expenses.

§ 331-42. Effectiveness 

This chapter was approved unanimously by the Teachers' Retirement Board and shall take effect and have the force of law after approval by the Governor and promulgation by the Retirement Board.

EDUCATION-PUBLIC SCHOOLS § 331-43. Proclamation, distribution 

These regulations and any subsequent amendments shall be printed and distributed. Copies thereof shall be given to any employer or participant who shall so request. 

§ 331-44. Amendment 

To amend this chapter the following procedure shall be followed: 

The executive secretary shall receive every proposed amendment to these regulations notifying the Board of the amendment so that the latter may determine whether or not it is urgent and necessary. If it is, public hearings shall be held as stipulated hereinafter. If it is not considered urgent and necessary, the executive secretary shall acknowledge receipt of said proposed amendment and shall file it properly until the first of May of each year when he shall submit it in writing to be studied and considered by the Board as a whole in the third week of that month for which purpose an extraordinary meeting shall be summoned. The executive secretary shall make arrangements to celebrate a public hearing in the city of San Juan, to explain said amendment to interested persons. At least 10 days prior to the date fixed for the public. hearing a notice shall be published thereof in one or more of the newspapers of general circulation published in San Juan. The executive secretary shall report as to the results of the hearing to the Board and the latter shall consider the adoption of the amendment, which once having been approved with at least four affirmative votes shall be recommended to the Governor of the Commonwealth for final approval. Once approved by the Governor it shall have the force of law and shall go into effect after having been promulgated by the Board.

§ 503-2. Notice to U. S. Commissioner of Education of law change The Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education, through its executive officer, will assume the responsibility of keeping the United States Commissioner of Education informed of any and all legal changes that may affect the vocational education program in 

Puerto Rico. 

§ 503-3. Authority of Board The Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education has the legal authority to: 285

T.§ 503-3 Ch. 23 

(1) Prepare, adopt, and submit a Commonwealth plan for the approval of the United States Commissioner of Education. The plan will include:

Administration and Supervision, Agriculture, Distributive Education, Home Economics, Trades and Industry, and Vocational Guidance. It will be formulated in accordance with the topical outline submitted by the United States Office of Education. (2) Approve budgets and expenditures of Federal and Commonwealth funds for vocational education to such schools and institutions as are approved by said Commonwealth Board and are entitled to receive such moneys under the provisions of the Smith- 

Hughes and the George-Barden Acts. (3) Select, employ and discharge all administrative and supervisory Commonwealth Board personnel.

The Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education will employ and discharge the employees of the different programs of vocational education upon the recommendation of the Executive Officer. § 503-4. Executive officer 

(a) Appointment. The Secretary of Education of Puerto Rico shall be the executive officer of the Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education. (b) The executive officer shall be immediately responsible to the 

Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education for the general administration of the program of vocational education in Puerto Rico. (c) It is not planned to have any Federal funds used for the salary of the executive officer, but Federal funds may be used for necessary official travel. 

§ 503-5. Commonwealth director of vocational education (a) The Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education shall employ, in accordance with the provisions of this plan, a director of vocational education who shall devote his full time to the administration of the services set forth in this plan. 

The salary and travel of the director of vocational education shall be reimbursed from George-Barden funds on the same prorated basis, to be determined by the Commonwealth Board, for all administrative expenses. (b) Duties. (1) Administrative: (A) It shall be the duty of the director of vocational edu- 286

Ch. T.18 § 503-5 

VOCATIONAL EDUCATION 

cation to prepare, with the supervisory staff, Commonwealth plans for vocational education to be submitted to the executive officer and to the Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education. (B) He shall have general direction of all vocational services represented in this plan in or out of the public schools of 

Puerto Rico, for which Federal funds may be used. (C) He shall have the direction of the preparation and publication of all bulletins on subject matter material and other articles issued for the promotion and further development of vocational education. (D) He shall be responsible for the preparation of all reports that are submitted to the United States Office of Educa tion by the Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education. 

(E) He shall have general administration of all vocational work done in all designated teacher-training institutions where 

Federal funds are used. (F) With the recommendation of the respective supervisors, he shall prepare budgets for the entire vocational education program in Puerto Rico, and shall submit such budgets for approval to the Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education, through the executive officer. (G) With the recommendation of the respective supervisors, he shall make final recommendations to the executive officer for the appointment of all personnel in the vocational education program by the Commonwealth Board for Vocational 

Education. 

(H) He shall represent the Commonwealth Board in all technical matters pertaining to the administration of vocational education. (I) He shall coordinate the work and the programs of the supervisors and the teacher trainers of the several sections of the Commonwealth program. (J) He shall promote such studies, surveys, and research as may be necessary and helpful in the development of vocational education in Puerto Rico. (K) He shall keep the Commonwealth Board informed at all times on the current status of vocational education in Puerto Rico. (2) Supervisory: 

It shall be the duty of the director to have general super- 287

T.§ 503-5 Ch. 23 

vision of the administrative personnel of the Division of Vocational Education, as well as supervision of the professional personnel of the teacher-training departments in the respective institutions where Federal funds are used for the training of teachers for the various services. 

(3) Promotional: 

It shall be the duty of the director of vocational education to contact persons and organizations for the purpose of giving information as to the nature of the program of vocational education, in order that he may bring about the further development of vocational education. (c) Qualification. (1) Education: 

(A) Technical: The Commonwealth Director of Voca tional Education must be a graduate of a recognized college or university. In addition he must hold a Master's degree from an institution designated to train teachers of vocational education. 

He must have the technical training that will enable him to meet the qualifications required for a head supervisor in one of the vocational education services provided in this plan. (B) Professional: The director must have the professional qualifications that will enable him to meet the requirements for a head supervisor in one or more of the vocational education services provided in this plan. These professional qualifications will comprise the following: administration, supervision, and proficiency in methods used in vocational education. (2) Experience: 

The director shall have five or more years of administrative experience in an approved program of vocational education, or five or more years of full-time teacher training experience in such an approved program. § 503-6. Supporting staff other than supervisors and teacher trainers Assistant directors shall be appointed by the Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education to assist the director in the general administration and supervision of the program of vocational education in Puerto Rico.

The administrative staff shall comprise, besides the director, assistant directors and all other administrative and clerical personnel needed. 288

§ 503-7. Assistant director Duties (a) Administrative. An assistant director: 

(1) Shall assist the Director in preparing, with the super visory staff, the Commonwealth Plan for Vocational Education to be submitted to the Office of Education in Washington, D. C.; (2) Shall assist the Director in the general direction of all vocational services represented in this plan in or out of the public schools of Puerto Rico, for which Federal funds may be used; (3) Shall assist the director in the general administration of the vocational activities carried on in the teacher training centers and shall report to the director; (4) Shall prepare and submit to the director, with the recommendation of respective supervisors, the budgets for the programs of vocational education in Puerto Rico; (5) Shall share with the director the representation of the Commonwealth Board in all official matters; (6) Shall represent the director, in his absence, in all technical matters pertaining to the administration of vocational education; (7) Shall assist the director in coordinating the work and the programs of the supervisors and the teacher trainers of the several sections of the Commonwealth program; (8) Shall keep the Commonwealth Board informed, in the absence of the director, on the current status of vocational education in Puerto Rico; (9) Shall assist the director in signing routine correspondence, leave of absence blanks, purchase orders, travel orders, vouchers, etc.; (10) Shall assist the director in the preparation, publication and distribution of all bulletins, monographs, reports, statistics, 289

T.§ 503-7 Ch. 23 

EDUCATION -- PUBLIC SCHOOLS 

and any other printed materials to be published in the interest of vocational education in Puerto Rico; (11) Shall assist the director in promoting such studies, surveys and research work as may be necessary and helpful in the development of vocational education in Puerto Rico; (12) Shall assist the director in promoting and securing cooperation from other government agencies in the interest of the vocational education program; (13) Shall assist in the drafting of laws for the vocational education program; (14) Shall assist the director and the supervisors in the organization of general meetings, conferences, and conventions, and in selecting data for publication about these activities. (b) Supervisory. An assistant director: (1) Shall assist the director in the supervision of administrative personnel; (2) Shall assist the director in the supervision of the technical phase of the work in the various fields of vocational education. § 503-8. 

Qualifications 

(a) General education and professional training. An assistant director shall possess at least a bachelor's degree from a standard college or university, with specialized training in keeping with duties. (b) Experience. An assistant director shall have had at least three years of experience in vocational education, one year of which shall have been in the supervision, teacher training or administration of a vocational program, in one or more fields of vocational education or vocational rehabilitation. (c) Others. An assistant director shall have: (1) Ability to deal with people; (2) Ability to coordinate the work and to secure cooperation from private and public agencies; (3) Thorough knowledge of education problems. 

§ 503-9. Representative Commonwealth advisory committees for vocational education including those of the respective fields 

(a) Type of committee. The Commonwealth Board for Voca tional Education will appoint, through the executive officer and the 290

Ch. 

T.18 § 503-9 

VOCATIONAL EDUCATION 

director of vocational education, Commonwealth advisory commit tees for Agriculture, Distributive Education, Home Economics, 

Trades and Industry, and Guidance, upon the recommendation of the respective supervisors. One or more members of each of these named committees will constitute the Commonwealth advisory committee for vocational education. (b) Interests represented. Members of these advisory committees shall be representative of the various activities on the Island of Puerto Rico. The executive officer, the director of vocational education, assistant directors, and the head supervisor of each field shall be members ex officio of the committees. (c) Method of selection. The personnel of the respective representative advisory committees and of the Commonwealth advisory committee for vocational education will be appointed by the executive officer, upon the recommendation of the Commonwealth director of vocational education and of the respective supervisors of the various fields of vocational education. (d) Term of office. The personnel of each of the representative advisory committees of Agriculture, Trades and Industry, Home 

Economics, Distributive Education, and Guidance will be appointed for a term of one, two, three, four, and five years, respectively, and in the case of the Commonwealth advisory committee for vocational education, the persons selected to represent Agriculture will be appointed for one year; those to represent Trades and Industry, for two years; those to represent Home Economics, for three years; those to represent Distributive Education, for four years; and those to represent Guidance, for five years. At the expiration of the term of office of the persons representing Agriculture, such persons or their successors will be appointed for a term of five years, thus rotating the term of office so as to have new members on this committee each year. (e) Duties. (1) It shall be the duty of the respective service advisory committees and of the Commonwealth advisory committee for vocational education to advise the director and the supervisors on any matters pertaining to vocational education. (2) It shall also be the duty of this committee to assist the director and the supervisors of vocational education in all matters pertaining to the promotion and further development of the vocational education program in Puerto Rico. (f) Provisions for meetings. (1) The advisory committees will 291

Ch. 23

be subject to the call of the director and/or the supervisors of vocational education. 

(2) No definite intervals will be designated for the meetings; their frequency will be determined by the director and/or the supervisors. (3) Traveling expenses will be allowed to cover the expenses of the personnel of the respective advisory committees when they receive an official call from the director and/or the supervisors of vocational education. 

§ 503-10. Commonwealth Board's responsibility for supervision 

(a) It will be the responsibility of the Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education to appoint a director, assistant directors, a 

Commonwealth supervisor of Agriculture, a Commonwealth supervisor of Distributive Education, a Commonwealth supervisor of

Trades and Industry, a Commonwealth supervisor of Home Economics Education, and a Commonwealth supervisor of Vocational 

Guidance, and such other staff personnel as is necessary for the effective administration and supervision of the vocational program. 

(b) The Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education will be responsible for employing only supervisors who meet all the qualifications set up in the Commonwealth plan. 

§ 503-11. Leave of absence to study 

The Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education, in an effort to maintain the professional standards of the supervisors of vocational education, may, after a period of five years in service, grant them a leave of absence with pay to study advanced courses in their respective fields. This leave will not exceed a period of ten months, will not be cumulative, and will be granted only on the written statement of the recipients that they will return to their positions with the Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education for at least a year. This leave shall in no way affect the vacation and sick leaves provided by the Commonwealth law. This will be done in case comparable privileges are granted by the 

Secretary of Education to persons in comparable positions in education.

(1) Education: He must be a graduate in agriculture from the land grant college in Puerto Rico or from a land grant college recognized by the United States Office of Education. § 503-14. Distributive education 

(a) Special duties of Commonwealth and assistant supervisors. 

(1) Promotional: 

(A) Promote the Commonwealth and National programs of vocational distributive education. (B) Promote and perfect a local, Commonwealth and National program for the distributors' clubs. (C) Promote and coordinate the program of distributive education with business organizations and employee groups. 

Commonwealth and assistant supervisors shall be responsible for establishing and maintaining the necessary contacts with organizations that contribute to the promotion, operation, and improvement of the total distributive education program. (D) Promote research in distributive education. (E) Make surveys of communities to determine justification of a distributive education program for youth and/or adults. (2) Supervisory: (A) Evaluate records of all teachers to see that they meet 296

Ch. T.18 § 503-14 

VOCATIONAL EDUCATION 

the Commonwealth requirements for vocational distributive education. (B) Approve and recommend the qualifications and fitness for the job, of teacher trainers, itinerant teacher trainers, assistant supervisors, and teachers. (C) In addition to providing adequate supervision of the reimbursable phases of business training, the Commonwealth supervisor of business education will devote a portion of his time to give assistance in non-reimbursable classes. 

(3) Instructional: 

(A) Assist in the formulation of courses of study to be given to teachers in training to become instructors in distributive lines, and assist in the training of these instructors. (B) Aid in the making of educational surveys and investigations in industry, in the collection of material, and in the preparation of bulletins, reports, plans, and teaching aids. (C) Assist coordinators in making long-time plans for the development of the program in each locality. (D) Give particular attention to the improvement of teachers of evening and part-time classes. (b) Qualifications of Commonwealth supervisor. (1) Education: He shall have a bachelor's degree from a recognized institution or equivalent in terms of courses completed on the college level. This training shall include at least 24 semester hours of technical courses in business of which not less than 12 semester hours shall have been in such subjects as marketing, advertising, retailing, salesmanship, and personnel problems; and at least 21 semester hours of professional hours shall have been in such subjects as methods and coordination in distributive education. (2) Experience: (A) He shall have had five years successful experience in teaching vocational business subjects; two of these five years shall have been devoted to teaching distributive classes and/or conducting conferences of store personnel. (B) Shall have had at least four years of business experience with at least the equivalent of two years of full-time experience in selling or other distributive work. (C) Shall have had at least three years in a responsible supervisory, administrative, or teacher-training capacity in the field of vocational education. 297

T.§ 503-14 Ch. 23 

(3) General: Shall have demonstrated leadership ability in his contact with business and education and shall have had successful cooperative relations with his employers and associates. (c) Qualifications of assistant supervisors.

The qualification of assistant supervisors shall be the same as those of the Commonwealth supervisor. However, in specialized distributive fields such as drugs, restaurants, or other lines of business, persons may be employed as assistant supervisors who are generally recognized to be highly competent in those fields and who meet at least one-half of the educational requirements set forth in this plan for the Commonwealth supervisor. 

§ 503-15. - Home economics education (a) The Commonwealth supervisor shall: 

(1) Work with the pre-service training program for home economics. (2) Keep alert to the needs for and possibilities of extending home economics to more individuals, schools, and communities. (3) Provide opportunities for teachers employed beyond the regular school year to serve the community effectively or for participating in activities provided for professional growth. (4) Take advantage of any possibilities of promoting or participating in educational experimental or research programs that show promise of homemaking implications. (5) Plan for the promotion of new work by working closely with the Department of Education in developing a total educational program of which home economics is an integral part. 

(6) Plan for supervision of work. The supervisor shall: 

(A) Visit teachers and schools with home economics programs. (B) Visit the teacher training and student teaching centers for vocational programs in home economics. (C) Evaluate the plant, equipment, supplies, and the records of each department. (D) Review reports of the supervisory staff of the vocational program and of teachers of home economics. (E) Evaluate the work of the assistant supervisors, teacher trainer, assistant teacher trainer, itinerant teacher trainer, and supervising teachers. (F) Evaluate the qualifications and fitness for the job, of 298

(B) Successful experience as a supervisor of student teaching in home economics. (C) Practical homemaking experience sufficient to assume responsibility of managing a home.

§ 503-51. Matching of Federal funds 

In order to receive the benefits of the Smith-Hughes and George- Barden Acts, the Commonwealth Government shall be required to match with Commonwealth and local funds, or both, 100 per cent of the appropriations of Federal funds. Commonwealth and local moneys used for vocational education may be used for matching Federal funds only when such moneys are used for work meeting all the conditions for Federal reimbursement. To be considered for Federal reimbursement, the Commonwealth Board shall provide the supervision, require the standards, and secure the reports required by the Federal plan.

through the offices of the Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education. § 503-53. Purposes other than teacher training for which Smith- 

Hughes and George-Barden funds are to be used 

Smith-Hughes. The Smith-Hughes Act stipulates that the appropriations made under this act are for specific purposes. The "several purposes" under the Smith-Hughes act are: (1) Salaries of teachers, supervisors, or directors of agricultural subjects. (2) Salaries of teachers of trade and industrial subjects in allday and evening schools or classes. (3) Salaries of teachers of trade and industrial subjects in part-time schools or classes. (4) Salaries of teachers of home economics subjects in all-day and evening schools or classes. (5) Salaries of teachers of home economics subjects in part-time schools or classes. (6) Maintenance of training of teachers, supervisors or directors of agricultural subjects. (7) Maintenance of training of teachers of trade and industrial subjects. (8) Maintenance of training of teachers of home economics subjects. (9) Salaries and necessary travel expenses of teacher trainers and supervisors of vocational education. (10) Maintenance, including communication, supplies, printing, rent, light, heat, and janitor service for teacher training. 

§ 503-54. Vocational purposes of George-Barden Act 

(a) The several purposes of the George-Barden Act are: (1) Vocational education in agriculture. (2) Vocational education in home economics. (3) Vocational education in trades and industry in part-time classes. (4) Vocational education in trades and industry in classes other than part-time classes. (5) Vocational education in distributive occupations. (b) George-Barden funds: 

(1) Salaries and necessary travel expenses of 

(A) Teachers, teacher trainers, and supervisors of vocational education. 307

After 1951, not more than 10% of the George-Barden funds will be used for this purpose. (A) For vocational instruction of less than college grade. (B) For reimbursable teacher training. 

503-55. Teacher training

The teacher training programs of the different services - agriculture, distributive education, home economics, trades and industry, and vocational guidance, shall be carried out under the supervision of the Commonwealth Board; such training shall be given only to schools or classes under public supervision or control; such training shall be given only to persons who have had adequate vocational experience or contact in the line of work for which they are preparing themselves as teachers, counselors (teacher advisors), supervisors, or directors, or who are acquiring such experience or contact as part of their training; and the Commonwealth Board shall establish minimum requirements for such experience or contact. § 503-56. Apportionment of Smith-Hughes teacher training funds

Not more than sixty per cent or less than twenty per cent of the money appropriated under the Smith-Hughes Act for the training of teachers of vocational subjects for any year shall be expended for any of the following purposes: For the preparation of teachers, supervisors or directors of agricultural subjects, or the preparation of teachers of trade and industrial subjects, or the preparation of teachers of home economics subjects. Any unused funds budgeted to any service may be used for other services, provided the requirements are met regarding minimum and maximum amount for each service as set forth by the United 

States Office of Education. 

308

Ch. T.18 § 503-59 

VOCATIONAL EDUCATION 

§ 503-57. Short, intensive technical courses; reimbursement 

George-Barden funds shall be used to reimburse the salary of an instructor of a short, intensive technical course under the following conditions: (1) The instructor has had suitable preparation and experience in the field of the short, intensive technical courses to be reimbursed: (2) Such course enrolls only qualified vocational teachers and supervisors. (3) The subject matter in such technical courses is of immediate value to the employed teachers and supervisors. (4) The course is authorized by the Commonwealth Board. (5) The course is not a regular course of a designated teacher training institution. § 503-58. Special professional courses; reimbursement 

Special professional courses in the philosophy, principles and practices of vocational education for school administrators, as well as for directors and supervisors of vocational education, are considered phases of teacher training and may be reimbursed from Federal funds when authorized by the Commonwealth Board. Reimbursement of the costs of such courses shall be prorated among the several Federal funds available for teacher training. § 503-59. Information, data, research 

The George-Barden Act provides that Federal funds may be used by the Commonwealth Board for securing necessary educational information and data as a basis for the proper development of programs of vocational education and vocational guidance. These activities may be: (1) Gathering and assembling of data and information which will be of assistance in the administration and operation of vocational programs. (2) Comprehensive research projects and basic investigations of problems, the solution of which presumably will be of help to other States also.

Smith-Hughes teacher training funds may also be used as reimbursement for the maintenance of research in vocational education conducted as a part of the program. 309

T.§ 503-60 Ch. 23 

 § 503-60. Services and supplies 

Federal funds may be used for the payment of clerical services, communication, printing, light, rent, janitor service, and supplies. 

§ 503-61. Consultants 

Teacher training funds may be used for the reimbursement of necessary travel expenses of consultants who are recognized authorities in their fields of work for assisting in conferences on problems of teacher training or program development, when called by the Commonwealth Board if requested by the Commonwealth supervisor of the service involved. 

§ 503-62. Technical subject matter teachers 

When resident college teachers of technical subject matter courses are requested by the Commonwealth supervisors to visit schools and communities for the purpose of studying and working on problems which confront teachers in the effective teaching of a specific occupation, teacher training funds may be used for the reimbursement of necessary travel expenses of such college teachers. § 503-63. Provisions for purchase or rental of equipment and purchase of supplies for vocational instruction George-Barden funds may be used for the purchase or rental of equipment and supplies for vocational instruction. After 1951 not more than 10% of these funds will be used for this purpose. 

Equipment for vocational instruction is taken to mean any physical object which may be expected to last, with reasonable use and care, for more than one year, and which is used exclusively by vocational teachers and teacher trainers in instructing, and by their students in learning, in an instructional situation in the classroom, laboratory, shop or field. 

Supplies for vocational instruction is taken to mean material which is consumed by use, either in a single usage or during a period of less than one year, and which is used exclusively by vocational teachers and teacher trainers in instructing, and by their students in learning, in an instructional situation in the classroom, laboratory, shop or field. The cost of magazines used for instructional purposes may be reimbursed as supplies. 312

§ 503-65. Limitation on the expenditure of trade, home economics, and industrial funds Part-time classes. In order to receive the benefits of Federal appropriations for the salaries of teachers of trade, home economics and industrial subjects, the Commonwealth Board for 

Vocational Education shall provide: 

(1) That such education be given in schools or classes under public supervision or control. (2) That the controlling purpose of such education shall be to fit for useful employment. (3) That such education shall be of less than college grade and shall be designed to meet the needs of persons over fourteen years of age who are preparing for a trade or industrial pursuit or who have entered upon the work of a trade or industrial pursuit. (4) That the Commonwealth Board shall provide the necessary plant and equipment. (5) That at least one-third of the sum appropriated for the salaries of teachers of trade, home economics and industrial subjects, if expended, be applied to part-time schools or classes for workers over 14 years of age (16 years if George-Barden funds are used) who have entered upon employment, and such subjects in part-time school or class may mean any subject given to enlarge the civic or vocational intelligence of such workers over 14 and less than 18 years of age. (6) That such part-time schools or classes shall provide for not less than 144 hours of classroom instruction per year. If George- 

Barden funds are used, the number of hours may be less. (7) That evening industrial schools shall fix the age of 16 years as minimum entrance requirement and shall confine instruction to that which is supplemental to the daily employment. (8) That the teachers of any trade or industrial subject shall have at least the minimum qualifications for teachers of such subjects as determined by the Commonwealth Board. (9) That one-third of the funds for trade and industrial education, if expended, shall be expended for part-time education

The inspectional activities of the local director shall be primarily for the purpose of discovering those points in which his teachers need help and assistance.

(A) Graduation from a degree granting course in a college or university of recognized standing, or its equivalent of courses completed on the college level. (B) Two hundred seventy hours of professional courses in vocational education on the undergraduate or graduate level. 

(2) Experience: 

(A) Trade Two years of journeyman trade experience. (B) Teaching - At least two years of successful experience as a teacher, one year of which shall have been in the field of trade and industrial education. 

§ 503-67. Methods of instruction 

Instruction shall be given by class discussions, demonstrations, work experience, and practice on the part of the students. Instruction will be adapted as much as possible to individual needs. 

Methods utilizing group activities shall be provided to promote understanding and the sharing of common purposes. 

§ 503-68. Plant and equipment 

The plant and equipment shall be suitable for efficient instruction, and shall be adequate to carry out the purposes for which the school or classes are organized. 314

The Commonwealth or local community, or both, shall provide the necessary plant and equipment. Commonwealth and local authorities shall provide sufficient funds for the purchase of necessary instructional and reference material and supplies. § 503-70. General statement on well-rounded courses of instruction

The cost of instruction supplementary to the instruction in agriculture, distributive occupations, home economics, and trade and industry, necessary to build a well-rounded course of training, shall be borne by the Commonwealth and local communities and no part of the cost thereof shall be borne by the appropriations of the Smith-Hughes or George-Barden Acts.

Typical courses of study prepared by individuals or groups of teachers, with the help of the supervisory staff, are available at the central office. § 503-71. Provisions which shall be included in this plan 

In order to secure the benefits of the funds for salaries of teachers of agriculture, distributive occupations, home economics, and trade and industrial subjects: (1) The schools or classes shall be under public supervision. or control within the requirements of the vocational education acts. 

(2) The controlling purpose of the education shall be to fit for useful employment. (3) The education shall be of less than college grade. (4) Instruction shall be designed to meet the needs of persons fourteen years of age or over. § 503-72. Provisions for cooperative planning and activities among vocational fields

Federal funds may be used to provide vocational training through cooperation of the school and industrial and business establishments for groups of young people whose individual occupational objectives differ and whose cooperative agreement provides for legal employment, systematic training on-the-job and supplemental training in the school. 315

§ 503-102. Program of instruction; types of classes to be conducted

The Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education proposes to establish schools and classes of less than college grade designed for persons 14 years of age or over who have entered upon or who are preparing to enter upon the work of the home farm or of any other farm. § 503-103. All-day classes of students 

Minimum number and minimum age

Thirty students will be considered minimum enrollment for a department. Students must be 14 years of age or have attained the school grade where students are normally 14 years of age. § 503-104. 

Length of course

A three-year course will be organized in every agricultural department. § 503-105. 

Length of daily sessions

Acceptable plans for meeting the minimum time provisions are as follows: 

Plan A Two consecutive 60-minute periods of instruction, five days per week, for one year; and one 60-minute period of instruction, five days per week, for the next two years.

Plan B Two consecutive 60-minute periods of instruction, two days per week, and one 60-minute period, three days per week, for each class, each year.

Plan C 

Two consecutive 45-minute periods of instruction per day, five days per week, for each class, each year. 

Plan D Sixty minutes of class instruction per day, five days per week, for each class, each year, provided there is in operation a program of systematic group instruction for out-of-school young farmers and/or adult farmers for not less than a total of 72 clock hours during the year.

Plan E Thirty hours of scheduled class instruction in agriculture during each school month for each class per year. 317

T.§ 503-105 Ch. 23 

Plan F Six hours of instruction per week for each class, per year; Provided there is in operation a program of systematic group instruction for young farmers and/or adult farmers for not less than 72 hours per year or the teacher teaches four classes of vocational agriculture per day.

Codification. The English of this section has been changed to correspond to the Spanish. 

§ 503-106. Number of sessions 

Three sessions of classroom teaching per day plus at least 450 minutes per week for project supervision will be required of every teacher of agriculture with three all-day groups. In departments where there are only two sessions of classroom teaching per day, at least 450 minutes per week must be devoted to project supervision and in the case of departments operating on plans A, B, C, or E a young or adult farmers' course of at least 30 hours of instruction and 10 hours of project supervision per person per year will be required. 

In schools following Plan F, the teacher may carry a four-class daily schedule four days of the week and devote one full day to project supervision or carry a three-class daily schedule four days and organize a program of systematic instruction for a group of out-of-school young and/or adult farmers which may meet once weekly, 450 minutes weekly being devoted to project supervision.

Codification. The English of this section has been changed to correspond to the Spanish. 

§ 503-107. Provisions for a supervised farming program 

Students enrolled in agriculture classes shall be required to do at least six months directed or supervised practice in agriculture per year.

This mandatory provision is interpreted to mean that all-day students will develop individual farming programs either on their own farms or other farms, under the direction of the local teachers of vocational agriculture to make a beginning in farming. § 503-108. Provisions for follow-up instruction 

Teachers of vocational agriculture will follow up former students and will encourage them to become gainfully employed as farmers, renters, sharecroppers, farm managers, or to work in occupations related to farming. 318

Ch. T.18 § 503-111 

VOCATIONAL EDUCATION § 503-109. - Provisions for supervising activities of the F.F.A. 

Every vocational agricultural department will be required to organize a chapter of the Future Farmers of America and to plan and conduct a program of activities for the year. 

The central office, through members of the supervisory staff, will supervise the activities of local F.F.A. chapters. 

§ 503-110. Day-unit classes 

It is not proposed to organize day-unit classes. 

§ 503-111. Young farmer classes 

Young farmer classes will be organized primarily for the purpose of providing a continued education program for boys who have gone as far as possible in all-day instruction, as well as for young men who have dropped out of school and are now living on farms. (1) Minimum enrollment and minimum age of students

Young farmer classes will be organized with not less than 10 students with a minimum age of 16 years. (2) Length of course

There shall be not less than 15 meetings each year with not less than 30 hours of instruction over at least a two-year period, or the program of instruction shall be planned for and conducted over the entire 12-month span of the year for a total of not less than 30 hours. (3) Length of class sessions 

Class sessions will have a minimum duration of 90 minutes. (4) Number of sessions per week, per month or per year There must be a minimum of 15 sessions per year with a total of not less than 30 hours of instruction. (5) Provisions for supervised farming

Provisions must be made for every student to carry a supervised farming program of at least six months' duration, on the home farm or any other farm. (6) Provisions for follow-up of students 

Teachers of agriculture should make at least three supervisory visits to each student each year in his own home or other farm situation. (7) Provisions for supervising activities of young farmers

Students of young farmer classes will be encouraged to join the 319

T.§ 503-111 

Ch. 23

EDUCATION · - PUBLIC SCHOOLS 

Young Farmers of America, and to take an active part in the program. § 503-112. Adult farmer classes

Adult farmer classes will be organized to provide an opportunity for adult farmers who have become established in farming to improve the efficiency of their operations and their proficiency throughout the calendar year. (1) Minimum enrollment and minimum age of students

Adult farmer classes will be organized with a minimum of ten students who are 18 years of age or over. (2) Length of course in years and in total hours of instruction 

There shall be not less than 10 meetings, totaling at least 20 hours, over a period of not less than two weeks in any one year. (3) Length of class sessions

Class sessions will have a minimum duration of 90 minutes. (4) Number of sessions per week, per month or per year There shall be a minimum of ten meetings per year, totaling at least 20 hours of instruction. (5) Provisions for supervised farming

Provisions must be made for every student to carry a farming program of at least six months' duration. (6) Provisions for follow-up of students

It shall be the responsibility of teachers of agriculture to supervise individual adult students at least three times during the year, and to keep records of new or improved practices adopted.

§ 159-4. Regularity of the services rendered by the Authority 

The Authority shall render the water and sewer services in the most regular and continuous manner possible. However, it may interrupt these services because of special circumstances, such as the depletion of volume of water, repairs, and improvements on the systems in operation. 

§ 159-5. Interference with systems 

Only the authorized agents of the Authority shall operate, make service connections and work in the water and sewer systems of this instrumentality. The public is forbidden to perform said acts or tamper with, manipulate, alter, obstruct, deface, mutilate, or destroy any installation, or any portion or part of said systems. 

§ 159-6. Construction of extension works to the waterworks and sewer systems

The Authority may make extensions to the waterworks and sewer systems and defray the expenses incurred in connection therewith from rent funds, provided these extensions prove to be

economically justified; that is, that they produce rents or other actual or potential profit that justifies the use of the funds that such constructions entail. § 159-7. Protection of the supply sources of the waterworks and sewer systems

It is prohibited to throw into the supply sources of the waterworks of the Authority such substances as sewage, industrial waste in general, liquid substances, matters or objects that may pollute the water. It is also prohibited to throw or deposit on the banks or shores of the water sources such waste, substances, liquids, matters or objects that may pollute the waters of the waterworks or hinder the effectiveness of the waterworks and sewer systems. 

§ 159-8. Other provisions for safeguarding public health 

It is also prohibited to bathe, swim, wash clothes, water and bathe animals, spit, wash vehicles in such water sources, or to use said waters or the aqueduct system for any purpose that might jeopardize the public health or alter its chemical or bacteriological composition; urinating, defecating, throwing or depositing urine or manure on the surrounding grounds or into such waters, depositing molasses or any rubbish, garbage, depositing or throwing dead animals or refuse from slaughterhouses, pens or butchering establishments, is also prohibited. 

The Authority may order the removal or abatement of the aforementioned infectious matter, substances or objects, and if not removed within 24 hours, it may do so at the expense of the offender. 

§ 159-9. Location of septic or gravel-walled wells 

It is prohibited to locate latrines, septic or gravel-walled wells in the vicinity of the supply sources of the waterworks of the Authority, where they may pollute the water of said sources. 

§ 159-10. Public nuisance 

Any act or thing done which may be detrimental to the aqueduct and sewer systems operated by the Authority or to the purity and conservation of the water supply sources of said aqueducts is hereby declared a public nuisance, and the Authority is fully empowered to correct or abate such public nuisance, according to law. 

Any illegal service connection or sewage discharge is hereby also
