§ 159-101. Charges for services rendered by the Authority 

The Authority shall operate on such economic basis as shall permit it to be self-sufficient; to this end it shall render no free services, the same to be rendered only upon payment of appropriate rates; provided, however, that no charge shall be made for water used in extinguishing fires.

VOCATIONAL EDUCATION § 503-123. Qualifications of teacher trainer 

(a) Education (1) Technical A bachelor's degree in agriculture from an accredited institution which has been approved for training teachers of vocational agriculture. (2) Professional A master's degree with a major in agricultural education from an approved teacher training institution. (b) Experience (1) Farming 

Two years of successful farming experience after age 14.

Experience obtained on the school farm as teacher of agriculture will be accepted. (2) Teaching, supervisory or administrative in approved programs in agricultural education.

At least five years of successful teaching experience in an approved program of agricultural education, two years of which shall have been in an itinerant teacher trainer, critic teacher, subject matter specialist, administrative or supervisory capacity in a program of agricultural education. 

(3) General 

Administrative ability and leadership as demonstrated in his contacts with farm people and other people, and an attitude of helpfulness toward the development of rural life. § 503-124. Qualifications of assistant teacher trainer, supervising teachers, subject matter and research specialists (a) Education 

A bachelor's degree in agriculture and at least 15 credits in special methods in agricultural education from an institution approved for the training of teachers of vocational agriculture. (b) Experience

Two years of successful farming experience after age 18 and teaching experience covering at least three years of successful experience as a teacher of vocational agriculture. § 503-125. Duties of the teacher training staff in vocational agriculture (a) Kinds of courses to be taught It shall be the duty of the teacher training department to teach such reimbursable courses as are outlined in sec. 503-120. 325

T.18503 Ch. 23 

(b) Follow-up of first year teachers

It is the distinct function of the teacher training department to follow up the teachers of vocational agriculture during their first year of work for the purpose of checking the effectiveness of the pre-employment training. This should be done at least three times during the year. (c) Itinerant service to employed teachers It will be the responsibility of the teacher training staff to coordinate with supervisors in visiting and helping those teachers who have been pointed out as weak by the Insular supervisor. (d) Preparation of teaching material It will be the responsibility of the teacher training staff to prepare teaching aids for all-day, as well as for young and adult farmer classes, which will help in the improvement of instruction. 

In addition, they will prepare releases including the latest information obtained at the experiment stations or from other agricultural agencies. (e) Supervision of directed teaching centers The teacher trainer will supervise the work of the trainees at least once a week and will make reports of his findings and recommendations to the Commonwealth supervisor. He will also meet his trainees at least once every two weeks for a roundtable discussion on methods, problems in teaching, organization, farm management, supervised farming, etc. (f) Research and studies in agricultural education All studies and research carried on for improving the program will be first approved by the supervisor of vocational agriculture. 

Studies may be carried on at the teacher training institution or at the Department of Education, or by both in cooperation. § 503-126. Name and address of the institution designated by the 

Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education for the training of teachers of vocational agriculture 

The College of Agriculture and Mechanic Arts of the University of Puerto Rico will be the institution designated to train teachers of vocational agriculture. The address of said institution is Mayagüez, Puerto Rico. § 503-127. Conditions for approval of institutions to train teachers of vocational agriculture - Procedures and standards to be used in determining whether enough vocational agriculture teachers are being prepared The number and quality of the teachers of agriculture available for teaching positions and the average number of teachers needed as replacements and for new departments over a two-year period will be a guide to determine whether enough vocational agriculture teachers are being prepared. 

§ 503-129. Standards with respect to facilities and staff for technical instruction in agriculture to be met by an institution before being approved to train teachers of vocational agriculture (a) There must be a qualified faculty to teach the technical courses offered at the proposed teacher training institution. 

The faculty should meet the minimum standards set forth by the University of Puerto Rico for the training of teachers of vocational agriculture. To accomplish these objectives the curriculum should include specific training in the following fields: (1) Communication including composition, literature, advanced writing and speech. (2) Mathematics. (3) Social Science including economics and psychology. (4) Natural science including botany, zoology, entomology, genetics, chemistry, and physics. (5) Agriculture including a minimum of 54 semester credit hours. (A) A maximum of 24 semester credit hours of general introductory courses in: (i) Agronomy (crops and soils) (ii) Animal husbandry (iii) Dairy husbandry 327

T.§ 503-129 Ch. 23 

 (iv) Poultry husbandry 

(v) Horticulture (fruits and vegetables) (B) Agricultural economics including farm management, agricultural marketing and farm finance . (C) Agricultural engineering including farm shop, farm power and machinery, farm buildings. (D) Animal nutrition (E) One or more advanced courses in each of the following fields: (i) Animal science including feeding, milk and meat hygiene, dairy cattle and poultry. (ii) Plant science including breeding, physiology, pathology, production of cereal crops, forage crops and pastures, cotton, corn, fruits, vegetables, farm forest and other special crops. (iii) Soil science including classification, fertility, conservation and management. (6) Professional education including methods and practice teaching. (b) The faculty must be made up of members adequately qualified by training and experience for teaching and research in the specific area to which they are assigned. Each member of the technical agriculture staff shall have a master's degree with a graduate major in the specific area of his teaching assignment or shall have a bachelor's degree in that area and be working under the direct supervision of a staff member who has an advanced degree in that area. § 503-130.

AQUEDUCT AND SEWER AUTHORITY 

§ 159-135. Prohibitions on the use of public fountains

It shall be prohibited to use public fountains installed by the Authority in certain rural or urban communities in such a manner as to deprive others of their rightful enjoyment, for hose connections, for car washing or bathing of animals, or to install branch connections to the pipeline supplying water to said public fountains. § 159-136. Sewer service; to whom rendered

Sewer service shall be rendered to persons having access to the pipelines in use, upon compliance with the requirements established by the Authority; provided that the owner, tenant, or occupant of any building, house or apartment adjacent to, or who may have access to, any street or thoroughfare having sanitary sewerage, operated by the Authority shall register as subscriber to said sewer facilities under the terms and conditions required, whereupon said subscriber shall cease using any other means for the disposal of the water served, sewage or other matter, unless said subscriber has an independent means for disposal of the water served, waste and other matter, constructed and operated in accordance with the prescribed specifications of this Authority and approved by the Secretary of Health. 

§ 159-136a. Multiple services 

Service may be furnished through one water meter to more than one residence, office or establishment within buildings under the horizontal property regime or apartment buildings as defined under sec. 159-3 of this title.

Amendments- 1964. This section was added by amendment File No. 897, cited in 1964 amendment note under 

§ 159-3 of this title. 

§ 159-137. Sewer service tapping

Installations connected to the sewer service tappings as well as those leading therefrom to the consumer's interior installations shall become the property of the Authority and as such shall remain under its exclusive control even though the cost of said installations might have been defrayed by the consumer.

§ 159-139. Compulsory use of grease traps 

The subscribers to the sewer system of the Authority, such as hotels, restaurants, inns or institutions where large quantities of food are cooked and served shall use grease traps. This requirement shall also be applicable to garages, gasoline stations and other establishments whose sewer discharge contains a considerable amount of grease or oil. 

§ 159-140. Illicit discharges 

Illicit discharges into the sewer system of the Authority are prohibited; the Authority shall reserve the right to charge the total estimated amount for the service utilized in connection with such illicit discharges. 

§ 159-141. Legalization of illicit discharges 

In case of illicit discharges, the Authority may permit such discharges as a part of its regular sewer service if the conditions of the illicit installations warrant such action. 

§ 159-142. Observance of instructions issued by the Authority 

Persons enjoying the recreational facilities of the reservoirs shall strictly observe the instructions communicated to them through the authorized agents of the Authority or by posters or signs placed in convenient places for that purpose. 

§ 159-143. Fishing and navigation 

Hook and rod fishing, as well as the use of small craft, in the reservoirs shall be permitted under the terms and conditions stipulated by the Authority, provided, that the use of said craft shall take place between the hours 6:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., and that said craft shall be removed from the water and grounds of the 

Authority upon expiration of said period. § 159-144. Minimum distance to be maintained from the dam 

Any craft in the reservoir shall be maintained a minimum distance of 500 feet from the dam at all times.

§ 196-2. Applications for service; general (a) Electric service under any of the rate schedules for residential, commercial and industrial power customers (secondary voltage service) is available on the filling out and the signing of the 

Authority's regular "Application for Service", if the prospective customer is within the distribution area of the Authority, if there is capacity available in the Authority's lines and equipment, and if no extension of the system is necessary. Acceptance of applications of customers outside of the distribution area of the Authority are subject to the terms of sec. 196-3 of this title. (b) Electric service under the rate schedules for public lighting and for primary distribution voltage and secondary transmission voltage customers is available on contract for not less than 1 year.

§ 196-3. Line extensions 

The Authority may accept an "Application for Service" or enter into a contract with any prospective secondary voltage service customer whose premises are outside the Authority's network of distribution lines for the sale of electric power under the following conditions: (1) If the Authority is satisfied that the amount of power to be used will justify the construction of a line to the point of delivery and the installation of a suitable transformer and meter by the Authority, the cost of the said line and of the said transformer and meter shall be borne by the Authority, provided the customer will obtain for or grant to the Authority an easement, if needed, for the extension of such line by the Authority and extension thereof in the future over the customer's premises. (2) If the Authority is not satisfied that the estimate of the amount of power to be used will justify the construction of a line to the point of delivery and the installation of a suitable transformer and meter by the Authority, the Authority shall require the pay- 

March 31, 1964

Vol. 3, No. 3 336

Ch. T.22 § 196-5 

ment of a minimum monthly bill that will justify the required investment, or the payment of an equitable portion of the construction of the said line and of the cost of installation of the said transformer and meter; provided, however, that the line, transformer and meter shall always be and remain the property of the Authority, and that the customer will obtain for or grant to the Authority an easement, if needed, for the extension of such line by the Authority as well as any extension thereof to supply other customers.

§ 196-4. Temporary service 

Customers of temporary electric service (for a period of less than 12 months) shall be required to pay for the cost of installing and removing all equipment and connections required to render such service, including meters and 10% of cost of materials. Charges for electric service shall be in accordance with rates specified in the rate schedule that applies to the type of service rendered. Seasonal service shall not be classed as temporary service. 

Amendments 1964. No change was made in this section by Revision File No. 561-A, cited in 1964 amendment note under sec. 196-1 of this title. 

§ 196-5. Seasonal service 

Seasonal customers, or seasonal consumption customers, as used in the Authority's rate schedules, shall be understood to be customers whose electric requirements occur periodically, or more or less at regular seasons, during the year. Charges for such service shall be in accordance with the rates specified in the rate schedule that applies to the type of service rendered, except that the minimum bill shall be computed as follows: Minimum monthly bill x 12/

Number of months in season. The months comprising the regular season shall be defined for each particular industry and will remain the same every year. Electric service will not be supplied by the

Authority during the off-season months and the transformers and other equipment necessary for normally supplying such service. shall be disconnected from the lines of the Authority. 

Amendments - 1964. No change was made in this section by Revision File No. 561-A, cited in 1964 amendment note under sec. 196-1 of this title.

Vol. 3, No. 3 337

PUBLIC WORKS § 196-6. Standby, auxiliary or breakdown service 

Agricultural, industrial, or commercial customers (except sugar mills that take all their off-season requirements from the Authority) who may want electric service to supplement seasonal or byproduct generation of electric energy, or for other purposes, may contract for such service under Rate Schedule SP-11 [sec. 196-244 of this title] only. The Authority is not obligated to supply or maintain standby, auxiliary or breakdown service unless a contract for this service has been previously signed by the customer. In case a regular customer of the Authority elects to install his own generating facilities, the Authority shall discontinue service unless a standby contract is signed within 10 days of such installation or purchase.

1964.

 § 196-7. Exclusive use of transformers 

Secondary voltage service customers requesting the installation of one or more transformers for their own exclusive use shall pay 40 cents per month per KVA of installed transformer capacity in addition to all other charges provided for in the applicable rate schedule.

Amendments- 1964. No change was made in this section by Revision File No. 561-A, cited in 1964 amendment note under sec. 196-1 of this title. 

§ 196-8. Deposits 

The Authority reserves the right to require from each customer those warranties which, in its judgment, are deemed advisable and satisfactory to properly guarantee the consumption of electric energy by the customer, either by means of deposit, bond from an insurance company or in any other way authorized by law. Interest shall be paid at the rate of three per cent per annum on those cases in which the Authority accepts as warranty for the preceding aims, deposits of a fixed amount in United States legal tender, except when the deposit is for less than $5 or when the deposit is retained for a period of less than one year in which instances no interest shall be paid. In those cases which bear interest, no interest shall be paid for periods of less than 6 months.

 § 196-10. § 196-12. Point of delivery of electric power 

The point of delivery is defined as the point or place at which the Authority delivers, to the customer, the electric power used by him, as shown below: (1) Electric power supply to municipal franchise holders for distribution in urban areas will be delivered at or near the outer boundaries of the urban zone of the municipalities. (2) Electric power supply to primary distribution voltage and secondary transmission voltage customers will be delivered at a 

March 31, 1964

Vol. 3, No. 3 339

T.S 196-12 Ch. 11 

PUBLIC WORKS 

point on the primary distributions or secondary transmission line of the Authority, as the case may be. The Authority will install, at its own cost, the necessary protective equipment to prevent defects in the customer's installation causing interruption of service in the Authority's system. The cost of the line connecting the customer's plant to said protective equipment shall be paid by the customers, and all such facilities shall be maintained by him. (3) Electric power furnished to secondary voltage service customers will be delivered at the customer's end of the service drop, as defined in this same section. (4) All underground services shall be furnished by the customer and the point of delivery shall be considered to be the point where the underground services connect to the secondary lines of the 

Authority. 

Amendments 1964. Subdiv. (3): Definition of the point of delivery of electric power, given by the National Electric Code of 1951, was substituted by that given in this section, by amendment File No. 561-A, cited in 1964 amendment note under § 196-8 of this title. 

§ 196-13. Electrical measurements 

Demand and energy measurements shall be made by suitable instruments at the point of delivery, or, at the option of the Authority, at some other nearby point where facilities may be more readily installed. The Authority shall, without charge to the customer (except for temporary service), install and maintain meters for measuring the amount of energy furnished to customers and the maximum demand, where the terms of the rate schedule require such measurements; Provided, That should these meters fail, or be found inaccurate, the amount of energy delivered and the maximum demand will be estimated by the Authority from the best information available. The customer consents to permit the use of his housing and other facilities for the Authority's metering equipment.

Provided further that the electric power service to primary distribution voltage or secondary transmission voltage may be measured for billing purposes, at the Authority's option, in terms of kilowatts (Kw). The conversion of billing purposes of kilowatts (Kw) to kilovolt amperes (KVA), will be done by applying a power factor to be determined by test, or at the Authority's option by the application of power factor of 85%, according to the circumstances of each case.

§ 196-14. Meter tests 

The Authority shall exercise due care to have all meters at customers' installations function correctly; and, in addition to the general inspection which is periodically made to determine the condition of all meters, it shall test, at its own initiative, any meter which may appear out of adjustment. When the customer questions the correctness of any meter and requests that it be tested, his request shall be complied with on condition that if the meter is found to be out of adjustment the cost of the test shall be borne by the Authority, but if the meter is found to be correct, within the limit stipulated by law, a charge of $1 shall be paid by the customer.

Amendments 

1964.

§ 196-15. Duplicate feeders 

In the event that a customer should desire to increase the reliability of his service beyond that normally provided for by one service drop, or one point of delivery for primary voltage customers, double feed from the line of the Authority may be available on the condition that the customer pay all the expenses of installing such alternate connection, and further, that the meters be so installed and adjusted as to include all the losses between the points of delivery and the customer's installation.

§ 196-17. Inspection 

The Authority shall have the right, but shall not be obligated, to inspect electrical installations at any time, and it reserves the right to reject any wiring or equipment not in accordance with its standards. Such inspection, or failure to inspect, or to reject, shall not render the Authority, its agents, or employees, liable or responsible for any loss, damage, or accident resulting from defects in the customer's installation of any electrical equipment, or for any violation of the application or contract of which this subdivision is a part.

§ 196-18. Right of access 

The customer shall permit entrance on his premises to identified employees of the Authority at all reasonable hours for all purposes related to the Authority's business.

§ 196-19. Determination of connected load 

(a) The term "connected load", as used in the Authority's rate schedules, shall be understood to be the manufacturer's rated capacity of the apparatus and lighting connected on customer's premises, including empty sockets at 100 watts each, except as noted below. Demands of not more than 10% above manufacturer's rating of apparatus installed will not be considered, for billing purposes, as deviating from manufacturer's ratings. (b) When the demand of the apparatus is greater than 10% above the manufacturer's rating, the "connected load" on which monthly charges shall be based shall be determined on the basis of the average actual power used by the installation during the maximum 15-minute period of operation for the month. The "connected load" on which monthly charges shall be based for any installation using power at rates less than 10% below the manufacturer's rating shall be taken equal to the manufacturer's rating, unless the customer installs, and maintains in good service, power factor corrective apparatus which will insure not less than 85% power factor for 

March 31, 1964

Vol. 3, No. 3 

342

Ch. T.22 § 196-21 

the installation, in which case the "connected load" shall be taken to be equal to the actual power used during the maximum 15minute period but in no event less than 50% of the capacity contracted for by the customer. (c) The "connected load" for X-ray equipment shall be taken as 1 KW for each 3 KVA, or major fraction, of transformer capacity. 

Transformers to be used exclusively for supplying service to such X-ray equipment should be installed whenever practicable and the customer shall then pay the normal charge of 40 cents per month per KVA stipulated in sec. 196-7 of this title in addition to all other charges. (d) In commercial installations under Rate Schedule C-5 [Sec. 

196–222 of this title] and public institutions under Rate Schedule C-6 [sec. 196-223 of this title], all heating appliances and aggregate motor load of 3 HP or less shall not be included in the determination of "connected load". (e) For industrial customers and for all commercial customers, the total of the number of HP or KW, respectively, which shall be used for establishing the "connected load" shall be to the nearest HP or the nearest KW, respectively. 

Amendments 1964. This section was amended to agree with the original Spanish version. § 196-20. Increases in connected load

The service connection, transformers, meters and equipment supplied by the Authority for the customer's use have a definite capacity, and no change shall be made in the customer's installation that may cause his load to exceed his contracted capacity except after notice to, and written permission from, the Authority. Additions to, or material changes in, the characteristic of the load, made without permission from the Authority, shall render the customer liable for any damages caused by the additional capacity of, or changes in, the installation.

§ 196-27. Customer's responsibility for Authority's property 

(a) All meters, services and other equipment furnished by the Authority shall be and remain its property and the right to remove, replace or repair all such equipment is expressly reserved.  § 196-28. SUBDIVISION 2. RESERVE FOR REVENUE STABILIZATION SECTIONS 196-101. Revenue Stabilization Reserve 

196-102. 196-103. 196-104. 

Rate to provide Reserve 

Formation of operating cushion Effectiveness 

§ 196-101. Revenue Stabilization Reserve 

In establishing rates for electric service every effort is made to set rates which will produce revenues only sufficient in amount to cover the operating costs of the Authority. However, in practice, it is impossible to set rates which will produce, from year to year, exactly the amount of revenue needed, and the rates in force, therefore, due to uncontrollable variations in the volume of sales and in operating costs may produce in any year somewhat more or somewhat less revenue than is needed. In order to avoid the necessity of frequent revisions of the basic rates to adjust the revenues to just the amount needed to cover the operating costs, the Authority, as a part of its rate structure, will set aside in a Revenue Stabilization Reserve any excess over the revenues required in any one year and will return subsequently, in the form of a percentage reduction on the monthly bills for electric service to all customers, except those covered by Rate Schedules SP-9, SP-10, LP-16, and LP-17 [secs. 196-242, 196–243, 196-264, and 

196-265 of this title], any amount not needed to supply possible deficiencies in the revenues required. 

March 31, 1964

Vol. 3, No. 3 

349

T.§ 196-101 

Ch. 11

PUBLIC WORKS Amendments 

1964.

§ 196-102. Rate to provide Reserve 

(a) In estimating the total revenues required to provide for operating expenses, a certain margin of safety must be allowed in order to have available at all times, during the fiscal year, a reasonable cushion which will absorb any impact caused by emergency expenditures. The need of using this cushion may arise at any time and particularly toward the end of the fiscal year at a time when it would be too late to adjust rates to make up any deficiency caused by such emergency expenditures. (b) Based on past experience, and in the light of present conditions, it appears that approximately 3% of the total revenues required to provide for operating expenses is an adequate provision for this operating cushion and that it is essential that it remain available during the entire fiscal year. 

Amendments- 1964. No change was made in this section by Revision File No. 561-A, cited in 1964 amendment note under sec. 196-1 of this title. 

§ 196-103. Formation of operating cushion 

To the extent that the accumulation in the Revenue Stabilization Reserve will permit, this operating cushion shall be formed as follows: 

(1) 3% total revenues required (as defined in sec. 502 of the Trust Indenture dated January 1, 1947), (2) plus 3% of the underrun, if any, of actual operating expenses, exclusive of fuel oil, below the operating expenses estimated in the annual budget, exclusive of fuel oil or minus 3% of the overrun, if any, of actual operating expenses exclusive of fuel oil, above the operating expenses estimated in the annual budget, exclusive of fuel oil, otherwise the amount of the cushion shall become whatever the revenues available will produce above operating cost requirements.

Amendments- 1964. No change was made in this section by Revision File No. 561-A, cited in 1964 amendment note under sec. 196-1 of this title. § 196-104. Effectiveness

Should the sum of the actual monthly kilowatt-hours consumed during the period be greater than the minimum annual guaranteed consumption, then any amount billed during such 12-month period in excess of that corresponding to the sum of the actual monthly kilowatthours consumed during the period, at the stated price of 5.5¢ per Kwh plus fuel oil adjustment, shall be credited to the customer.

Qualifications of teacher trainers (1) Education technical and professional 

(A) Shall be a graduate of a four-year college course with a bachelor's degree in home economics education from a college or university approved for the training of teachers for vocational programs in home economics. (B) Shall have a master's degree in home economics education or in home economics with a minor in home economics education or shall have completed her master's degree within six years from the time of her appointment. Her advanced training shall include a course in journalism. (C) Shall have done outstanding work in the subject matter areas of home economics during her four-year college training and shall have demonstrated marked evidence of being accurate, comprehensive, and thorough in her work. (D) Shall be able to speak, understand, and write correctly both English and Spanish. (2) Experience - teaching and homemaking (A) Shall have at least three years of successful teaching experience in home economics. (B) Shall have a practical homemaking experience sufficient to assume responsibility of managing a home. § 503-339. § 503-401. Commonwealth supervision 

(a) Duties of the Commonwealth supervisor and assistant supervisors (1) Shall promote active cooperation with industry and organizations of employees and employers. (2) Shall provide for the preparation and distribution of instructional materials for vocational industrial education. (3) Shall assist public school authorities in conducting occupational surveys and provide for studies and research necessary for program improvement. (4) Shall provide assistance to industrial concerns by providing for the organization of essential training programs. (5) Shall promote safety education and safety practices in the shops and laboratories of the trade and industrial schools. (6) Shall promote and supervise day, evening and part-time programs of education and training in the fields of trades and industry, service trades, and technical occupations. (7) Shall supervise programs of related instruction for apprentices and assist in developing teaching materials and courses of study through cooperation with the apprenticeship council. (8) Shall provide for the improvement of teachers through in-service and summer session teacher training. Also to provide for the pre-service training of prospective teachers. (b) Qualifications of the Commonwealth supervisor (1) Education (A) Graduation from a degree granting course in a college or university of recognized standing. (B) 450 clock hours of professional courses in vocational education on the undergraduate or graduate level. (2) Experience (A) Trade 

Three years of experience in one or more trades at journeyman wages. (B) Teaching 

Three years of successful experience as 370

§ 503-405. Evening trade extension classes 

(a) Minimum entrance age requirement sixteen years (b) Character and content of course of study (1) The work in the evening classes, conducted for male or female workers during their nonworking hours, shall be organized in short-unit courses so that a person may secure instruction in only those parts of the trade and/or industrial pursuits for which a need is felt. The character and content of the course of study must be such as will increase the skills and knowledge of the worker in the trade and/or industrial pursuit in which he is employed or has been employed. It may include manipulative and technical instruction as well as safety, first aid, State and Federal labor laws, and the socio-economic problems of his occupation. 372

VOCATIONAL EDUCATION § 503-410. Part-time general continuation 

(1) Type A - Other than cooperative to assist students in making proper employment and social adjustments. (A) Hours per week and weeks per year

At least 144 hours of instruction per year shall be required in classes reimbursed from Smith-Hughes Funds. (B) Character and content of courses of study In these classes, training is provided for out-of-school youth employed in a trade or industrial occupation who did not have an opportunity to complete their education before they entered employment. Instruction is offered to enable young workers to meet changing conditions in their vocations or to meet more effectively their citizenship or workers' requirements. In arranging courses, teachers shall arrange the work, as far as possible, to meet individual needs. (C) Qualifications of teachers (i) Education-professional Any properly certified teacher may qualify for service in the part-time general continuation classes. (ii) One year of successful teaching experience and/or work experience. (iii) Training for teaching 

to pro- In-service teacher training is given on the job. (2) Type B - cooperative (diversified occupations) vide vocational training through a cooperative plan of the schools and industrial and public establishments for groups of young people interested in learning a trade or occupation. Practical training as well as technical instruction supplementary to the training is offered.

Students enrolled shall be 16 years of age and legally employed under agreement (preferably written) between the schools and the employer. Such employment shall be in conformity with Federal and Commonwealth regulations. All minors under 18 years of age shall have a permit issued by the Department of Labor of the United States or of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, as the case may be. In certain occupations declared hazardous by the Departments of Labor of the United States or of Puerto Rico, student learners shall be over 18 years of age.

Student learners shall be employed for at least half of the usual working week of the occupation in which they are employed, 375

T.§ 503-410 

Ch. 23

EDUCATION · · PUBLIC SCHOOLS 

and in no case shall this employment be for less than 15 hours per week. The time at work shall equal or exceed the time in clock hours devoted to school instruction throughout the year. In no case shall the time at school and the time at work be such as to violate legal employment regulations.

Occupations included shall be those which offer real chances for training and advancement in the trade or industrial occupation selected by the student as a vocation. 

Provisions shall be made for adequate coordination and supervision. Sufficient time shall be provided for the coordinators to visit student learners on the job and the employers in order that training at work and in schools may be properly correlated. 

The amount of related vocational instruction required shall be based on the length of the cooperative program and the amount of vocational training which may have been already completed in the all-day school. The following suggested plans take into account these two factors: (A) For a cooperative part-time program covering two school years, an average of at least one regular class period a day is devoted to related vocational instruction in which enrollment is limited to this group, and taught by the coordinator as a segregated class. (B) In a cooperative part-time program covering one school year, an average of at least two regular class periods a day is devoted to related vocational instruction in which enrollment is limited to this group and taught by the coordinator as segregated classes.

All instruction should be organized and conducted with the advice and counsel of a representative advisory committee composed of employers and employees.

The school authorities should provide adequate instructional materials for the related vocational classes to make the instruction effective. Individual study guides which meet at least the minimum needs for technical and other related instruction should be made available for each student enrolled.

All cooperative part-time student learners shall receive a monetary wage at a rate commensurate with wages paid other employees doing similar work. Such wage rates shall be in conformity with 

Federal and State wage regulations.

§ 503-412. Day trade and industrial classes

The instruction will be planned to give training in the manipulative part of the work and also in the mathematics, drawing and science related to it. Provisions shall be made for the life adjustments required of self directing citizens in a democracy. 

The shop teachers shall follow in each trade the content of the course of study drafted according to the trade analysis. VOCATIONAL EDUCATION (1) Character and content of courses of study 

Instruction shall be given in intensive courses operated for any length of time. This type of training shall be given to equip learners with the basic skills, technical knowledge and related industrial information which will enable them to get a job, hold it, and advance in the industrial occupation. 

Courses of study shall provide experience for students in all the basic shop or laboratory processes of the trade or occupation being taught; instruction shall be planned to include both manipulative processes and related and technical instruction. (2) Amount of time given to: (A) Practical work on a useful or productive basis. Such classes may be operated without the requirement that a minimum of 50 per cent of the school time must be given to shop work on a useful or productive basis. (B) Related instruction shall be given as an integral part of the shop work. (3) Length of school year in months and hours per week 

May be offered for any length of time. (4) Qualifications of teachers (A) Shop and trade-practice teachers 

Same as for Type A. (B) Related subjects teachers 

Same as for Type A. (5) Qualifications of students

Admission shall be restricted to those who are physically able and mentally competent to profit by the instruction. 

Age of admission shall be limited to persons over 18 years of age or those over 16 years who have legally left the full time school and will be of employable age upon completing the training. 

§ 503-413. Plan for coordination 

All coordination in the various programs shall be made by the assistant supervisors and local directors. In the diversified occupations program the coordination will be carried on by the locally designated coordinator.

§ 503-416. Program of teacher training 

The program of teacher training in Puerto Rico is composed of three phases pre-service, in-service institutional and also of special courses organized by the Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education. Enrollment in teacher training courses, reimbursed from Federal funds, is limited to persons who have the trade experience required for the teaching position for which they are qualifying or who are acquiring such experience in the trade they are preparing to teach and will have met the requirements of trade experience by the time they have completed their professional courses in trade and industrial education. § 503-417. Duties and qualifications of the teacher trainers (a) Duties of teacher trainers (1) Shall train and supervise work of personnel, especially of new instructors, and keep the necessary records of the preparation of instructors. (2) Shall supervise and direct the preparation of teaching aids, trade analyses and courses of study. (b) Qualifications of teacher trainers (1) Education - professional (A) Graduation from a degree granting course in a college or university of recognized standing. (B) 450 clock hours of professional courses in vocational education on the undergraduate or graduate level. (2) Experience 381

T.18 503 

Ch. 23

(A) Work At least two years of journeyman trade experience. 

(B) Teaching 

Three years of successful experience as a teacher, two of which shall have been in the field of trade and industrial education. 

(C) Supervisory At least three years in a responsible administrative or supervisory capacity in the field of trade and industrial education. § 503-418. Allocation of responsibility among the agencies providing teacher training 

(a) Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education. All teacher training in this field shall be under the general supervision and control of the Commonwealth Board for Vocational Education. 

(1) Systematic group instruction. In-service training shall be given by means of local and district conferences of teachers, coordinators and local directors, and through the organization of work shops for teachers and other personnel of the trade and industrial education section. 

Whenever possible, pre-service training shall be offered to groups of prospective teachers. (2) Systematic individual instruction. Individual in-service instruction shall be given by the teacher trainer and other members of the supervisory staff through extension courses or visitation to the different localities or vocational schools, or by the local director. (3) Short, intensive instruction — individual or group. Shortunit conferences for improvement of personnel shall be conducted for teachers, coordinators and local directors, by the teacher trainer and other members of the supervisory staff. (b) Designated institutions 

(1) Systematic group instruction. The University of Puerto 

Rico, designated institution to offer teacher training to vocational trade and industrial education personnel, will offer approved courses to groups of in-service and prospective teachers. (2) Systematic individual instruction. Itinerant individual instruction will be provided by the teacher trainer of the designated institution under the direction of the supervisor. (3) Short, intensive instruction individual or group. Short, intensive courses shall be offered to the trade and industrial education personnel, coordinators and supervisors. 382

§ 503-419. Courses of training Titles of courses with brief description 

(1) Principles and practices in vocational education Three semester hours; 48 clock hours. Objectives; types of schools and activities; present status in the United

Students, school and job schedule. Teaching related subjects. Placement and follow-up. Records and reports. 

Commonwealth and Federal laws. Coordination problems. (3) Methods for industrial teachers Three semester hours; 45 clock hours. The fundamental principles, methods, problems and procedures of teaching vocational industrial subjects. (4) Psychology for industrial teachers 

Three semester hours; 45 clock hours. Points of view, incentives, and normal psychological reactions of individuals to social and industrial situations and how to apply this knowledge to specific situations in the field of industrial education. (5) Tests and measurements in industrial education 

Three semester hours; 45 clock hours. An understanding of existing standard intelligence tests, mechanical aptitude tests, trade tests, and achievement tests. The development and use of the various forms of tests and examinations for shop and classroom instruction and the evaluation of results. 

(6) Special methods in industrial education 

Three semester hours; 45 clock hours. The determination of curriculum content and preparation of instruction sheets for trade and industrial education. Methods of instruction such as demonstration, project, conference, and projection of films and slides, illustrations. Using the blackboard, charts, bulletins, magazines, books. 383

Federal funds may be used to maintain the Commonwealth program of training vocational counselors when the classes are organized and conducted for (1) classes composed of persons enrolled in a program qualifying for vocational counseling, (2) classes composed of persons enrolled in a program qualifying for vocational teaching, (3) classes composed of teachers, counselors, supervisors or directors of vocational education or vocational guidance.

Ed. 261 Nature, sources, use, and techniques of educational and occupational information. 

Sources of information on occupational training, and placement facilities; the use of educational and occupational information with individuals as part of the counseling process and the various means for disseminating this information to groups. 

(3) COUNSELING Ed. 273 Counseling techniques. 

The underlying principles, techniques, and procedure used in assisting the individual to solve his personal, educational and vocational problems. Includes initiation of the counseling relationship; selection and evaluation of information about the client; interviewing techniques and practices; case conferences; follow-up, recording, termination, and evaluation of counseling. 

Ed. 465 Supervised counseling practice.

Observation and supervised practice during one semester in a variety of counseling duties. Students practice counseling during 15 hours a week in schools, colleges, and community organizations under the supervision of the teacher or counselor trainers and guidance supervisors. One meeting weekly for discussion of problems which arise in their practice, observations, and conferences.

Ed. 269 Administrative relationships in the guidance program. 

The place of guidance services in the total school program; establishment of working relationships within the school and with community agencies; interpretation of the program to staff and community.

§ 503-513. In-service training (1) Group work 

The Commonwealth supervisory staff and counselor trainers may organize and direct workshops, conferences, and other group activities in guidance practices for training counselors, teachers, and administrators. (2) Individual work

The Commonwealth supervisory staff and counselor trainers may render individual professional services to counselors and staff members under their supervision through cooperative evaluation and in assisting the counselor in planning for the extension and refinement of guidance services on whatever problem and whatever level they may arise. § 503-514. Plans for studies, investigations, and research and the preparation, distribution, and utilization of these and other guidance materials for the professional use of guidance and vocational personnel 

With the recommendation of the Commonwealth supervisor of the vocational guidance service and the approval of the Commonwealth director of vocational education, a counselor (teacher advisor), guidance specialist, a counselor trainer, or a member of the Commonwealth supervisory staff may conduct studies, investigations, and research for the purpose of securing information useful to the vocational guidance program both directly and indirectly. § 510-3. Courses 

The course lasts for 10 months, from March to December, and includes a variety of subjects, such as restaurant service, art of cooking, menu preparation, bartending, cocktail preparation, geography, tourism, health, food handling, English, and interior decoration.

Amendments 1962. The requirements "High School Di ploma" and "High School credit Transcript" were changed to "Passed second year of high school" and "Credit transcript", by amendment adopted by Secretary of Education Oct. 17, 1962; filed with Secretary of State Oct. 22, 1962; File No. 804. 

§ 510-7. Classes 

Classes are held from Monday to Friday inclusive, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. On Mondays, theory, and the rest of the week practicing. 

The practical classes are held at various first class hotels and restaurants. 

§ 510-8. Absences 

(a) Students absent for five consecutive days without a reasonable excuse will be dropped from the roster. (b) Absences due to sickness to be justified only with a medical certificate. 

§ 510-9. Expulsion from school 

The following will be reasons for dropping students from the school: (a) Failure to comply satisfactorily with the mark requested by the director of the school. (b) Disobedience to immediate supervisor in hotels and restaurants where practical lessons are conducted. (c) Any act of disrespect to customers at the hotels and restaurants where student is assigned, or to his fellow students. (d) Tardiness for more than 15 minutes or for leaving classes before specified hour. Three consecutive delays will be considered as one absence. 1963 Vol. 2, No. 1 396

Ch. T.18 § 510-10 

VOCATIONAL EDUCATION § 510-10. Duties 

(a) All students shall work at any time, Saturdays and Sundays inclusive, at La Fortaleza, when so ordered. They shall also work, upon request, extra hours at the hotels where practical lessons are held. (b) Students taking this course must agree to follow it as a career (or profession), otherwise they will be obliged to reimburse the school an amount of $300.00. (c) Also it will be compulsory to remain in Puerto Rico for at least one year after graduation.
